entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}21 ({@damage 4d8 + 3}) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken.

action.name: Create Specter
entries: The wraith targets a Humanoid corpse within 10 feet of itself that has been dead for no longer than 1 minute. The target's spirit rises as a {@creature Specter|XMM} in the space of its corpse or in the nearest unoccupied space. The specter is under the wraith's control. The wraith can have no more than seven specters under its control at a time.

entries.name: Wraith
entries: {@i Essence of Evil}

Wraiths are spectral evils, life-hungry embodiments of malice and terror. Arising from the souls of tyrants, moments of catastrophic pain, or magical blasphemies, wraiths spread suffering and the torment of undeath. Humanoids that die near a wraith might be entrapped by the foul spirit and rise as specters bound to the wraith's sinister will.

Wraiths lurk in forgotten dungeons, accursed ruins, or lands influenced by sinister planes of existence. Such haunted domains might bear hints of the tragedies or foul magic that brought the wraiths into being.
Wraiths might arise from a single powerfully evil soul or other baleful forces. Roll on or choose a result from the Wraith Manifestations table to inspire the wickedness a wraith embodies.

entries.caption: Wraith Manifestations
rows: The blasphemous magic of a cursed location.
The exorcised evil of a redeemed villain.
A legendary villain who returns once a century.
Locals' fear of a superstition or legend.
The memory of a tragedy.
A profane idea or foul piece of lore.
The torment of one or more suffering souls.
The viciousness of a profane Artifact.
The vile dreams of a slumbering god.
The voracity of a life-hungry realm, such as the Shadowfell or Negative Plane.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyvern makes one Bite attack and one Sting attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Sting
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 24 ({@damage 7d6}) Poison damage, and the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of the wyvern's next turn.

entries.name: Wyvern
entries: {@i Draconic Hunter with a Venomous Sting}

Opportunistic predators, wyverns are draconic ambushers that strike from above. These territorial hunters attack with their fangs and stinger-tipped tails. Wyvern stingers drip with deadly venom, a painful toxin feared by monster hunters and coveted by alchemists.

Wyverns are aggressive and claim sizable territories around the mountains, crags, and ruins where they dwell. Despite their considerable strength, they're opportunistic hunters that target unwitting livestock and groups of encamped travelers. Wyverns usually land only to finish off creatures they've weakened with their poison and strafing attacks. Creatures that fight back or take flight might deter wyverns, convincing them to search for easier prey.

Once wyverns overpower a quarry, they carry it to their cavernous lairs to either consume it in safety or trap it to eat later. Most wyverns don't hoard treasure, but their lairs are littered with the possessions of past victims. It isn't uncommon for wyverns to carry off chests, carts, or small boats along with their prey.

trait.name: Earth Glide
entries: The xorn can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the xorn doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

trait.name: Treasure Sense
entries: The xorn can pinpoint the location of precious metals and stones within 60 feet of itself.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The xorn makes one Bite attack and three Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 4d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Charge
entries: The xorn moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} or {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} straight toward an enemy it can sense.

entries.name: Xorn
entries: {@i Treasure-Devouring Glutton}

On the Elemental Plane of Earth, xorn roam in search of meals they consider delicacies: gems, crystals, and veins of precious metals. For xorn, the Elemental Plane of Earth presents an endless buffet. Those that find their way to the Material Plane discover that most worlds are culinary wastelands. These xorn scour subterranean depths, consuming whatever sparse gems and ores they find. This might bring them into conflict with miners or others who hide their treasures underground.

Xorn have three eyes, three arms, and three legs arranged around their trilaterally symmetrical frames. At the top of their bodies is a toothy maw that's equally capable of crushing minerals and dangerous creatures. Xorn move through the earth magically, leaving no tunnel or sign of their passage.

Rapt gourmands, xorn focus on their next meals. They care little for living creatures and avoid harming them when possible. They know others also covet the earth's treasures, and they're not above bargaining for their meals. Xorn might share their knowledge of the Underdark in exchange for snacks of gems, coins, or magical metals. If starving or angered, xorn might try to forcibly take their meals.
Roll on or choose a result from the Xorn Delicacies table to inspire a xorn's favorite fare.

entries.caption: Xorn Delicacies
rows: Adamantine or mithral.
Coins minted by a long-dead empire.
Fossils or petrified wood.
A gem that's part of a magic item.
The keystone of a great arch or bridge.
Parts of a galeb duhr or stone golem.
A piece of a meteor or moon.
The stone crowning a mountain peak.

trait.name: Fear of Fire
entries: If the yeti takes Fire damage, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The yeti can use its Chilling Gaze and makes two attacks, using Claw or Ice Throw in any combination.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Ice Throw
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 6}, range 30/120 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d4 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Cold damage.

action.name: Chilling Gaze
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, one creature the yeti can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Cold damage, and the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the start of the yeti's next turn unless the target has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the Chilling Gaze of all yetis (but not abominable yetis) for 1 hour.

Yetis hunt alone or in small family groups. They avoid the settlements of other creatures but lurk near paths frequented by traders and herders to pick off unsuspecting prey. Yetis make their homes in icy caves near frozen peaks and at extremes where few dare travel.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The yochlol casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

trait.name: Demonic Restoration
entries: If the yochlol dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in the Abyss.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The yochlol has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The yochlol can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Walker
entries: The yochlol ignores movement restrictions caused by webs.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The yochlol makes two Caustic Lash attacks, and it can use Spellcasting to cast {@spell Web|XPHB} or {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} if available.

action.name: Caustic Lash
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft. {@h}25 ({@damage 6d6 + 4}) Acid damage.

bonus.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The yochlol shape-shifts into a Medium Humanoid or a Medium spider or back into its true form. Its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

reaction.name: Toxic Escape
entries: {@actTrigger} The yochlol is hit by an attack roll. {@actResponse} The yochlol halves the attack's damage to itself (round down), and it teleports to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 feet of itself. {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, each creature within 5 feet of the yochlol's destination space. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Yochlol
entries: {@i Demon of Depraved Will}

Yochlols embody the pernicious will and infectious philosophies of the Abyss. In their rarely seen true forms, these noxious manipulators appear as ever-shifting masses of dripping tentacles and toxic flesh crowned by a single baleful eye. More often, though, yochlols take the form of spiders or zealous cultists. They use manipulative magic and dangerous rhetoric to spread demonic cults, corrupt the righteous, and further the plots of their fiendish overlords. They relish coercing the unwitting into furthering demonic plots and turning mortals against one another.

Most yochlols serve Lolth. The Demon Queen of Spiders claims all yochlols as minions and orders any yochlols that disagree destroyed. In rare cases, yochlols might serve other demon lords, particularly manipulative or changeable ones like Graz'zt, Juiblex, and Zuggtmoy.

Despite their service to demon lords, yochlols harbor their own vicious whims and ambitions. They might claim to speak for their overlords to further their own ambitions or seek to reveal rivals' selfish goals to gain standing with their demonic masters.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Acid damage.

action.name: Acid Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 49 ({@damage 14d6}) Acid damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

Most young black dragons claim a hidden lair—typically a dismal place accessible through deadly ruins or a treacherous bog. They delight in exploiting fearful servants and might terrorize small communities or impress groups of kobolds or troglodytes into their service. Some ally themselves with powerful undead such as death knights and vampires or aberrations such as aboleths and kuo-toa.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d6 + 5}) Slashing damage plus 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Lightning damage.

action.name: Lightning Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 55 ({@damage 10d10}) Lightning damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

Young blue dragons seek to establish themselves as forces to be feared. Many claim isolated communities to rule over or ancient ruins where they might find magical paths to power. These blue dragons might temporarily cooperate with other dragons or powerful villains to gain followers and influence.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks. It can replace two attacks with a use of Sleep Breath.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 40-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 38 ({@damage 11d6}) Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Sleep Breath
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn, at which point it repeats the save. {@actSaveFail 2} The target has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. This effect ends for the target if it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it.
Young brass dragons travel extensively, often spending a few years in a region before circling back to their lair. Some work closely with other metallic dragons, carrying information between allies.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Repulsion Breath.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 2d10 + 5}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Lightning Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 49 ({@damage 9d10}) Lightning damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Repulsion Breath
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} The target is pushed up to 40 feet straight away from the dragon and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

Many young bronze dragons become experts in a type of problem, like driving off pirates or protecting communities from storms. Young bronze dragons collect friends with varied expertise, cultivating a community of experts they can rely on.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Slowing Breath.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Acid Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 40-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 40 ({@damage 9d8}) Acid damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Slowing Breath
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} The target can't take Reactions; its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved; and it can take either an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on its turn, not both. This effect lasts until the end of its next turn.
Young copper dragons forge strong connections with a community or group of friends while flitting from one artistic fixation to the next.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Weakening Breath.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 2d10 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 55 ({@damage 10d10}) Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Weakening Breath
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 17}, each creature that isn't currently affected by this breath in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength-based {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} and subtracts 3 ({@dice 1d6}) from its damage rolls. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
Young gold dragons have seen glimpses of the world's true evils and crusade to oppose them. They often seek bold and direct solutions to problems.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage.

action.name: Poison Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 42 ({@damage 12d6}) Poison damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

Young green dragons frequently control groups of ettercaps, kobolds, thieves, or other cowardly servants. These dragons do so while avoiding other evil dragons, who would sabotage them. Gradually, oppressing weaker creatures and amassing meaningless fortunes bore young green dragons, and they pursue more ambitious ways to indulge their egos.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d6 + 6}) Slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 56 ({@damage 16d6}) Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

Young red dragons number among the most unpredictable of their kind. They seek territories rich with treasures and potential followers, raiding, burning, and slaughtering to enforce their will. Unless these dragons meet significant resistance, they cement their power and begin reigns of terror that can last for centuries.

trait.name: Heat Aura
entries: At the end of each of the remorhaz's turns, each creature in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the remorhaz takes 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Fire damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Fire damage.
Young remorhazes scorch and consume any creatures they can chase down and overwhelm.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Paralyzing Breath.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Cold Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 49 ({@damage 11d8}) Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Paralyzing Breath
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail 1} The target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn, when it repeats the save. {@actSaveFail 2} The target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

Young silver dragons usually have close ties with elder metallic dragons or heroic role models, helping those with great goals achieve their ambitions. They might serve as messengers for or representatives of such do-gooders.

trait.name: Ice Walk
entries: The dragon can move across and climb icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. Additionally, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} composed of ice or snow doesn't cost it extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Cold damage.

action.name: Cold Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 40 ({@damage 9d8}) Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

Young white dragons defend their hunting grounds from rivals. In some cases, kobolds and groups of humanoids might offer food and treasure to young white dragons, attempting to keep the dragons satiated and less likely to prey on their communities.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting (Yuan-ti Form Only)
headerEntries: The yuan-ti casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

trait.name: Magic Resistance

bonus.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The yuan-ti shape-shifts into a Large snake or returns to its true form. If it dies, it stays in its current form. The yuan-ti's game statistics are the same in each form, except where noted. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

Yuan-ti abominations have traded away nearly all evidence of their humanity, coming to resemble giant, upright serpents with scaly arms and hands. In battle, they relish opportunities to crush foes in their powerful coils or strike with their venomous fangs. These abominations can also shape-shift into snakes. In these forms, abominations are indistinguishable from normal serpents.

The true threat of yuan-ti abominations stems not from their physical might but from their cunning. These masterminds often lead cult-like cells of other yuan-ti and direct them in enacting elaborate conspiracies. Abominations avoid jeopardizing themselves, typically scheming from hidden bastions where they're protected by yuan-ti and serpent guardians. These cold-hearted leaders have a unique understanding of the supernatural forces that grant yuan-ti their powers, and they usually have insidious magical traps and contingencies at their disposal.

trait.name: Keen Smell
entries: Bödvar has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on smell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: In bear form, Bödvar makes two Rend attacks. In humanoid form, he makes two Greataxe attacks. In hybrid form, he can attack like a bear or a humanoid. He can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

action.name: Bite (Bear or Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it instead becomes a {@creature Werebear|XMM} under the DM's control and has 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this werebear's curse for 24 hours.

action.name: Greataxe (Humanoid or Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7} to hit, reach 5 ft.. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d12 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Rend (Bear or Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Shape-Shift
entries: Bödvar shape-shifts into a Large bear-humanoid hybrid form or a Large bear, or he returns to his true humanoid form. His game statistics, other than his size, are the same in each form. Any equipment he is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

fluff.name: Bödvar Örskýrsson
entries: {@i I will be jarl until my last breath!}

entries.name: Stubborn as a Bear
entries: Jarl Örskýrsson's lycanthropic curse is a wellkept secret. Not even his closest berserkers realize this is why no blade seems to touch him in battle.

entries.name: Battle Tactics
entries: Jarl Örskýrsson is used to fighting with a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} inside or behind a shield wall, where his powerful swings eviscerate any foe within reach. Örskýrsson will prefer to gang up on single targets with his berserkers, fighting as a grouped unit. However, if Örskýrsson is provoked into a rage (likely by the truth of his brother's fate being exposed) he transforms into his bear form and attacks whoever is the closest within reach. He uses his claws and spreads his attacks to try and inflict as much carnage as possible. He never uses his bite attack (or risks creating another werebear) unless he is consumed by his lycanthropic instincts.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The meyana makes one Bite attack and one Greatclub attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Acid damage, or 10 ({@damage 4d4}) Acid damage if the target is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the meyana. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 12}). Until the grapple ends, the meyana can't Bite another target.

action.name: Greatclub
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage.

fluff.name: Meyana
entries: {@i "Some people eat only plants. A few plants are happy to return the favor."}
Meyanas are bipedal plant creatures that walk on leglike roots, and they can hold and utilize tools in appendages resembling arms. These appendages end in dangerous pincers.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Acid damage, or 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Acid damage if the target is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the meyana. If the target is Small or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). Until the grapple ends, the meyana can't Bite another target.

fluff.name: Young Meyana
entries: {@i "Some people eat only plants. A few plants are happy to return the favor."}
Meyanas are bipedal plant creatures that walk on leglike roots, and they can hold and utilize tools in appendages resembling arms. These appendages end in dangerous pincers.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The norn casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Strands of Fate
entries: When the norn rolls for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, they roll {@dice 3d20} and note down each result. When a creature the norn can see makes a {@dice D20} Test, the norn can choose to replace the number the character rolled on the dice with one of these results instead. Once a result has been used in this way, it is discarded.

trait.name: Nimble Movement
entries: The norn never provokes Opportunity Attacks.

action.name: Wilting Touch
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d6 + 3}) Necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Bolstering Spirit
entries: The norn chooses a creature it can see within 60 feet of itself. That creature regains 8 ({@dice 2d4 + 3}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

reaction.name: Swift Escape
entries: {@actTrigger} The norn is hit by a melee attack.   Response: The attack misses and the norn moves up to its {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}.

fluff.name: Svár
entries: Svár is an ancient fey queen of the winter court. Her domain once stretched much further than the Skuggiskogr. She has, at different times, been an aid and an adversary to the Valikans making their homes on the forest's edge. Though her whims seem capricious to the clanfolk who know her (usually by different names in different villages), earning her favor usually depends on whether she feels respected and appreciated.

As a norn, Svár is a weaver of fates. She provides gifts that allow her beneficiaries to seize a bright destiny, though she never offers a thing without expecting recompense. Though her wrath can be overbearing when she feels betrayed, Svár is not cruel—she's simply contractual. She believes any suffering experienced by mortals is the result of their own choices, never her undue malice.

entries.name: Norn
entries: {@i A person's fate is not their own. We're all playthings for greater beings.}

entries.name: Fate Weavers
entries: Norns are powerful fey who pluck the strands of fate to manipulate destiny. They act as advisors to fey kings and queens, though often hatch their own schemes as well. They use their skills in divination to manipulate others and grow their influence, whether within they fey courts or a region they've claimed as their own.

entries.name: Hag Kin
entries: Norns are frequently mistaken for hags, though hag is really a mortal word for a variety of differing fey kin. Though norns are manipulative, use animal familiars and divine futures, they are not always malicious. They also don't live in huts or stir cauldrons, and don't need a broomstick to fly.

entries.name: Ethereal Spirits
entries: A norn's physical appearance is unimposing, though very strange. They are shaped like humanoids draped in garments of white, red or brown. Yet they move swiftly and ethereally, as if their body had no physical weight. Stories of ghosts whispering ill portents are as likely to have originated from encountering a norn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The puck casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Fey Evasion
entries: If the puck is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, the puck instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The puck has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Plant Bond
entries: If the puck remains within 20 feet of a Huge or smaller plant for 8 hours, it can use special dust to form a bond with the plant, granting it sapience as if by the {@spell Awaken|XPHB} spell. The target gains the ability to understand Sylvan and becomes a puck version of an animated plant, such as a puck tree or puck shrub.

The puck can have only one plant {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way at a time. The condition ends if the puck harms the plant, and the plant can make a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw to end the condition if a request from the puck guarantees the plant's destruction. Plants freed from the charm leave the puck's grove, becoming inanimate again after 24 hours. Otherwise, the plant is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the puck for 30 days, after which the plant becomes the puck's willing servant.

The puck is emotionally bonded with each plant it has animated, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, and enthralled. Provided such a plant is within 1 mile, the puck is aware when the plant takes damage and knows its location. If such a plant is destroyed, the puck has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn as it grieves.

action.name: Superior Invisibility
entries: The puck magically becomes {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until its {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends. Any equipment the puck wears or carries is {@condition Invisible|XPHB} with it.

bonus.name: Plant Manifestation
entries: The puck causes a plantlike duplicate of itself to emerge from a Plant within 120 feet that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or enthralled by it. The puck can act through this duplicate until the end of its turn, at which point the duplicate disappears.

reaction.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the puck can see hits it with an attack.   Response: The puck halves the damage it takes from the attack.

legendary.name: Illusionary Menace
entries: Six images of the puck appear in multiple locations, each moving and speaking independently during the puck's turn. At the start and end of the puck's turn, and one time during the puck's movement, it can teleport to the location of one of these images. The images remain until the next round.

legendary.name: Hostile Nature
entries: Grasping vines and roots manifest in the lair. Strength or {@actSave dex} {@dc 10}, each creature hostile to the puck in the lair. {@actSaveFail} The target is moved up to 20 feet to another unoccupied space in the lair and gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

legendary.name: Poisonous Plants
entries: Inanimate plants in the lair twist and sprout thorns. The area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} to creatures hostile to the puck until the next round, and are subject to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 10} when a creature moves more than half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} in the area. {@actSaveFail} The creature gains the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. {@actSaveSuccess} the creature is Immune to the Poisonous Plants effect for 24 hours.

fluff.name: Raatvidur
entries: Raatvidur was once a dryad that cared for certain trees in the Skuggiskogr, but the corrupting magic of the Winter fey court changed it into a puck. It now travels the forest looking to grow new trees in ground infused with the corpses of fleshy creatures. It wants its former domain back, but Svár now rules this part of the forest instead. It is curious and talkative in a horrifying way.

entries.name: Puck
entries: {@i "I've heard pixie dust is beautiful, magical stuff. The dust I saw was definitely magical, but it wasn't beautiful."}

A puck is a pixie whose hopes and dreams, loves and playfulness, have been erased by mistreatment, betrayal, or loss. Once a beautiful and merry being, a puck is now a sad, twisted monster. Once the transformation happens, the pixie's dust dissipates. Without pixie dust, a pixie can't fly, can't use its magic, and can't turn {@condition invisible}. They lose their ability to commune with nature.

name: Rime Hunger
languages: understands the languages it knew in life

trait.name: Fed Fortitude
entries: For 1 minute after the rime hunger regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, when damage reduces the rime hunger to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 5} plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Fire, Radiant, or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a successful save, the rime hunger drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft.   {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 12}). The rime hunger can only grapple one target at a time.

action.name: Sapping Grasp
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, one creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the rime hunger.   Failure: 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage, and the rime hunger regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the Cold damage dealt.   Success: Half damage only.

fluff.name: Rime Hunger
entries: Rarely straying far from where they died and never willingly wandering into areas of warmth and sunlight, rime hungers are frost-covered, sickly blue corpses that haunt frozen regions in continuous search for victims.

trait.name: Berserker Endurance (Recharge after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: If the berserker takes 10 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 hit points, it is reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The berserker makes two handaxe attacks.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target.   {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Aggressive
entries: The berserker moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} toward a hostile creature it can see.

fluff.name: Valikan Berserker
entries: {@i We die with the taste of our enemies blood on our lips!}

entries.name: Feared and Hated
entries: Valikan berserkers are feared and hated in equal measure. They are sometimes equally unpopular among their fellow clanfolk as much as those from the coastal villages they raid. They are rough, violent, and cruel by habit. They respect no one except their fellows and those who lead them. It takes a fierce but tempered leader to train a warband of berserkers, and keep them from becoming ruffians in their own communities.

entries.name: Theatrical Violence
entries: Berserkers are trained to draw strength from their trauma, rage, and bestial instincts. Before battle they spend time together beating their chests, gnashing their teeth, and howling at the sky. They wear the pelts of animals they wish to embody, be that bear, wolf, or boar. Yet unlike true lycanthropes, this display of beastliness is spiritual and not physical.
