entries.name: Thaumaturge Archmage
entries: Full-fledged Thaumaturge mages are arcane powerhouses. They can easily manipulate magic thrown at them, and teleport around the battlefield while throwing spells at their opponents. They can summon devastating rifts to unleash destructive energy or summon monstrous allies. Multiple mages can combine energies for even grander feats.

name: Watchful Priest
languages: one regional language plus one other language

trait.name: Enraging Sacrifice
entries: When the priest dies, each ally within 20 feet who can see the priest gains 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute.

trait.name: Zealous Aura
entries: The priest radiates an aura of zeal in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from it. Each ally in the area has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} checks, and their successful attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Radiant damage. This aura becomes inactive if the priest has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The priest makes two Castigating Word attacks.

action.name: Castigating Word
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) Radiant damage, and one ally of the priest within 20 feet of the target can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The priest casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

bonus.name: Righteous Morale (1/Day)
entries: The priest chooses up to three other creatures it can see within 20 feet of it. Each target regains 4 ({@damage 1d8}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and has  {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions until the start of the priest's next turn.

entries.name: {@book Watchers of the Faithful|GrimHollowCG24|13|Watchers of the Faithful}

entries: Though the gods no longer grace the heavens, the Arch Seraphs still guide the way.

Born in the fires of the Gods' End, the Watchers of the Faithful rose to prominence first in Castinella as part of its theocratic government. Priests, paladins, chaplains, and other clergy rallied to the remaining Arch Seraphs to hold the fabric of society together. Throwing their faith behind the Arch Seraphs, the major churches reformed into a large organization dedicated to preserving the old faiths in a new form.

This young faction is utterly devoted to Sagrado Valieda's Eternal Dogma: revere the Arch Seraphs, follow their laws as handed down by the Divine Speaker, and destroy all that is unholy and evil in their sight through any means necessary. Where the Arcanist Inquisition is militant in rooting out corruption, the Watchers instead pursue Valieda's mandate to fight for the Arch Seraphs with fiery words. Swords are well and good in defense of the faith, but the real battle is in the hearts and minds of the faithful.

Through preaching and persuasion, the Watchers seek to make the change in the world that they believe the Arch Seraphs desire. Edicts declaring heresy inflame the Inquisition to hunt for monsters or tainted spellcasters. A public proclamation that a government is straying from the true path causes citizens to rise up and force change. Decrees are issued creating new ecclesiastical rules that the faithful embrace over secular laws issued by less religious rulers. Slowly but surely, the Watchers guide the world to a better place.

entries.name: Agents
entries: The Watchers of the Faithful are not soldiers. While they may have some have martial training, their members are priests, spies, and evangelists. Watchers fight with words and not blades. They spur faithful populations to turn against those they deem heretical. They are not single heroes, but rather the voice behind the zealous mob. The most common missionaries are Watchful Priests who combine divine spells with an almost magical command of oratory to enflame crowds.

name: High Priest
languages: one regional language plus two other languages

trait.name: Enraging Sacrifice
entries: When the priest dies, each ally within 40 feet who can see the priest gains 20 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 hour.

trait.name: Zealous Aura
entries: The priest radiates an aura of zeal in a 40-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from it. Each ally in the area has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} checks, and their successful attacks deal an extra {@damage 3d6} Radiant damage. This aura becomes inactive if the priest has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The high priest makes three Sharp Rebuke attacks.

action.name: Sharp Rebuke
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 10} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) Radiant damage, and one ally of the priest within 20 feet of the target can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain 9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and make a melee attack.

action.name: Call Soldiers of the Faith
entries: The high priest calls forth celestials that take the form of {@dice 1d4 + 1||Warrior Veterans} {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans} or {@dice 1d3||Lions} {@creature Lion|XMM|Lions} that enter the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} at the end of the high priest's turn. The celestials follow the priest's commands and remain for 1 minute or until slain.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The priest casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

bonus.name: Inspiring Monologue (3/Day)
entries: The priest chooses any number of allies within 60 feet who can hear the priest. Until the end of the priest's next turn, each target has  {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions and does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

reaction.name: To Me!
entries: {@actTrigger} The priest is attacked or targeted by a spell. {@actResponse} The high priest chooses a Small or Medium ally within 5 feet of itself. The priest and that ally swap places, and the ally gains 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and becomes the target of the attack or spell instead.

entries.name: {@book Watchers of the Faithful|GrimHollowCG24|13|Watchers of the Faithful}

entries: Though the gods no longer grace the heavens, the Arch Seraphs still guide the way.

Born in the fires of the Gods' End, the Watchers of the Faithful rose to prominence first in Castinella as part of its theocratic government. Priests, paladins, chaplains, and other clergy rallied to the remaining Arch Seraphs to hold the fabric of society together. Throwing their faith behind the Arch Seraphs, the major churches reformed into a large organization dedicated to preserving the old faiths in a new form.

This young faction is utterly devoted to Sagrado Valieda's Eternal Dogma: revere the Arch Seraphs, follow their laws as handed down by the Divine Speaker, and destroy all that is unholy and evil in their sight through any means necessary. Where the Arcanist Inquisition is militant in rooting out corruption, the Watchers instead pursue Valieda's mandate to fight for the Arch Seraphs with fiery words. Swords are well and good in defense of the faith, but the real battle is in the hearts and minds of the faithful.

Through preaching and persuasion, the Watchers seek to make the change in the world that they believe the Arch Seraphs desire. Edicts declaring heresy inflame the Inquisition to hunt for monsters or tainted spellcasters. A public proclamation that a government is straying from the true path causes citizens to rise up and force change. Decrees are issued creating new ecclesiastical rules that the faithful embrace over secular laws issued by less religious rulers. Slowly but surely, the Watchers guide the world to a better place.

entries.name: Agents
entries: The Watchers of the Faithful are not soldiers. While they may have some have martial training, their members are priests, spies, and evangelists. Watchers fight with words and not blades. They spur faithful populations to turn against those they deem heretical. They are not single heroes, but rather the voice behind the zealous mob. The most common missionaries are Watchful Priests who combine divine spells with an almost magical command of oratory to enflame crowds.

trait.name: Hold Breath
entries: Snapjaw can hold its breath for 30 minutes.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Snapjaw makes three attacks: two with its bite and one with its tail.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}31 ({@damage 3d10 + 15}) piercing damage, and the target is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 16}). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition restrained}, and Snapjaw can't bite another target.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target not {@condition grappled} by Snapjaw. {@h}24 ({@damage 2d8 + 15}) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a {@dc 16} Strength saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}.

trait.name: Subdermal Plating
entries: {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} scored against Andora become normal hits.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Andora makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 4}) Force damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Lightning damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

reaction.name: She's Alive!
entries: {@actTrigger} Andora takes Lightning damage. {@actResponse} Andora gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Lightning damage dealt.

She's an odd one, that barmaid. Downright obsessed with every murder what happens in this forsaken city and always so modestly dressed because she's covered in stitches underneath. Least, that's what they say.

entries.name: Spark of Life
entries: Created by an eccentric inventor in the Raevan countryside, Andora spent her early years isolated from the outside world in his sprawling manor. The inventor had long ago been expelled from polite society in Raevo for his experiments on the dead, and he frequently opined about the small-mindedness of his contemporaries. He believed that when he finished Andora's education he would reveal her to his peers in Castalore and be applauded for his genius. He may have been, had he not died of natural causes before he considered Andora's education complete.

entries.name: Failed Attempt
entries: As part of her education, Andora learned etiquette, estate management, and several foreign languages—but not even the basics of her inventor's craft. After years of careful research into his methods, she attempted to restore her creator to life using a modified version of the alchemical ritual he'd used to create her. The ritual failed to bring the inventor back to life, but it did waken his corpse and instill it with an insatiable need for violence. Andora fled the estate and began a new life in Castalore.

entries.name: Catch a Killer
entries: Now Andora serves food and drink at a tavern and listens for news of the ruthless serial killer stalking the Raevan countryside with anxious guilt. She believes the murderer is none other than her accidental creation. Although Andora is reluctant to ask for help, if she discovers the player characters are also looking to find and stop the killer, she would share what she knows and join them on their mission. If the player characters help her in destroying her creation, they earn her trust— and she requests to join them for further adventures.

trait.name: Artificial Form
entries: The clockwork horror has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to disease. It does not need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe.

trait.name: Chain the Beast
entries: When the clockwork horror is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it transforms back into {@creature Llanna Deyern|GrimHollowMG24}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The clockwork horror makes a Gore attack and two Slam attacks.

action.name: Gore
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 10 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 10 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Artificial Form
entries: Llanna has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to disease. She does not need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe

trait.name: Defense Mechanism
entries: When Llanna is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, she uses Unchain the Beast, if able. At the end of the duration, she has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack.
entries: Llanna makes two attacks using Dagger.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one creature. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Faerie Glamour
entries: Llanna casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, appearing as a fleshand-blood half-elf child.

bonus.name: Unchain the Beast (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: Llanna transforms into the Clockwork Horror for 1 minute. Her {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are replaced by those of the clockwork horror until the duration ends.

trait.name: Dwarven Resilience
entries: Gillian has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Heavy Hitter
entries: Gillian's {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

trait.name: Innate Toughness
entries: Gillian can add her Constitution modifier to her {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB|AC} instead of her Dexterity modifier (included above).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Gillian makes two {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, or three {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} if she has the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Unarmed Strike
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage.

reaction.name: Now I'm Angry (Recharges after a Long Rest)
entries: {@actTrigger} Gillian becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. {@actResponse} Gillian gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half her {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, which last for 10 minutes. While she has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, she has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
Her? Oh, she's a regular here. Drinks until she gets into a fight, wins more often than not, then calls it a night. Sweet girl.

entries.name: Storm Break
entries: For over a thousand years the Hammerstorm clan mined the Rock-Teeth Mountains to the east of Liesech. After the Weeping Pox swept through the city, it found its way to the Hammerstorm's underground domain, where it decimated the clan. Less than five years later, only a handful of dwarves remained. The survivors realized they could not sustain their ancestral estates and dispersed to other lands. Gillian, the youngest surviving Hammerstorm, settled in Liesech.

entries.name: Demon in a Bottle
entries: Since the dissolution of her clan, Gillian has taken to spending her inheritance drinking away her nights. She came to Liesech hopeful that she could earn a lasting heroic legacy for the Hammerstorm name, but the rampant cynicism and brutality of the city quickly wore her down—and she abandoned her dream. Quick to anger, Gillian has been kicked out of most reputable taverns in the city for starting fights, leaving her to exclusively patronize ale houses of lesser quality.

entries.name: Last Call
entries: Player characters who accomplish a heroic and public act might catch Gillian's attention, causing her to temporarily set aside her bitterness for the chance at redemption. In this circumstance, Gillian tracks the player characters down and asks to join their party. Otherwise, Gillian can be found at any of Liesech's seedy taverns, and she eagerly joins any group of adventurers that pays her tab or helps her win a bar fight.

trait.name: Lasting Curse
entries: If Claunt is restored to his original form by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic, he returns to his porcine form the next time he finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Only a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell, or slaying the spellcaster that cursed him, can permanently remove the curse.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Blackpowder Pistol
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 3} to hit, range 25/100 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Fire damage.

action.name: Satchel of Sorcerous Sales
entries: Claunt reaches into his satchel, dropping in any number of gold pieces to withdraw a nonmagical item with a value equal to or less than the deposited sum. {@item Gold|XDMG} deposited into the satchel goes directly into Gorodyn's infernal treasury. In addition to nonmagical items, Claunt can also purchase the following potions from his satchel: {@item Potion of Climbing|XDMG} (50 GP), {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG} (25 GP), {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG} (100 GP), {@item Potion of Resistance|XDMG} (200 GP), and {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG|Potion of Waterbreathing} (200 GP). Only Claunt can attune to this item.

reaction.name: Enlightened Self-Interest
entries: Claunt takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.
We're out of stock on that particular item. If you don't mind who you do business with, there's a pigheaded merchant in the market right now who claims to have anything a body could want.

entries.name: Cursed Merchant
entries: Once a successful merchant in Morencia, Claunt was cursed to a porcine form by a powerful sorcerer for steeply raising the prices of staple foods during a famine. In the years since, one business venture after another failed as partners ended contracts with him out of an abundance of superstitious caution. Though not destitute, he lived far beneath the means he once enjoyed and became desperate to reverse his fortune.

entries.name: Friends in Low Places
entries: To that end, Claunt took to worshipping Gorodyn. After a particularly bad falling out with a previous business partner, Claunt made a terrible sacrifice to the Arch Daemon of Avarice and was rewarded with a {@i satchel of sorcerous sale}. With supply no longer an issue, and hoping to escape the consequences of the sacrifice, Claunt began traveling to sell his wares. It wasn't long before he discovered that even individual buyers wanted little to do with someone in his condition.

entries.name: Open for Business
entries: Now more distraught than ever, Claunt is most likely to be encountered on the road or the outskirts of major settlements, living on whatever meager sales he can make. He happily travels with any player characters agreeing to purchase his goods on an ongoing basis. If Claunt believes he can mentor (or exploit) a particularly charismatic player character, he offers to provide them with supplies if they serve as the face of his business. If he believes the player characters as a group are capable, he asks their help in tracking down and slaying the sorcerer who cursed him.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Abree casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Smite
entries: When Abree hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, she can expend a spell from her Spellcasting action. The spell has no effect, and the attack deals an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage for a 2/Day spell or 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage for a 1/Day spell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Abree makes two attacks, using Dagger or Vile Spit in any combination.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Vile Spit
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 13}, one creature Abree can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Poison damage and the target {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Hunter's Mark (2/Day)
entries: Abree casts {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

bonus.name: Inquisitor's Eye (Recharges after a Long Rest)
entries: Abree grants herself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}), Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}), and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks for 10 minutes.
She came through two nights ago looking like she was on the run. If I'd known she was a deserter I'd have alerted the authorities straightaway, Empyreus' truth!

entries.name: Trial by Fire
entries: Having lost her parents at a young age to a wicked spellcaster, Abree Simoni dedicated her life to becoming an inquisitor. Her diligent study of Empyreus' dogma earned her the privilege of joining the Inquisition's ranks at fourteen years old. Over the course of her first years in the Arcanist Inquisition, Abree's faith was unwavering. When her superiors directed her to root out corruption, she did so with meticulous fervor When asked to put fire to the kindling beneath accused spellcasters, she did so without hesitation. Then she was deployed to the village where she and her brother had been raised by distant family following the death of their parents. She discovered her brother was accused of casting magic. Her unit was charged with incarcerating him until his trial and execution.

entries.name: Crisis of Faith
entries: Certain her brother would never practice magic, Abree tried to find proof of his innocence. When she couldn't, turning up witnesses who'd seen him engage in ritual bloodletting, she did the unthinkable—she betrayed the Inquisition and fled town with her brother. They were on the run only a few days when Abree woke in the middle of the night to find her brother had left her on her own. With no answers to the accusation against her brother, and no excuse for her superiors, Abree continued her flight from the region.

entries.name: Lost and Alone
entries: Now Abree travels from town to town, trying to make her way out of the Castinellan Provinces unnoticed. Should the player characters win Abree's trust by showing her kindness, she requests their assistance. Her first goal is to find her brother and ensure his safety. She also wishes to flee the lands where the Arcanist Inquisition holds power. If anyone among the player characters is an inquisitor, she changes her plans and asks if they could vouch for her so she can return to her post. Regardless, if the player characters agree to assist Abree in keeping her safe from the Inquisition, she happily travels with and fights alongside them.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Grimaldo casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit 5} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Bloody Brilliant
entries: Grimaldo has a pool of seven {@dice 7d12|d12s}. Whenever he casts a sangromancy spell that calls for the expenditure of a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die}, he can spend an equal number of these d12s instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Grimaldo makes two Necrosis attacks.

action.name: Bejeweled Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one creature. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Necrosis
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Necrotic damage, and the target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of Grimaldo's next turn.

bonus.name: Blood Magic (4/Day)
entries: Grimaldo casts {@spell Blood Rush|GrimHollowPG24} (level 2 version), {@spell Crimson Lash|GrimHollowPG24}, or {@spell Wilting Smite|GrimHollowPG24} using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.
They say the Thorn of Sante Viegre has killed a hundred inquisitors. It's probably closer to ten, but I can't deny that the brutality of his attacks seems to resonate with the common folk.

entries.name: Family Secrets
entries: Grimaldo Simoni and his older sister were raised by cousins. Told from an early age that his parents had been killed by a warlock, Grimaldo was tortured by the sense of loss. A sensitive child, he noticed that older villagers seemed to make a point of avoiding him and his sister. Only after his sister left to join the Arcanist Inquisition did he discover the reason late one night when his cousins had been drinking: his parents were not killed by a spellcaster but had been accused of being spellcasters themselves and subsequently put to death by inquisitors.

entries.name: Thicker Than Blood
entries: Shortly after learning the truth of his parents' deaths, Grimaldo began to study the occult. He became obsessed with following in his parents' footsteps and avenging them by bringing pain and suffering to as many inquisitors as he could. When a traveling merchant came through his village with a book on blood magic, Grimaldo spent everything he had to buy it. Eventually rumors began to spread around his village that he was pursuing the arcane arts. The Inquisition was notified. He was captured easily and assumed he would die. His sister, however, who had joined the Inquisition, was charged with detaining him while he awaited his trial. She released him and led him away from sure death. For a few days they traveled together, but Grimaldo knew that she could not travel the same path as he. He snuck away from her and forged his own trail.

entries.name: The Thorn of Sante Viegre
entries: Grimaldo spends his time continuing to hone his mastery of blood magic and carrying out guerilla attacks on small units of inquisitors in the Sante Viegre region of the Castinellan Provinces. He shows no mercy in these attacks, killing inquisitors and those who help them hunt arcanists. He leaves his victims in a state that shocks and terrifies anyone finding them. Grimaldo has many associates among wine smugglers in the area and is always looking to recruit those who might be sympathetic to his cause. If the player characters are known to dislike the Inquisition, or have a run in with inquisitors, Grimaldo might approach them to join forces.

name: Ancient Blightscale Dragon

trait.name: Accursed Death
entries: {@actSave con}: {@dc 22}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the dragon when it dies. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats its save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

However, a target that fails two saves is cursed. While cursed, the target can't regain Hit Points. Upon being cursed and every 24 hours thereafter, the target takes 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Necrotic damage, can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken. If this effect reduces the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum to 0, it dies.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day or 5/Day in Lair)
entries: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon uses Sickening Presence, then makes three Rend attacks.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 15} to hit, reach 15 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 2d8 + 8}) Force damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Sickening Presence

action.name: Swarm Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 22}, each creature in a 90-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 35 ({@damage 10d6}) Piercing damage plus 42 ({@damage 12d6}) Poison damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

legendaryHeader: Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the dragon can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The dragon regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary.name: Bursting Pus
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 22}, each creature in a 30-footlong, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} The target is covered in eye-watering pus. It has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition and can't ingest anything until a creature takes an action to scrub off the pus. The effect ends early if the creature is doused or submerged in water. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The dragon can't use this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary.name: Tail Swipe
entries: The dragon makes one Rend attack.

legendary.name: Take Flight
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 22}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the dragon. {@actSaveFail} The target takes 17 ({@damage 2d8 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The dragon flies up to half its {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}. The dragon can't use this action again until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Ancient vampires should be in a position where adventurers opposing them would have to go through several levels of challenge and danger just to get a clue that the ancient vampire even exists. Such a creature is strong and resourceful enough that it would be at the center of an entire campaign, and its reach would touch on a great number of schemes, plots, and intrigues. The ancient vampire would have created a vast number of spawn, young, and adult vampires that serve it. More importantly, entire groups or organizations would act on behalf of the ancient one. Assassin guilds, military groups, baronies or kingdoms, and entire church sects would, wittingly or unwittingly, be doing the work of the ancient vampire. And most importantly, heroes would have to survive the attention of all those groups, fighting their way through to the leadership, just to get an inkling that the ancient vampire is involved.

entries: I thought the brutes were going to tear me apart. Little did I know they had a worse fate planned for me.

entries.name: Physically Imposing
entries: Already an imposing creature, a bugbear afflicted with vampirism becomes even more of a hulking brute. Their muscles grow enormous, with ropey veins bulging from flesh that their fur fails to cover. Bugbear vampires are capable of great feats of strength. They eschew the weapons they used in life in favor of the visceral close combat of tooth and claw.

entries.name: Reckless Predators
entries: Corruption has made bugbears wild and chaotic in their normal lives. Vampirism has a similar effect. A Bugbear Vampire is a brutal fighter who aims to kill quickly without much consideration for personal safety. Few vampires survive to the adult stage, but even fewer Bugbear Vampires do.

entries.name: Might and Stealth
entries: Only an elder vampire of considerable might can prevent young Bugbear Vampires from reducing prey to gory remains. But under such direction, Bugbear Vampires are effective — if ruthless— agents for missions that require infiltration or a bloody ambush.

entries.name: Bugbear Vampire Customization
entries: A Bugbear Vampire is stronger than others of its age, having a higher Strength score and the Rampage trait— see the stat block. The vampire relies on this brute force and much less on reason and charm, so their Intelligence and Charisma is often lower. Such vampires outgrow the brashness of the spawn stage more slowly, and they're therefore often still chaotic evil. The vampire loves to surprise foes, then fight, feed, and kill in an efficient but brash manner. A Bugbear Vampire has the Clawing Lunge, Reckless, and Surprise Mauling traits, as shown in the stat block. As with many other creatures who have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} in life, the Bugbear Vampire has {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} superior to that of typical vampires its age (add 30 feet).

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The muscles of a Bugbear Vampire can provide a gruesome reward. Somebody who has proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill can harvest muscle tissue from a Bugbear Vampire. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or the {@skill Arcana} skill can then treat the muscles with reagents worth 2,500 GP over 14 days. Exposure to sunlight during this process causes the tissue to wither and become useless. Otherwise, the process requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check and, if successful, produces one {@item Muscle Graft|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The vampiric curse intensifies a bugbear's worst tendencies while increasing their strength to astonishing levels. Bugbear vampires relish close combat.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Bugbear vampires are so bloodthirsty and overconfident that they can fail to look out for their own safety. Goading such a vampire into anger is one way to make them reckless.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Bugbear Vampires play a strange role in the history of their kind. Having already succumbed to {@disease Tormach's Rage|GrimHollowMG24}, bugbears are fearsome killers. Those bugbears who succumb to vampirism take on new powers, but they no longer fit into the plans of Tormach. Different groups of normal bugbears might treat a Bugbear Vampire much differently. Some might assume the vampirism is another blessing from Tormach, while others might see it as a corruption. Adventurers might easily find themselves caught in a struggle between a group of bugbears and a Bugbear Vampire's followers.

I heard the mournful song as I rounded the corner of the crumbling church. By the time I realized the creature singing had been feasting on a family visiting the graveyard, it was nearly too late for me.

entries.name: Sorrowful Singers
entries: A Downcast Vampire is a sad, broken creature. Stripped of divinity and further shackled by the curse of vampirism, they spend their days in sorrow, distracting themselves by killing and singing. Creatures hearing a Downcast Vampire's dirge can be driven to extremes, and some lose consciousness.

entries.name: Creature of the Light
entries: Although the curse of vampirism changes the downcast, celestial ancestry makes the vampire less susceptible to turning. The undead state insulates the celestial form completely against Necrotic damage. But the vampire's form is less mutable.

entries.name: Downcast Vampire Customization
entries: A Downcast Vampire often has higher Wisdom than other vampires, although the change into vampiric form costs the vampire their celestial magic. Downcast vampires lack the Beast Form and Mist Form actions, although the creature still turns to mist if close to destruction. They also have the Turn Resistance trait. Young and older Downcast Vampires have the Dirge action.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The flesh of a Downcast Vampire, reduced to ash, can be a potent healing agent if activated properly. (Using the flesh in this way precludes rendering it into ointment but doesn't prevent the use of the vampire's claws, tongue, or bones.) Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or the {@skill Arcana} skill and {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} can take the ash from one adult or older Downcast Vampire's remains and brew it for 1 day with a {@item Potion of Healing|XPHB}. If the brewer succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check, the brew becomes a {@item Potion of Heal|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Failing the check results in a {@item Potion of Harm|GrimHollowMG24} (see chapter 4), although it appears no different from its counterpart until consumed.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Downcast were anchored to the world when their lords perished. The curse of vampirism bars them from returning to celestial realms. Mentioning this fact might cause debilitating sadness, but it could also lead to reckless rage.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A Downcast Vampire's mournful dirge sends all but the bravest who hear it running in terror. Some are so overwhelmed, they pass out.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A Downcast Vampire is immune to Radiant damage and the creature is extremely hard to turn.

name: Dragonborn Vampire (Young)

items: fire

items.name: Brutal Attacks
entries: When the vampire scores a Critical Hit on a melee attack, it deals an extra die of damage.

items.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Fire damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 16}) from one of two claws.

items.name: Bite
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or that has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage. The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that amount

items.name: Breath Weapon {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Fire damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

legendaryHeader: Legendary Action Uses: 2 (3 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the vampire can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The vampire regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries: The vampire had golden scales and glittering eyes. It breathed fire, charring and rotting flesh at the same time.

entries.name: Precise Predator
entries: Dragonborn subjected to vampirism become calculating killers. They enjoy the hunt and the fight, but they approach each with cunning and skill. Even dragonborn vampire spawn are calmer and more precise than is normal for vampires of that age. This love of the hunt and battle, nevertheless, makes dragonborn vampires more likely to take risks, which their pack mates take advantage of. Many dragonborn vampires perish in confrontations before aging into more power.

entries.name: Rotting Breath
entries: Vampirism pollutes the draconic bloodline with a curse of undeath. This corruption strengthens the dragonborn's breath weapon, allowing it to deal the damage it dealt before alongside life-withering necrosis. A dragonborn vampire can also use this breath more often than living counterparts.

entries.name: Dragonborn Vampire Customization
entries: A dragonborn vampire retains an edge in Strength compared to their peers. Also, the vampire has the resistance and breath weapon their draconic ancestry grants. Use the vampire's {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} as their level for the damage the breath deals. However, the breath also deals Necrotic damage equal to that the vampire's bite deals. This Necrotic damage neither reduces a target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum nor causes the vampire to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Vampirism accentuates the predator aspects of a dragonborn's draconic ancestry, and so their breath recharges more quickly their of living counterparts. A dragonborn vampire also has the Brutal Attacks trait.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A dragonborn vampire's teeth hold magic more readily than other vampires. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} can fashion a vampire's fang into a {@item Corrupted Tusk-dagger|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Making the weapon requires 5 days of work and other materials worth 250 GP. To utilize the teeth properly, the smith or somebody assisting them must have proficiency in the {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion} skill.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Dragonborn vampires are reputed to be cunning and precise hunters who relish combat.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Vampirism heightens the draconic ancestry of a dragonborn, who retains the resistances and breath weapon of that line.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A dragonborn vampire's breath weapon not only deals elemental damage, but also withers life, and the vampire can use that breath more often than typical for dragonborn.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: The key to defeating a vampire is learning and exploiting its weaknesses while avoiding its strengths. A cautious vampire does everything in its power to hide those weaknesses. Unfortunately, players have access to fancy tomes detailing monsters that their characters do not have access to. Fortunately, GMs have their imaginations!

One way to keep players on their toes is to change some of the weaknesses and strengths for monsters, and a dragonborn vampire is an excellent candidate for change. With a connection to elements because of their draconic ancestries, dragonborn vampires' stats can be changed to show that elemental affinity, or the perversion of it. For example, Fire or Cold damage instead of Radiant damage may be needed to negate a red dragonborn vampires Regeneration.

items.name: Nightmare Walker
entries: To benefit from a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the vampire must touch the dreams of at least one Humanoid within 1 mile. After finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the vampire gains one skill or tool proficiency until the end of its next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Multiattack
entries: The vampire makes two Claw attacks and uses Bite or Nightmare Killer.

items.name: Bite
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or that has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Psychic damage. The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that amount. A Humanoid reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by this damage and then buried rises the following sunset as a vampire spawn under the vampire's control.

items.name: Nightmare Killer {@recharge}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 16}, one creature the vampire can see within 120 feet. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Psychic damage taken, and the vampire regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that amount.

While {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, the target is immersed in an illusory dreamscape in which the vampire is a manifestation of the target's fears. If it chooses, the vampire can prevent the target from sensing {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creatures. The target rationalizes any inconsistencies between the real world and the dreamscape.

On its turn, the vampire can forego its Bite and force the target to repeat the save, taking damage again on a failure or ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts for 1 minute, ending early if the vampire dies or ends its turn more than 120 feet from the target.

items.name: Dreamer Escape
entries: {@actTrigger} The vampire drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} outside its resting place. {@actResponse} The vampire shape-shifts into a cloud of luminous ectoplasmic vapor ({@variantrule Speed|XPHB} 5 ft., {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} 30 ft. [Hover]) that sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius. Anything it is wearing transforms with it. If the vampire can't shape-shift, it is destroyed.

While in vapor form, the vampire can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless and can enter an enemy's space and stop there. If air can pass through a space, the mist can do so, but it can't pass through liquid. It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight. If the vampire ends its turn inside an object, the vampire dies and returns to its true form, its body merged with the object.

While it has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in vapor form, the vampire dies if it takes damage three times or Radiant damage once. It can't return to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in its resting place, it returns to its vampire form and has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until it regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. It regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} after spending an hour there.
It moved in an eerie pattern, stumbling with some steps, as graceful as a dancer with others. It called to mind my mother, before and after she fell ill. Then, I realized I was alone in the dark.

entries.name: Nightmare Feaster
entries: Dreamer vampires take their sustenance from nightmares, visiting sleeping mortals and inflicting night terrors. When close to a sapient creature, a dreamer vampire can plunge that victim into an illusory nightmare world and feast upon the victim's terror.

entries.name: Dream Voices
entries: A young or older dreamer vampire communicates and moves in enigmatic ways. Their mind taps the dream world regularly, and the vampire filters useful information that often comes in a cryptic form. Dreamer vampires have been known to accurately predict coming events, especially catastrophes, despite possessing no skill in divination magic.

entries.name: Dreamer Vampire Customization
entries: A dreamer vampire needs to eat the psychic energy from others, and does so in small ways via dreams. Dreamer vampires are resistant to psychic damage instead of necrotic. They are a little less agile and more analytical than vampires of a similar age. All dreamer vampires have the Nightmare Walker trait. A young or older dreamer vampire trades in illusion instead of reality and can't change their shape. Instead, they have the Dreamer Escape reaction. Young and older dreamer vampires have the Nightmare Killer action, too.
A dreamer vampire might be more ponderous than other vampires of their age (lower Dexterity and AC). But the vampire makes up for that loss with resilience (higher Constitution and hit points).

Horrid tales speak of ancient dreamer vampires who can use Nightmare Killer on multiple targets. To make this legend true, once per day, the ancient dreamer vampire can use Nightmare Killer on creatures of its choice within a 30-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point the vampire chooses within range of the effect.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The brain of a young or older dreamer vampire has a connection to nightmares and bizarre prescience. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB} can prepare the brain according to a fabled recipe. Doing so requires other ingredients worth 250 GP, and the preparer must succeed on a {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check. If the process is successful, the brain produces four portions, and each portion makes the eater impossible to surprise for 24 hours. An improperly prepared brain has only the deleterious effect of eating a vampire body part.

A spellcaster can eat the whole properly prepared brain of an adult or older dreamer vampire as part of casting the {@spell Foresight|XPHB} spell. Doing so extends the spell's casting time to 10 minutes but increases the spell's duration to 24 hours.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A dreamer vampire is as connected to dreams as a living dreamer, but the vampire prefers nightmares.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Dreamer vampires damage the mind more than the body when they feed. They can create a nightmare dreamscape to drain victims of psychic energy.

items.name: Earth Glide
entries: The vampire can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and any nonmagical stone. While doing so, the vampire doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

items.name: Earthen Escape
entries: The vampire has the following flaws:
{@i Forbiddance.} The vampire can't enter a residence without an invitation from an occupant.
{@i Running Water.} The vampire takes 20 Acid damage when it ends its turn in running water.
{@i Stake to the Heart.} The vampire dies if a weapon that deals Piercing damage is driven into the vampire's heart while it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.
{@i Sunlight Hypersensitivity.} The vampire takes 15 Radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks.

items.name: Earthen Escape
entries: {@actTrigger} The vampire drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} outside its resting place. {@actResponse} The vampire sinks into nonmagical unworked earth or any nonmagical stone. The substance must be large enough to hold the vampire's body and must be within 50 feet of the vampire. If the vampire can't meld with earth or stone, it is destroyed

Once within the earth or stone, the vampire has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until it regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The vampire can only hear what's going on beyond the earth or stone and makes Wisdom (Perception) checks to do so with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. It regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} after spending an hour there.
If the earth or stone is damaged and becomes too small to hold the vampire, the vampire is destroyed and its body is expelled into the nearest unoccupied space.
Dwarves delve, even when they're dead and need blood to survive.

entries.name: Earth Bound
entries: Vampirism amplifies the dwarven connection to earth and stone, awakening ancient elemental connections in the dwarf's bloodline. Dwarf vampires burrow like ghosts passing through walls, and instead of turning to mist when near death, they meld into the nearest earth or stone. Similarly, a person slain by a dwarf vampire's bite spontaneously sinks into the ground.

entries.name: Silver Scorned
entries: For some reason, the corruption of vampirism makes dwarves susceptible to silver. They dislike its presence near them, and wounds from silver weapons slow the vampire's healing. A silver spike through the vampire's heart is a sure way to destroy them, although unlike other vampires, wood isn't useful in that regard.

entries.name: Dwarf Vampire Customization
entries: Vampirism connects a dwarf to the element of earth more closely. A dwarf vampire has the speed of a dwarf (25 feet) but can burrow and glide through some types of earth and stone without disturbing it, gaining a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} and Earth Glide trait. The vampire retains much dwarven resilience in the form of high Constitution, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to effects that turn undead. The vampire's {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} is also better than normal for a vampire of that age.
A dwarf vampire is slower on their feet (lower Dexterity and AC). However, their toughness is legend (higher Constitution and hit points).

Young and older dwarf vampires cannot turn to mist as other vampires do. Instead, these vampires sink into the earth or stone when near death—see the Earthen Escape trait. Those a dwarf vampire slays with a bite also sink into the earth. This burial is enough to assure rebirth as a {@creature Vampire Spawn|GrimHollowMG24}.

Dwarf vampires have a {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to silver unusual for vampires and ironic for dwarves. It's an odd reversal of an affinity for valuable metals dwarves have in life and the elemental expressions of a dwarf vampire.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Dwarf vampires often display avarice. They collect treasure with zeal. Most wear numerous valuable objects and pieces of jewelry, eschewing anything silver.

Someone who eats the tongue of an adult or older dwarf vampire gains no ability to speak with beasts but can instead speak to nonmagical, unworked earth or nonmagical stone for 10 minutes. These substances can tell what creatures have been within 10 feet of them within the last 24 hours, as well as what they conceal, if anything. Earth and stone have limited perspective but offer as much information as they are asked for.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Dwarf vampires spend their time hunting prey or wealth, preferably under the ground.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Vampirism connects a dwarf strongly to the earth. The vampire can meld into earth and stone and travel through it. They do so when near death, hiding in the earth to heal.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Silver irritates a dwarf vampire and makes their wounds slow to heal. But Poison is ineffective against a dwarf vampire, and only the most faithful can hope to turn one.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Dwarf vampires should be particularly dangerous, as they can hide in lairs deep underground. Passing easily through the earth, they have access to areas that heroes might find hard to reach. Remember, though, that these vampires need access to blood, so they must come out of their hiding places as some point.

items.name: Multiattack
entries: The vampire makes three Claw attacks and uses Bite.

items.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Slashing damage and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 19}) from one of two claws.

items.name: Fey Majesty
entries: The vampire casts Dominate Person, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}), and the duration is 24 hours. The target is a willing recipient of the vampire's Bite, the damage of which doesn't end the spell. While within 300 feet of the target, the vampire can communicate telepathically with it.

Each time the vampire or the vampire's allies do anything harmful to the target, it repeats the save, ending the effect on a success. The effect ends early if the vampire dies, is on a different plane of existence than the target, or takes a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end the effect.

items.name: Move and Claw
entries: The vampire moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes a Claw attack.

bonus.name: Distressing Whispers
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}, one creature within 300 feet of the vampire. {@actSaveFail} The target is A) filled with despair and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks, or B) confused, as with the Confusion spell. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

She was ancient, tall and gaunt, imperious and fierce. Her skin was translucent and slightly luminous with the crimson fluid beneath lending it a bizarre, vibrating flush. Her anger and sorrow reached from her, sharing the sense of a time before my people cut and burned the forest. I wept.

entries.name: Fey Horror
entries: Vampirism emphasizes fey qualities among elves. The elf becomes wispier, more ephemeral and haunting. An elf vampire's fey resistances become enhanced to the point that the vampire is hard to turn and can't be rendered {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} or {@condition Charmed|XPHB}. The vampire enters a trance for a few hours instead of sleeping, remaining aware of their surroundings during that time.

entries.name: Fey Majesty
entries: Fey ancestry and vampirism combine to give an elf vampire influence over the minds of humanoids and beasts. Legends of vampire enchantments could stem from the powers of elf vampires, who might have been the first to suffer this curse. The power of mental influence also allows the vampire to share sorrow and fear with those the vampire has {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, or to befuddle their minds.

Also, those the elf vampire {@condition Charmed|XPHB|Charms} for long periods develop an attachment to the vampire, which can grow into a macabre affection even when the creature isn't {@condition Charmed|XPHB}. Tales say ancient elf vampires can {@condition Charmed|XPHB|Charm} creatures other than humanoids and beasts.

entries.name: Elf Vampire Customization
entries: As shown in the following stats, young and older elf vampires gain Turn Resistance and immunity to being {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or rendered {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. Although some wood elves are an exception, most elf vampires do not take on animal form and, therefore, lack the Beast Form action. Young and older elf vampires also gain the Fey Majesty action, but until the vampire is ancient, as is the one in the stat block, they can affect only humanoids and beasts with this power.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: An elf vampire's flesh turns to glittering powder when the vampire dies. This powder can still be used to make the ointment rendered vampire flesh can make. However, this dust can also be used as a material component for any enchantment spell or spell that deals Necrotic damage. If a spellcaster uses the dust in this way, the spell save DC for the spell increases by 2. If the spell requires an attack roll, the caster scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20, and any damage die for Necrotic damage that rolls a 1 is treated as a 2. One vampire produces enough dust for two uses, plus one use per age category of the vampire beyond spawn.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Elf vampires don't sleep, so they are aware all the time. And they can't be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or knocked {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Fey ancestry combines with vampirism to render elf vampires resistant to effects that turn undead.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Elf vampires can manipulate the minds of beasts and people. Legend says that ancient elf vampires can sway the minds of other creatures.

items.name: Speak with Beasts
entries: The vampire can communicate with Beasts as if they shared a language.

items.name: Turn Resistance
entries: The vampire has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

items.name: Multiattack
entries: The vampire makes two Claw attacks and uses Bite. It can replace one Claw attack with a use of Trip.

items.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature and both Claw attacks hit, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Trip
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 17}, one creature within 5 feet of the vampire. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Command Beasts
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15}, up to three Beasts that can hear or see the vampire within 30 feet of it. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target sees the vampire as a leader to be heeded and protected, following its verbal commands and acting in its interest even when left without a command.

Each time the vampire or the vampire's allies do anything harmful to a target, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until the vampire dies, is on a different plane of existence than the target, or takes a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end the effect.

The vampire appeared among the wolves as if it had been one of them moments before. Despite its childlike size, it retained a feral aspect. The wolves treated it like their leader and died to protect it.

entries.name: Vampiric Throwback
entries: Gnome vampires are fierce and feral but still clever, and their fangs and claws are outsized for a small frame. The curse connects them with their ancestral roots, putting them in closer touch with nature and animals. As a gnome vampire ages, their connection with beasts grows stronger. Older vampires might have numerous animal allies, groomed over the ages as loyal minions. But gnome vampire spawn can speak to animals and easily cultivate relationships with them.

entries.name: Mental Mettle
entries: Although vampirism causes a kind of regression in a gnome's ancestral traits, the curse fortifies the mental strength common to gnomes. Gnome vampires are notoriously resistant to anything that forces them to act against their will or subjugates their personality or mental faculties.

entries.name: Gnome Vampire Customization
entries: Gnome vampires are Small, with a speed of 25 feet, and often weaker than other vampires (lower Strength). But they're just as agile and vicious—their attacks are just as accurate and damaging—and they can have more cunning (higher Intelligence). When converting the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to {@dice d6|d6s} for a Small creature, keep the hit point maximum as close to the same as possible. A gnome vampire has enhanced {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} (add 30 feet) and retains the resilient mind of a gnome, having Turn Resistance and proficiency in Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. Gnome vampires also have the Speak with Beasts trait, and those young and older gnome vampires that can speak with beasts have the Command Beast action. Ancient gnome vampires can command five or more beasts with one action.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Gnome vampires love trinkets and mementos. A gnome vampire has several such personal objects. These objects might not have much real value, but the vampire holds them dear and might bargain to regain or protect them.

Eating the tongue of a young or older gnome vampire imparts the beast speech benefits normal for the tongues of all adult vampires. The tongue of an adult or ancient gnome vampire allows the eater to cast {@spell animal friendship} (spell save {@dc 13} for adult, {@dc 15} for ancient) at will while the beast speech effect lasts. The effect of an ancient tongue lasts 2 hours.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Gnome vampires display a strong will like that of gnomes, allowing them to resist effects that work on the mind or other mental faculties.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Vampirism throws a gnome back to some ancient time when gnomes were strongly connected to natural beasts. The vampire can speak to and command animals.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The resistance to mental effects extends to effects that turn undead.

items.name: Nimble Stealth
entries: The vampire can move through the space of any creature larger than it. Also, the vampire can attempt to {@action Hide|XPHB} when obscured by a creature at least one size larger than it.

items.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d6 + 4}) Slashing damage, and the vampire has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack before the end of its turn.

items.name: Bite
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or that has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage. The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that amount

items.name: Innocent Eyes
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 30 feet of the vampire that can see it targets it with an attack or harmful effect that affects only the vampire. {@actResponse}—{@actSave wis} {@dc 14} (the target benefits from any traits that help it avoid the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition). {@actSaveFail} The target must choose another target or effect, or lose that use of the attack, spell, or effect. The target can choose not to cast a spell or use an ability rather than lose that use of it. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this vampire's Innocent Eyes for 24 hours.

items.name: Scurry
entries: The vampire moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. It can also use the {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
entries: The vampire take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

They were among us before we knew they were coming, and they easily avoided our weapons, dodging among our legs, tearing with their claws and fangs. When Johan finally got a bead on one, he found he couldn't shoot such an 'innocent' being.

entries.name: Deadly Speed
entries: Halfling vampires are supernaturally agile and their small size does little to decrease their deadliness. A halfling vampire moves easily among larger foes, spreading mayhem while sidestepping reprisals. And if resistance becomes too much, a halfling vampire retreats and hides, returning to the fray on their terms.

entries.name: Brash Action
entries: A halfling vampire, especially a spawn or young vampire, is less likely to think before acting than other vampires. They eagerly go for food and pleasure, showing little restraint, and they can kill without intending to. Being so heedless of consequences and focused on immediate reward means halfling vampires have a harder time surviving to older ages than most other vampires.

entries.name: Corrupted Fortune
entries: Halflings have uncanny luck, and in part, that fortune is due to the childlike look and nature of many halflings. Halfling vampires use this natural charm as a defense. Those who wish the vampire harm find it difficult to follow through on an attack while looking into the vampire's big, innocent eyes.

entries.name: Halfling Vampire Customization
entries: A halfling vampire is Small and has less practical Strength than Medium vampires, along with smaller claws and teeth. But a halfling vampire shows amazing alacrity (higher Dexterity), moving with amazing grace past other creatures and disappearing with little cover—see Cunning Action and Nimble Stealth. When converting the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to {@dice d6|d6s} for a Small creature, keep the hit point maximum as close to the same as possible. Halfling vampires have a childlike aspect that supernaturally influences other creatures to refrain from harming the vampire in the Innocent Eyes reaction. Vampirism also accentuates halfling bravery, making the vampire fearless. But halfling vampires lack Beast Form.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} can distill the blood of a young or older halfling vampire into a {@item Potion of Speed|XDMG}. A young vampire produces enough for one dose, an adult for two, and an ancient for three. Each dose requires 3 days of brewing and other reagents worth 500 GP, and the brewer must succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. Drinking one of these potions has the same effect as eating any vampire part.
Consuming the eye of a young or older halfling vampire also affects the eater as if {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} were cast on them.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Halfling vampires are incredibly stealthy and fast. They can attack and disappear before victims realize what's happening.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A halfling vampire can prevent you from attacking them with a look. This defense is a form of enchantment magic.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: The social nature of halflings puts them in a strange position. They're more likely than most vampires to be found interacting with society, meaning more opportunity to feed. They must then rely on their luck and cunning to stay hidden, as opposed to relying to hidden, isolated lairs.

items.name: Speak with Beasts
entries: The vampire can communicate with Beasts as if they shared a language.

items.name: Water Reliance
entries: After 4 hours without being immersed in water or drinking blood, the vampire takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Acid damage, and takes this damage again at the end of every subsequent hour. The vampire can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} lost in this way until it drinks blood or is immersed in water.

items.name: Shape-Shift
entries: If the vampire isn't in sunlight, it shape-shifts into a Small or smaller terrestrial beast ({@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} 30 ft.), a Medium or smaller aquatic beast ({@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} 30 ft.), or a Medium cloud of mist ({@variantrule Speed|XPHB} 5 ft., {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} 20 ft. [hover]), or it returns to its vampire form. Anything it is wearing transforms with it.

While in beast form, the vampire can't speak. Its game statistics, other than its size and {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, are unchanged. If its beast form lacks claws, its Claw attacks become Slam attacks that deal Bludgeoning damage instead of Slashing damage.

While in mist form, the vampire can't take any {@variantrule Action|XPHB|Actions}, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless and can enter an enemy's space and stop there. If air can pass through a space, the mist can do so, but it can't pass through liquid. It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage.
The creature's flesh was loose and wrinkled, like he had soaked too long. His hair was tangled, matted with seaweed and sand. He had a wild look, and he made a slurping sound as he charged in.

entries.name: Cursed Waters
entries: The Llana'Shi Empire is no stranger to the dark tales of vampires. Vampirism has been among laneshi for ages, despite the protection of the sea. With more laneshi visiting lands above the waves, the curse has spread further. Old legends among laneshi speak of warriors falling under the curse for misdeeds, or of mystics transformed due to missteps or intentional arcane experiments.

entries.name: Blood Drinkers
entries: More than other vampires, laneshi vampires prefer to drink their sustenance. Their feeding method leaves victims who survive parched. This connection to water gives a laneshi vampire some benefits. Running water never bothers laneshi vampires, and {@item Holy Water|XPHB} is less effective against them. The downside to these advantages is that laneshi vampires can't survive without immersion in water.

entries.name: Laneshi Vampire Customization
entries: Laneshi vampires retain the swim speed of their living kin, and the undead state enhances their {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}. Vampire blood brings out the long laneshi tradition of hit-and-run fighting styles in the Skirmisher trait. Running water doesn't harm a laneshi vampire, and they have resistance to the Radiant damage {@item Holy Water|XPHB} deals. A laneshi's bite drains moisture—see the Bite attack—and the vampire must regularly immerse in water or feed to stave off deadly dehydration. See the Water Reliance trait.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who consumes part of a laneshi vampire can breathe water for 1 hour, in addition to other benefits and drawbacks.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Laneshi vampires prefer to drink their sustenance and can rarely resist consuming blood if they see or smell it.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Vampirism makes laneshi agile fighters who move easily in and out of combat. They retain water-related advantages, including not only swimming, but also no weakness to running water other vampires have and a resistance to {@item Holy Water|XPHB}. A laneshi's bite leaves a victim parched.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A laneshi vampire can die if unable to immerse in water or feed. The vampire's body disintegrates if it dies in this way.

items.name: Massive
entries: The vampire is considered to be one size larger when determining what can grapple it, as well as its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

items.name: Charm {@recharge 5}
entries: The vampire casts {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}), and the duration is 24 hours. The vampire can also target Beasts with this spell. The {@condition Charmed|XPHB} target is a willing recipient of the vampire's Bite, the damage of which doesn't end the spell. When the spell ends, the target is unaware it was {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the vampire.

The massive creature filled the room, its face just visible amid folds of noxious flesh. Then it smiled. It was a brilliant smile, with just a hint of malice. And when it spoke, it offered secrets, but at what cost?

entries.name: Gluttony Scions
entries: An ogresh feels a natural desire to settle into an area that can support their immense appetite. The curse of vampirism enhances this desire to monstrous proportions. An ogresh vampire risks consuming everything around them, leaving a region barren for years to come. They grow large and corpulent. If left to their own devices, they can become so large that standard buildings can no longer accommodate them. Still, their movement isn't impeded, and so witnessing an ogresh vampire charging is memorable and terrifying.

entries.name: Vicious Feeders
entries: An ogresh vampire relishes consumption, especially consuming a sapient creature. Other vampires prefer to feast on blood, but an ogresh vampire prefers flesh, bone, and marrow.

entries.name: Deviant Socialite
entries: Ogresh set down deep social roots as they age, and those rare few that contract vampirism are no different. They work a complex series of deals and trades, ranging from goods to secrets and everything in between. However, their longevity, combined with the lengthy maturation period as a vampire, leads them to appear youthful for many more decades than normal. This appearance can cause others to underestimate an ogresh vampire at inopportune moments.

entries.name: Grandiose Plans
entries: Nothing about an ogresh vampire is small. They plan extensively, with backup plans, and backup plans for those backup plans.

entries.name: Ogresh Vampire Customization
entries: An ogresh vampire is agile for their mass, but less so than a typical vampire of their age (lower Dexterity and AC). The vampire makes up for the slowdown with sheer durability (higher Constitution and hit points) and higher Charisma. An ogresh vampire also gains its proficiency bonus on Constitution saving throws but lacks it on Dexterity saves. These vampires are immune to disease and Poison, and they can't be {@condition Charmed|XPHB}. However, an ogresh vampire can use Charm on others but lacks Beast Form. Ancient ogresh vampires can affect any sort of creature with their Charm, not only humanoids or beasts. Ogresh vampires gain the Massive trait in their later years.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Ogresh vampires are likely to hide treasure in their folds of flesh. They also have a specialized bile that can be harvested. Someone who has proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill can siphon this bile with a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check and 10 minutes of work. Doing so successfully produces five doses of the bile. In its raw form, with 1 minute of application time, the bile masks the scent of a creature, meaning other creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on smell to detect the creature coated in bile.

This bile also masks poisons in a similar fashion. A creature that tries to detect the Poison with smell has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the check to do so. If mixed with an ingested Poison and consumed, this bile has the effect of any consumed vampire part.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: An ogresh's natural charm lends itself well to the curse of vampirism. Planning, coercion, bribes, and gluttony come easily to them.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Vampirism makes a creature more of what they are, and an ogresh is rarely interested in small or short-term thoughts. An ogresh vampire grows larger than their mortal kin. And a beast form like that of other vampires is beneath a creature who places importance on reason and charm.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: An ogresh vampire can grow so large that they seem too big for their home. This appearance is deceptive. The vampire might be slightly less nimble, but it is as or more dangerous than other vampires. And the vampire can move about its home in mist form.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The alchemical berserker makes three Longsword attacks.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Battle Draught (3/Day)
entries: The alchemical berserker consumes an unstable chemical compound. For the next minute, the berserker gains two of the following abilities: {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to spell damage; {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; 20 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}; or 4 ({@damage 1d8}) extra damage with weapon attacks. Choosing the same ability twice can extend the draught's duration, but has no other effect.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d10 + 2}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Battle Draught (1/Day)
entries: The marauder consumes an unstable chemical compound. For the next minute, the marauder gains one of the following abilities: {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to spell damage; {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; or 2 ({@damage 1d4}) extra damage with weapon attacks.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The amorphous horror can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The amorphous horror makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
