headerEntries: The Tormach zealot casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

action.name: Whip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 10 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Slashing damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it is pushed 5 feet or has the Prone condition (zealot's choice).

bonus.name: Blood-Soaked Inspiration
entries: After dealing damage, the Tormach zealot chooses one creature within 60 feet that can see and hear it. The target can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the result to one {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the end of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Tormach cultist uses Frightening Scream and makes two Handaxe attacks.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Frightening Scream
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 10}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the cultist that can hear it. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the cultist's next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the Frightening Scream of all Tormach cultists for 24 hours.

bonus.name: Rampage
entries: When the Tormach cultist reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a melee attack, it can move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make a melee attack.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The champion of Tormach casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

spellcasting.name: Hunter's Mark (2/Day)
headerEntries: The champion of Tormach casts {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (1/Day)
headerEntries: The champion of Tormach casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Protection Aura
entries: The champion of Tormach emits a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of protection. While the champion doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, each creature of the champion's choice in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} gains a +2 bonus to saving throws. A creature can benefit from only one such aura at a time.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The champion of Tormach makes two Battleaxe attacks.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) Slashing damage.

reaction.name: Smite
entries: When the champion of Tormach hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, it can expend a spell from its Spellcasting. The spell has no effect, and the attack deals an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Necrotic or Radiant damage.

name: Chiropteran Behemoth
languages: understands one language but can't speak

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The behemoth doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} while it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The behemoth gains 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of its turn. If the behemoth is exposed to an Undoing Elixir, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. The behemoth dies only if it starts its turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and doesn't regenerate.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
entries: If the chiropteran behemoth fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The behemoth has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Potent Weapons
entries: The behemoth's attacks ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The behemoth makes a Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 5 ft. {@h}33 ({@damage 6d8 + 6}) Force damage. If the behemoth has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, it deals an extra 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 10 ft. {@h}20 ({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Force damage. {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}: 48 ({@damage 12d6 + 6}) Force damage, and if the target dies, its head or another vital body part is severed or destroyed. If the behemoth moved at least 20 feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Shriek {@recharge}
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 19}, each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 45 ({@damage 7d12}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

bonus.name: Darkness Aura
entries: The behemoth creates magical darkness in a 40-foot radius {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} until the start of its next turn. A creature with {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} can't see through this darkness and nonmagical light can't illuminate it. A light-producing spell of level 5 or lower is dispelled if its area overlaps the darkness's area.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The chiropteran behemoth makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Claw
entries: The behemoth makes a Claw attack.

legendary.name: Swoop
entries: The behemoth moves up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes a Claw attack. The behemoth can't use this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary.name: Wing Buffet
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20}, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the behemoth. {@actSaveFail} 20 ({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet away. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target also has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.{@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The behemoth flies up to half its {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|Flying Speed}, and can't use this action again until the start of its next turn.
They say the monster flies on silent wings in a shroud of darkness and can't be killed. But those who've seen it can't say anything anymore.

entries.name: Unkillable Legend
entries: Rumors of the chiropteran behemoth are just that. The batlike monster is said to be the size of a house, as silent as the breeze, and unkillable. The only verified account of a chiropteran behemoth describes one that serves Grand Duke Koshevek of Soma, lairing beneath the dome of the Vonsantra Cathedral. Sages posit that if one behemoth can be created, others can.

entries.name: Unstoppable Servant
entries: Chiropteran behemoths serve their creators with undying devotion, following orders to completion. The ritual creating a chiropteran behemoth allows the creator to know where its servant's location at all times. While its natural weapons are dangerous, its ear-splitting shriek is more so. The bat-monster can also unleash a sphere of darkness that doesn't hinder its senses.

entries.name: Undoing Elixir
entries: Unfortunately for the forces of good and light, the rumors of the chiropteran behemoth's immortality are true. The beast returns to life unless exposed to an elixir of rare components, including its own guano. Gaining access to this last ingredient is the challenge, made even greater if the behemoth's master knows its vulnerability.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: To make one dose of an Undoing Elixir that can render a chiropteran behemoth vulnerable to death, its guano must be mixed with other reagents worth 250 GP. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} must brew the mixture for 3 days. As a Magic action, someone can splash a dose onto a behemoth if it's within 5 feet or throw a vial of it up to 20 feet, the vial shattering on impact. In either case, the attacker makes a ranged attack against the behemoth, treating the vial as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the behemoth takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Radiant damage and its Regeneration temporarily ceases.

The chiropteran behemoth's two canines are good for making a {@item Rapier of Life Stealing|XDMG|Rapier} or {@item Shortsword of Life Stealing|XDMG}. Making the weapon requires someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} to work for 7 days and use materials worth 1,500 GP along with the two upper canines from the behemoth. Somebody must cast {@spell Vampiric Touch|XPHB} on the fangs three times during the process.

Claws of a chiropteran behemoth can be used to make a unique {@item Vorpal Sword|XDMG}. Crafting the sword requires the remnants of the behemoth and other rare components worth 25,000 GP. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} must work with someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to create the weapon over 30 days. Somebody must also cast {@spell Power Word Kill|XPHB} on the weapon each day of its making.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A chiropteran behemoth serves Grand Duke Koshevek of Soma. This behemoth is the only one whose existence has been verified.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The ritual that created the chiropteran behemoth makes it regenerate even when it should die. However, any mortal magic can be undone. The behemoth's leavings—skin, fur, broken teeth, and guano—found in its lair need to be studied to learn the behemoth's weakness.

entries.name: {@dc 25} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: To create the elixir that can render the chiropteran behemoth vulnerable to death requires its guano—see Salvage.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The coldfire ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Coldfire
entries: Cold damage dealt by the coldfire ooze ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}, and treats {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} as {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} instead.

trait.name: Ignite
entries: A creature or flammable object that takes Cold damage from the coldfire ooze ignites. Until the target takes Fire damage, it takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage at the start of each of its turns.

trait.name: Illumination
entries: The coldfire ooze sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The coldfire ooze can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Coldfire Flare {@recharge}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.{@actSaveSuccessOrFail} If a significant amount of flammable material is in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, the area ignites, dealing 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage to creatures and objects that enter the area for the first time on a turn or end their turn there. A target that takes Cold damage from the area is subjected to Ignite.

reaction.name: Split
entries: {@actTrigger} The coldfire ooze is Medium or Large, has 10+ {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and takes Cold and Slashing damage. {@actResponse} The coldfire ooze splits into two new coldfire oozes. Each new ooze has {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the original ooze's, rounded down. New oozes are one size smaller than the original ooze.
Coldfire's a menace, sure, but at least it doesn't move around on its own. Why are you staring at me like that?

entries.name: Spreading Corruption
entries: Coldfire oozes spread coldfire throughout the north. Corrupted slurries of ice and snow, coldfire oozes have become a menace to frontier towns among the Valikan Clans.

entries.name: Burning Slime
entries: Those who first faced coldfire oozes didn't realize how the slimes could split. This mistake in the first skirmishes allowed the oozes to further multiply. Now, they can be found all over the northern wilds.

entries.name: Ooze Nature
entries: A coldfire ooze doesn't require sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can use the remains of one coldfire ooze to make one {@item Flammable Tincture|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Making the tincture takes 1 day of work, materials worth 50 GP, and a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Coldfire oozes are rare creatures that spread coldfire.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: As with coldfire, fire is the best way to deal with a coldfire ooze. Fire is the only way to put the coldfire out.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The coral grazer can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The coral grazer deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Unnatural Presence
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the coral grazer and can sense it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave wis} {@dc 17}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the coral grazer's next turn. {@actSaveFailBy 5} While {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the Unnatural Presence of all coral grazers for 24 hours.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The coral grazer makes three Bite attacks and uses Horrid Gaze.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 15 ft. {@h}24 ({@damage 4d8 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Horrid Gaze
entries: The coral grazer fixes its eye on one creature it can see within 120 feet. The creature is subjected to the coral grazer's Unnatural Presence.
I used to live in a village in the western shallows. Then a grazer came by and, in one night, everything I knew was gone.

entries.name: Unnatural Disasters
entries: Sea- and coast-dwellers fear coral grazers. Many such people consider the arrival of a coral grazer to be a natural disaster, but these monsters are far from natural. Equipped with beaked tentacles surrounding its single massive eye, a coral grazer uses its beaks to tear apart and consume coral. But the creature doesn't restrict itself to coral shelfs—it eats anything made of a similar substance, from shells to some stone. It also consumes bones, although in smaller quantities. One coral grazer can lay waste to a whole fishing village.

entries.name: Ancient Horrors
entries: Accounts of coral grazers can be found throughout recorded history, yet their origins re main a mystery. The oldest legends tell of a cataclysm that precedes the creatures being seen in the shallows. Sages speculate this disaster either gave rise to coral grazers or forced them into new territory. The look of coral grazers is akin that of Aether Kindred and denizens of their mad realm. If the cataclysm that gave rise to coral grazers had its source there, it could explain much.

entries.name: Progeny Plague
entries: Coral grazer spawn can be as much of a threat as their elder kin. Larvae are up to 6 feet long and they eat tremendous amounts to fuel their growth. After gorging themselves for a year, they retreat to deeper waters, returning to familiar feeding territory when they have reached full size. Most folk prefer to kill the larvae before they can grow.

An adult coral grazer can attract several larvae to its feeding area. That means adults are more dangerous when larvae are about in surrounding waters. Sages have noted that larvae are more likely to show up when an adult is in danger.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Some artisans prize a coral grazer's beaks, which can make fine, sharp, and unusual blades. The beaks from one larva can fetch 50 GP, and those from an adult up to 200 GP.

Someone who has proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill can extract an adult coral grazer's eye in perfect condition with a successful {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check. Treated three times with a {@spell Flesh to Stone|XPHB} spell and special oils worth 1,000 GP per casting, the eye shrinks and works like a {@item Crystal Ball|XDMG}, provided the caster makes a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check with each casting.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Coral grazers are dangerous tentacled beasts that tear apart coral and similar material for food.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: An adult coral grazer's presence can cause paralyzing fear. Although the grazer eats little flesh, it often takes a chunk of a paralyzed creature to get to its delicious bones. The adult can also attract larvae in the area to join it in feasting and fighting.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: While a coral grazer is at home in the coastal waters of the lands of Etharis, they can be captured and trained by evil-doers to acts as guards and thugs. Little is as terrifying as a moated lair of an enemy that is also full of coral grazers. In fact, some coral grazers have been gifted with the power of magical flight, making them extremely effective and dangerous hunters, even out of water.

The paralyzing fright caused by a coral grazer makes them terribly dangerous against those creatures who fail their saving throws. However, higher-level characters who are immune to fear, or who boost others with a fear-negating ability, make this paralyzing fright irrelevant. That's why it's important, when you want to challenge a powerful party, to take down those characters or separate them from their allies during a coral grazer attack. A {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} to remove the effects of a {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB} is also strategically beneficial.

trait.name: Hold Breath
entries: Out of water, the coral grazer larva can hold its breath for 30 minutes.

trait.name: Water Breathing
entries: The coral grazer larva can breathe only underwater.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The coral grazer larva makes two Bite attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage.

trait.name: Corpse Bound
entries: A corpse wisp can't stray more than 300 feet from the remains that spawned it.

trait.name: Dead Light
entries: The corpse wisp sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The corpse wisp can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

action.name: Tendril
entries: {@atkr ms} {@hit 7}, reach 15 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d8)}) Necrotic damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 12}). While grappled in this way, the target is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. A creature that starts its turn {@condition Grappled|XPHB} takes 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Cold damage.
Some crypts are lit by lanterns. Others by the fragments of lost souls.

entries.name: Soul Remnants
entries: Sometimes a soul stays in the mortal world to haunt the living. More often, wicked spiritual remnants stay behind to haunt the body's final rest. These remnants form weird, dead lights—corpse wisps—that float in graveyards and other places of death, searching for the living to feed on.
These fragments have little sense of the creatures they once were. Still, they cling to the body they once inhabited. Hunger can't destroy them, but they crave life force.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A corpse wisp doesn't require air, drink, food, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When a corpse wisp is destroyed, it leaves behind a soft, black rock the size of a coin. This "coal" can be used as an extra material component when casting a spell that deals Necrotic damage. Used in this manner, the coal causes the spell to deal an extra {@dice 1d4} Necrotic damage. Using the coal in this way consumes it

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: These lights, called corpse wisps, are undead spirit fragments caught between life and the great beyond.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Corpse wisps are nearly immaterial. Radiant damage is most effective against them, while Poison, Necrotic, and damage from nonmagical attacks are least effective.

trait.name: Adamantine Jaws
entries: The corpsejaw's Bite attack is considered adamantine, scoring a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage. {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}: If the target is wearing nonmagical armor, the armor takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers. Armor reduced to an AC of 10 is destroyed.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the corpsejaw moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and the corpsejaw can make a Bite attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

Cousins to mountain lions, corpsejaws are battlefield scavengers. Their powerful jaws allow them to tear through most armor, so they can eat carrion other scavengers leave behind. Military organizations such as the Free Swords issue bounties on corpsejaws to prevent damage to valuable salvage.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The eye crawler can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

An eye crawler is an ambulatory eye that observes everything. It might be spying for something else. An eye crawler has no effective attacks. Mages theorize eye crawlers derive sustenance from light or ambient magical energy.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The eye crow can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a person whispering, a baby crying, or an animal chittering. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The eye crow has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the crow's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Beak
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Piercing damage. {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}: The target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of the eye crow's next turn.

entries.name: Popular Birds
entries: Eye crows are big corvids plentiful throughout Etharis. They mimic sounds and voices, and they're extremely clever, remembering faces, locations, and how other creatures treat them. People keep eye crows as pets and often use their iridescent black feathers, which have a deep-green sheen, to decorate.

entries.name: Eye Eaters
entries: Eye crows have a strong inclination to eat eyes, especially those of Humanoids. A murder of these birds is bold enough to attack a person directly. They coordinate and communicate noisily as they chase prey.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The nest of an eye crow contains glittering baubles, coins, gems, or jewelry worth at least 5 GP. Feathers of one eye crow can fetch a similar amount of money.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Eye crows can be tamed and trained for simple tasks. Unscrupulous trainers teach the crow to attack others, going for the eyes.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Eye crows are a wonderful tool for GMs to deliver cryptic messages or clues to the characters, even as they are trying to peck out the eyes of the heroes. They make wonderful, creepy additions to encounters.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The beetle deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage.
Massive grazing beetles, flatbacks have thick armor. A flatback beetle's dorsal side can accommodate several creatures and can support a howdah.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: For areas of Etharis that you want to make seem creepy or different, you can turn flatback beetles into beasts of burden or plow animals. For example, some backwater hamlet in Soma might breed these monstrous insects specifically and think nothing of it.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Piercing damage plus 1 Cold damage. If the target is a creature and takes Cold damage, it can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Rare Hunter
entries: Wild frostbite foxes live in packs in Grarjord. They change with the seasons, fur turning white in the winter and brown in the spring. What doesn't change is the fox's weird ability to deliver a jolt of cold with its bite.

entries.name: Clan Culture
entries: These foxes are an important part of the Valikan clan culture. Their furs help the people of the North survive harsh winters, and the clans are careful not to overhunt the species.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} can create {@item Clothing, cold weather|IDRotF|cold-weather clothing} from the pelts of five frostbite foxes. Doing so takes 8 hours of work.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The chilled fangs of a frostbite fox can overwhelm the senses.

trait.name: Glowing Mane
entries: The goldmane boar sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot Radius.

trait.name: Relentless (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: If the goldmane boar take 11 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

action.name: Tusk
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the goldmane boar moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Slashing damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Staple of Etharis
entries: Boars are a central part of everyday life in Etharis. Domesticated or hunted in the wild, they are a centerpiece in feasts. A wise adventurer keeps an eye out for particularly aggressive boars, acknowledging their danger and the potential of a filling meal.

entries.name: Rare Beast
entries: Occasionally, a hunter glimpses a goldmane boar. These animals avoid humanoid contact. Cleverer than a regular boar, a goldmane boar can be detected easier at night when its mane glows softly in the dark. Killing a goldmane boar is considered bad luck.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The glowing bristles from a goldmane boar can be harvested. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB} can braid the bristles into a {@item Gold Boar Ring|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Doing so takes 8 hours of work, other materials worth 20 GP, and a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Goldmane boars can be tamed and used as mounts.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The jelly can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 1}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Acid damage.
Jellies are the cast-off portions of oozes. They can be dangerous, but they primarily scavenge for food.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The knifewing doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Glider
entries: The knifewing can't ascend while flying and its altitude decreases by 5 feet for every 30 feet it flies. If flying, the knifewing falls if it doesn't fly at least 30 feet during its turn.

action.name: Knifewing (Flying Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.
A knifewing is a gliding lizard about the size of a small dog. Its gliding flaps have hard edges that are sharp while stretched taut when the lizard glides.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The skin of a knifewing is prized for making a {@item Knifewing Cape|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}.

trait.name: Regrowth
entries: When the mold spider is killed by damage other than Fire damage, it releases spores that grow a new mold spider in 3 days.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The mold spider can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Slashing damage.
Mold spiders are twisted bits of plant matter that forage in dark caves and ruins for rotting matter to settle on and "eat."

trait.name: Hold Breath
entries: The ormwurm can hold its breath for 30 minutes.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Piercing damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). Until this grapple ends, the ormwurm can't Bite another target.

entries.name: Burrowing Carnivores
entries: Ormwurms are big lizards with red, green, or tan scaly skin, a serpentine body, and two strong arms. They slither as they move, using their arms to help them climb. An ormwurm can sacrifice its tail to get away from a predator. The tail eventually grows back.
These burrowers live along riverbanks or on sandy beaches. They hunt larger animals, including cattle, and they eat carrion. An ormwurm pulls its prey underground to eat.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can use the skin and gizzard of one ormwurm, along with other reagents worth 25 GP, to create a {@item Potion of Acid Resistance|XDMG}. Doing so requires 4 hours of work and a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Some stories say that Gormadraug was an ormwurm that never stopped growing.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The scuttling maw can breathe air and water.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Pincers
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). Until this grapple ends, the scuttling maw can't use its Pincers on another target.

bonus.name: Gnash
entries: The scuttling maw makes a Bite attack against a creature it has {@condition Grappled|XPHB}.
Crablike scuttling maws patrol shorelines, searching for prey to devour. Their meat is a delicacy.

action.name: Ram
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage. If the shieldhead moves 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage and, if it is Large or smaller, has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
A shieldhead has a broad bone faceplate to protect itself and to ram foes. An expert rider can also use the bone like a shield. People have domesticated shieldheads for riding.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The sloth galloper makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Speed Burst
entries: The sloth galloper takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. It can't move across {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} using this movement.
A sloth galloper is a hybrid sloth-ape that is an agile climber and fast sprinter. The beast's four apelike hands are sensitive, so it hesitates to move rapidly over rough terrain.

trait.name: Eat Fire
entries: When the torcheater flies through fire, it reduces the fire's area by a 5-foot cube. A fire goes out if its area is reduced to nothing.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Fire damage.
Torcheaters are small batlike creatures that feed on fire, swooping down to douse torches and campfires.

name: Crawling Grave
languages: understands all languages it knew in life but can't speak

trait.name: Lethal Overrun
entries: If the crawling grave enters the space of a creature that is dead or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, it picks up the creature. The creature moves with the crawling grave , has a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0 that cannot be increased, and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}. A creature that loses the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition or is revived stops moving with the crawling grave. A creature within 5 feet of the crawling grave can take an action to pull a creature or corpse free of the crawling grave with a successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

At the end of the crawling grave's second turn after picking up a corpse, the corpse breaks apart and the crawling grave regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half that corpse's former {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum or 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, whichever is fewer. The crawling grave expels anything the corpse was wearing or carrying.

trait.name: Swarmlike
entries: The crawling grave can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the crawling grave can move through any opening large enough for a Small creature.

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the crawling grave to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. {@actSaveSuccess} The crawling grave drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The crawling grave makes two Slam attacks

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d10 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the crawling grave is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, it deals 8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage and doesn't impose the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
This thing was born from a mass grave? Makes you wonder who the real monster is, doesn't it?

entries.name: Undead Victims
entries: Unspeakable violence leads to the creation of mass graves, where the dead lie lost and forgotten. The energy from this cruelty can coalesce into tangles of bones that rise to seek out and add new skeletons to the hideous mass.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A crawling grave doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can use powdered bones from a destroyed crawling grave to brew a death-defying potion. If a creature drinks the potion, the first time they would drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} within 8 hours after drinking they instead drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}. Brewing the potion takes 2 days and materials worth 50 GP, and brewing it correctly requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. One crawling grave has enough bones to refine into four doses of this potion.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Tales tell of mass graves that spawn massive undead due to the violent energy that surrounds them.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A crawling grave can absorb a corpse and add the bones to its mass.

name: Withered Steed
languages: understands one language its creator speaks but can't speak

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The withered steed can't shape-shift.

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage.
Against the lightning, a tan horse dripping tattered flesh rears, its antlers and empty skull reflecting the light. Saddleless, it lowers its head to pull its master onto its back.

entries.name: Rider-Bonded
entries: Thought to have originated in Grarjord, the withered steed is a rare sight due to the difficulty of creating one. Withered steeds are the most loyal of all the summoned and created steeds in Etharis, living only as long as their creator.

entries.name: Ritual Creation
entries: To create a withered steed, a spellcaster must have at least one 4th-level spell slot and materials worth 5,000 GP, which the ritual consumes. The ritualist must remove and consume a living horse's heart under a full moon. In its place, a living raven encaged in tree roots must be inserted. The body must be buried with its head removed and a stag skull in its place. The creator pours 1 pint of their own blood over the body and places a rope necklace inscribed with runes of summoning magic placed around the corpse's throat. The ritual takes 6 hours. By the new moon, the withered steed frees itself from its grave.

entries.name: Constructed Nature
entries: A withered steed doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When a withered steed dies, it becomes a mass of gore with a deer skull and a cage containing an undead raven. If someone frees the raven and cares for it for 10 days, it becomes bound to that person who can then summon it with a {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell, provided the keeper is able to cast that spell by some means. This undead raven has the Immutable Form trait, and the damage and condition immunities of a withered steed.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A withered steed is a construct with related {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The steed's form can't be changed. If its master is slain, the steed is instantly destroyed.

name: Ghost Mustang
languages: understands one language its creator speaks but can't speak

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the ghost mustang to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a success, the ghost mustang drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage.
The faint stench of death surrounds a translucent horse, a pale glow shining where its eyes should be. An ornate saddle jingles as it stomps in place.

entries.name: Necromancer Steeds
entries: Ghost mustangs are the favored mounts of necromancers, who often create these horses as an early experiment in mastering the arts of undeath. While loyal to their creator, a ghost mustang avoids the afterlife and endangers itself only if ordered to do so.

entries.name: Ritual Creation
entries: Ghost mustangs are ectoplasmic manifestations of wild horses that died of unnatural means. A spellcaster with at least one 4th-level spell slot can enact this ritual, using materials worth 5,500 GP, which the ritual consumes. A wizard of the school of necromancy must instead be 5th level. In a ritual performed at night, the creator creates a magic circle around the slain horse and places a drop of the creator's blood in each eye. The creator then incants for 6 hours. The body disappears during the ritual, and the ghost mustang appears to serve the creator 13 days later.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A ghost mustang doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The ghost mustang disappears when it dies, leaving behind puddles of ectoplasm. This substance can be used to brew a {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG} when combined with a hair from the creator's head and materials worth 100 GP. This process requires proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check, and 8 hours of work.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A ghost mustang is Undead, made of corporeal ectoplasm. It has related {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and is hard to kill.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A ghost mustang has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage, and that type of damage can keep the steed from surviving a killing blow

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Medium or smaller.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Fire damage.
This fanged horse with scaly red skin stretched across its frame has cloven hooves dripping with dark oil. Embedded chains hold a black saddle to its back.

entries.name: Infernal Mounts
entries: Created in the Netherworld, these steeds come into existence when a contract for a {@optfeature Gift of Liberating Freedom|GrimHollowPG24} is signed. Like most fiends, the crimson stallion can be summoned by learning its true name. These true names are often revealed in dreams to worthy owners, usually as rewards to fiends or mortals who have sent many souls to hell. Crimson stallions are reluctantly bound into service and fulfill their contracts, but rarely bond with their creators.

entries.name: Ritual
entries: Once a true name is discovered, a spellcaster with at least one 4 spell slot can summon a crimson stallion in a {@spell Magic Circle|XPHB} drawn using the summoner's blood and materials worth 5,000 GP, which the ritual consumes. The bond is completed when the summoner attaches a bridle made of humanoid sinew and chains to the fiend.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A crimson stallion ignites upon death, burning the body to ash within seconds, leaving only the hooves. Each of these can be ground into a powder and used to create a {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}. Doing so requires proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence check, and 2 hours of work per vial.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A crimson stallion is a fiend that has related {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A crimson stallion's bite and hoof attacks are fiery.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The daemon oak deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The daemon oak makes two attacks, using Lash or Rock in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Spew.

action.name: Lash
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 5d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 18}). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The daemon oak can grapple four creatures at a time.

action.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 10}, range 60/180 ft. {@h}32 ({@damage 4d12 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Spew {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Acid damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Tree Thrall (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The daemon oak curses and animates one tree within 30 feet. The tree becomes a {@creature Daemon Oak Thrall|GrimHollowMG24}. This thrall is the daemon oak's ally, and it takes its turn just after the daemon oak. The thrall obeys the daemon oak's verbal commands (no action required for the daemon oak). If issued no commands, the thrall attacks a creature that isn't the thrall's ally. A thrall dies after 24 hours, when the daemon oak uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to sever the connection to the thrall, the thrall is more than 1 mile from the daemon oak, or the daemon oak dies.

reaction.name: Chain
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 10 feet of the daemon oak starts to move. {@actResponse} The daemon oak makes a Lash attack against the triggering creature.
Twisted and tortured, the many faces of this walking, dark-barked oak scream and call as the creature moves through the forest, spreading destruction.

entries.name: Twisted Treants
entries: Where daemon blood and ichor fall, feindish power ruins the ground. Plant life becomes desiccated and twisted, most falling to rot. But the hardiest plants become warped mockeries of their verdant kin. Among these are {@creature treant|MM|treants} who become daemon oaks, which have elongated, lashing limbs and grasping roots, all bound in infernal chains.

Like a host of tormented souls attempting to free themselves from a woody prison, a multitude of faces manifest along the trunk of these animate trees. Some of these faces have a fixed place. Others emerge and then fade into the daemon oak's despoiled bark.

entries.name: Thrall Spawners
entries: Daemon oaks can cause other trees to share their corruption. Instead of awakening trees, daemon oaks can replace wood and sap with acidic ichor. Once corrupted, a tree serves the daemon oak, amplifying the daemonic tree's menace until the thrall is destroyed. Then, it explodes into a shower of acid.

entries.name: Unrelenting Destroyers
entries: Daemon oaks are sedentary creatures, drawing their nutrients from corrupted soil. They might stand for decades, wailing in some gloomy corner of deep woods, avoided by animals and sane folk alike. But when roused to action, they rarely stop their rampage until forced to do so.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Daemon oak ichor is a powerful if unstable reagent. Harvesting one vial from a daemon oak requires a successful {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check. One vial of ichor harvested from a daemon oak can fetch 500 GP from the right buyer.

Someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} can use the chains from one daemon oak to fashion a {@item Chain Shirt of Acid Resistance|XDMG|Chain Shirt of Resistance (Acid)} or {@item Chain Mail of Acid Resistance|XDMG|Chain Mail of Resistance (Acid)}. These armors also offer a +1 bonus to AC. Instead, the chains can be used to make a {@item +1 Acid Fighting Chain|GrimHollowMG24|magic chain weapon} {@homebrew |(see Grim Hollow Player's Guide)}. Such a weapon offers a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, and when the wielder hits with an attack using such a weapon, it deals {@damage 1d6} extra Acid damage. Each of these rare items requires 10 days and additional materials worth 1,000 GP to make.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Fell forces twisted this walking tree. It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A daemon oak can turn other trees into thralls. Each servant is nearly as powerful as its master, although far less cunning. A daemon oak thrall can't spit acid like its master, and thralls perish if their master dies. When a thrall dies, it cracks apart, showering acidic ichor over an area within 10 feet of the thrall.

name: Daemon Oak Thrall
languages: understands Infernal and Sylvan but can't speak
cr: — with a daemon oak (3 [700] by itself)

trait.name: Caustic Demise
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the thrall when it dies. {@actSaveFail} 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Acid damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The daemon oak thrall deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Parasitic Release
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the danxoni when it dies. The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} spreads around corners. {@actSaveFail} The target is infected with {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The danxoni makes four Claws attacks and one Bite attack.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d6 + 5}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) Piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Acid damage.

action.name: Symbiont Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Acid damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Piercing damage and 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Poison damage. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target is infected with {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

It's a blessing that danxoni—strange, elongated, multiarmed monstrosities—are a rare sight. Not only are they prone to violence, but if they were to proliferate any faster, their voracious appetites would quickly strip an area of its natural resources.

entries.name: Churning Innards
entries: The warm moistness of a danxoni's digestive tract is an ideal habitat for insects, fungi, and other tiny organisms. The relationship is symbiotic. The smaller creatures flourish in a secure environment with ready access to nourishment, and the digestion they do helps the danxoni absorb its varied meals.

entries.name: Multitude of Hungers
entries: Danxoni observed in the wild have been recorded as eating anything. They eat fresh prey, carrion, wood, poisonous plants, and rock and metal. To eat, a danxoni rips chunks with its strong arms and stuffs the material down its throat. The digestive powers of a danxoni's hitchhikers allow it to extract sustenance out of any substance.

entries.name: Once Sapient?
entries: Some observant adventurers have noted the oddly humanlike appearance of a danxoni's face. All attempts to communicate with a danxoni have confirmed an animal intelligence, leading some to wonder whether danxoni were once a sapient species.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} can process portions of a dead danxoni's internal colonies to produce {@item Antitoxin|XPHB} or an herbal cure for {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}. Doing so requires 1 hour of work and a successful {@dc 11} Intelligence or Wisdom check. One danxoni can provide enough material for four doses of {@item Antitoxin|XPHB} or herbal cure, or a mix of both.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}):
entries: Danxoni can exhale their internal symbionts in a caustic, poisonous, and infectious cloud. Killing a danxoni releases these disease-causing parasites. If harvested properly, however, these creatures can be used to make {@item Antitoxin|XPHB} or a cure for {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Necrotic damage can quickly wipe out large numbers of the danxoni's internal symbionts, so this damage is very effective against a danxoni.

trait.name: Camouflage
entries: The dark mist stalker can {@action Hide|XPHB} while {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB} by foliage, heavy rain, mist, or other natural phenomena. If it misses with a ranged attack while it has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, it does not lose that condition.

trait.name: Dead Eye
entries: The dark mist stalker's attacks with Ranged weapons ignore {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} and {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three Quarters Cover}, and score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

trait.name: Hunter's Stride
entries: The dark mist stalker ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

trait.name: Night Stalker
entries: The dark mist stalker treats {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} within the range of its {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} as {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dark mist stalker makes three attacks, using Skinning Knife or Hunting Bow in any combination.

action.name: Skinning Knife
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) sSlashing damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 16}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowPG24} condition.

action.name: Hunting Bow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 150/600 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) Piercing damage, and the target is pushed 10 feet straight away from the dark mist stalker

action.name: Aim
entries: The dark mist stalker chooses a creature it can see and maintains {@status Concentration|XPHB}. While doing so, creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the dark mist stalker. If the dark mist stalker is still maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} when it makes its next Hunting Bow attack against the target, the attack has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} and deals an extra 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Skirmisher
entries: {@actTrigger} A Hostile creature moves within 5 feet of the dark mist stalker. {@actResponse} The dark mist stalker makes a Skinning Knife attack against the triggering creature, then moves up to 20 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

As we made camp the mist rolled in. Lassiter screamed, but we didn't see anything. Then another scream. And an arrow. Then another. No twang of a bow, just the sharp sound of impact. A full retreat was ordered and we all ran for our lives. At least the three of us who weren't dead.

entries.name: Trespassers Beware
entries: In places where the fey courts claim dominance in the mortal world, guards were placed to keep out trespassers. Then the Mists came. The noble fey guards were turned into dark versions of their past selves. They no longer serve their fey patrons—instead, they kill any interlopers.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The hunting bows of the dark mist stalkers are renowned for their accuracy and ranges so much so that foolish adventurers and hunters of all skill levels attempt to recover them. A slain dark mist stalker has a {@chance 10|10% chance|Dark Mist Stalker Bow|The bow can be truend into an oathbow.|The bow cannot be turned into an oathbow.} to be carrying a weapon that can be turned into an {@item Oathbow|XDMG}. Such a weapon can be altered by a proficient weaponsmith, who must succeed on a {@dc 25} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check after spending 10 days and 7500 GP of components.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Dark mist stalkers hide in the woods and always come with the mist! Avoid the mists to avoid your death!

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Dark mist stalkers can hide in the rain and see you without light. Find another way to find them.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The bow shot of a stalker can knock you back, and the touch of their knives can cause a wound that can't be staunched.

trait.name: Sunlight Weakness
entries: While in sunlight, the darkfeather has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on D20 Tests.

action.name: Beak
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Poison damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} If this damage reduces the target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the target is stabilized and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 hour. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition.

bonus.name: Shadow Blend (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: While in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, the darkfeather has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, along with anything it is wearing or carrying. The condition lasts until the darkfeather attacks, is in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end it.

A figure moves silently through the city, well past midnight, a masked doctor treating those who have contracted the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. Those who look closer see a monster—and not a masked healer—walking the streets.

entries.name: Mimic of Healers
entries: Darkfeathers are monsters that mimic the appearance of the few who try to safely help victims of the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. Traditionally, these healers dress in long, feathered black robes with a beak-like mask to protect themselves from contracting the disease. A warped mixture of magic and disease transformed these healers, merging the mask and pestilence, into a humanoid creature with a bird-like skull.

entries.name: Deathbringer
entries: To some, darkfeathers might be a blessing. Within their skull are two poison glands and a proboscis to deliver the poison to sickened individuals. Victims of a darkfeather seem to improve for a couple of days after the creature's visit, giving the family and victim hope. But death comes quickly, and the darkfeather tracks its victims to drink the liquified remains.

entries.name: Shadow Lurker
entries: When confronted, the darkfeather retreats and blends into darkness. It avoids conflict unless cornered, and then fights with ferocity to escape. Accurate knowledge of this mimic is rare.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Glands within a darkfeather's skull can be harvested and processed into one dose of a {@item Necrotic Poison|GrimHollowMG24}, which acts as a {@item Potion of Poison|XDMG} that inflicts both Poison and Necrotic damage if invested. Harvesting and preparing the poison requires proficiency with a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, takes 4 hours, and requires a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence check.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A darkfeather is a venomous Monstrosity that has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A darkfeather can blend with the shadows and is averse to {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, especially sunlight.

trait.name: Light Sense
entries: The dawndrinker can sense any light source within 120 feet. This sense penetrates most barriers, but it is blocked by 3 feet of wood or dirt, 1 foot of stone, or 1 inch of metal.

trait.name: Radiant Absorption
entries: When the dawndrinker would take Radiant damage, it instead takes no damage and regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Radiant damage dealt.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dawndrinker makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of the dawndrinker's next turn.

bonus.name: Drink Light
entries: The dawndrinker drinks light, extinguishing nonmagical light sources within 30 feet. Magical lights in the area created by spells of level 3 or lower, or by creatures of {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB|CR} 7 or lower, are dimmed: {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} is reduced to {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}, and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} is extinguished. An extinguished magical light is dispelled, or suppressed for 1 minute if the light source is continuous.

The dawndrinker can extinguished stronger magical lights by succeeding on a Constitution check with a DC of 10 plus the spell's level or 5 plus the creature's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB|CR}, whichever is lower.

bonus.name: Shadow Cunning
entries: In {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, the dawndrinker can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Sometimes it's darkest after the dawn.

entries.name: Alien Gloom
entries: A dawndrinker is the fear of the dark incarnated in a leonine shape. But the creature's head is alien, with five orbs that act as eyes and no mouth or nose. Three protrusions around the trunk function as ears. These organs vibrate when the dawndrinker is agitated, sounding like the rumble of an earthquake.

entries.name: Thirsting {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}
entries: These creatures are thought to have emerged from the City Below. Others claim dawndrinkers came to this world to defend their summoners against the Arcanist Inquisition. Whatever the case, dawndrinkers leech light from the surroundings, feeding on it and growing stronger. In the presence of a dawndrinker, torches flicker and fail, the sun seems distant, and magical illuminations dim and go out.

entries.name: Midday Night
entries: When a dawndrinker makes its home, usually in a cave or dense thicket hidden from the sun, it slowly feeds on light in the area. The longer it feeds, the stronger it grows and the shorter the days seem near its lair. After a season, a dawndrinker can grow powerful enough create a small area where it appears the sun never rises.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Dawndrinkers have a special organ that stores and processes light the way that other creatures digest food. Most of the creature's body disintegrates after it dies, but this light stomach remains. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}, or an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} can prepare the stomach with other ingredients worth 25 GP. If the preparer succeeds on a {@dc 13} Wisdom or Intelligence check, the organ makes a tasty, sweet meal for up to four creatures. After partaking, a creature gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet for 24 hours, or extends their existing {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} range by 60 feet. All partakers also gain Blindsight to a range of 10 feet for the same duration.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A dawndrinker is a cunning predator that can easily hide and move in shadow. It greatly lessens and even extinguishes light sources.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A dawndrinker can sense light, its food, at a great distance. The monster has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire, absorbing some of its energy, and has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Radiant damage, which is a source of quick nourishment for the dawndrinker.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A dawndrinker's attacks can temporarily take away the victim's ability to perceive light.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While a death cap remains motionless and isn't possessing a creature, the cap is indistinguishable from an ordinary object.

action.name: Crush
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, and the death cap attaches to the target. While attached, the death cap can't attack creatures other than the target, but it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls. The death cap's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0, it can't benefit from any bonus to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and it moves with the target.
A creature can take an action to remove the attached death cap with a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. The death cap can detach itself using 5 feet of movement.

action.name: Possession
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 14}, one creature the death cap is touching. {@actSaveFail} The target is possessed by the death cap. The death cap attaches to the target, as with its Crush attack, and the target loses control of its body. The death cap retains its mental ability scores, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and senses, but otherwise uses the target's statistics, gaining access to the target's knowledge, class features, proficiencies, and languages. The death cap can possess one target at a time and can't use its Crush attack while possessing a target.

The possessed target deals one extra die of damage with melee weapons. At the start of its turn, the death cap can grant the target {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls until the start of its next turn. Attack rolls against the target have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} for the same duration.

A creature can detach the death cap only if the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, or {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions. The attempt provokes an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} from the target. If the death cap is detached, the possession ends.

Every 24 hours, the death cap drains one of the target's {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, which it regains only after the possession ends. If the target has no {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, it dies. After losing a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} in this way, the target can repeat the save, ending the possession on a success. The possession also ends if the target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the death cap is turned, or the death cap ends the possession as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When the possession ends, the death cap falls to the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet and the target is immune to the death cap's Possession for 24 hours.

variant.name: Other Slayers
entries: While a cap appears to be the favored form of these horrid creatures, stories abound about other forms, from cloaks that seem more patient than the cap form to gauntlets or even weapons, more interested in political power than pure slaughter. These different types of death caps keep their host around for extended periods, sometimes even years, which means the death cap either doesn't feed on the host or keeps them alive with some form of necromancy.
Some necromancers and priests educated in the dark arts either scoff at such tales or warn that the cap form might be a lesser form of this item-haunting undead.
It draped over her head, and everything changed. That insecure bard we all knew and loved was gone. She sliced through us as if we were butter.

entries.name: Deadly Spirit
entries: The death cap is the manifestation of an executioner's or assassin's spirit, who not only killed without remorse, but hungered for murder. Their spirit and dark hunger live on after death, coalescing into some form of a cap or a hat.

entries.name: Patiently Waiting Release
entries: These caps are slow movers—landbound slitherers. It spends most of its time patiently waiting for prey, seeming nothing more than a clean but discarded item of clothing made of a lush material. It doesn't reveal its true nature until someone dons the hat.

entries.name: Psychic Hijacker
entries: Once upon a living creature's head, the transformation begins as the hood attempts to control the mind of its host. When it does, it stretches into a deep black hood, and that's when the carnage begins.

entries.name: Parasitic Killer
entries: The cap wants nothing more than to slake its murderous desires. While it can be cunning, it rarely passes on an opportunity to kill. It kills its host by pushing it into battle and psychically draining the host's life force.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A death cap doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The fabric of a defeated death cap is very valuable to tailors and creators of magical clothing, fetching 250 GP. Creating a magical cloak, hat, or other clothing using the fabric from a death cap cuts the creation time in half.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Placing the death cap on one's head opens one up to possession by the malignant undead. Once a death cap takes control, it pushes its host to murderous carnage. While one can cut down the host, the easiest way to rid a possessed creature of the cap is to Turn Undead.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The death cap rides roughshod over its host, not only pushing it into battle but also denying it sustenance and sleep. Worst still, it slowly devours those it possesses. The cap can be forced off a host's body by using {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB} or similar magic.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The ooze can breathe air and water.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the ooze remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a mass of waste.

trait.name: Infection
entries: A non-Ooze creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the ooze or touches it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target also contracts {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the Infection of all urban oozes for 1 hour and to {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG} for 24 hours.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage, and the target is subjected to Infection.

reaction.name: Diminish
entries: {@actTrigger} The ooze becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. {@actResponse} The ooze splits into two {@creature Diminished Urban Oozes|GrimHollowMG24}. Each new ooze acts on the original ooze's {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. The original ooze's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are divided evenly between the new oozes (round down).
I thought I'd found a place under the street where no one would find me, but then the sewage moved.

entries.name: Tainted Waste
entries: In the polluted recesses of urban environments, masses of sewage and trash sometimes congeal with the leavings of other oozes to form an urban ooze. These repulsive creatures are nearly invisible in the cesspools they live in.

entries.name: Disgusting Death
entries: The ooze's fetid form is filled with pestilence. Being near it can be dangerous. But the creature is a hunter. Prey it doesn't kill and devour, it drags to the bottom of cesspits to bury beneath layers of putrefaction for later consumption.

entries.name: Ooze Nature
entries: An urban ooze doesn't require sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB} can use the remains of a diminished urban ooze and other reagents worth 25 GP to make {@item Basic Poison|XPHB|one dose of basic poison}. This poison remains potent for 1 hour instead of 1 minute. Making one dose takes 4 hours and requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: An urban ooze is living waste. The stinking air around it is full of pestilence, and so is its touch.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: When wounded, an urban ooze can break into smaller oozes. One can quickly become four.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The ooze can breathe air and water.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the ooze remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a mass of waste.

trait.name: Infection
entries: A non-Ooze creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the ooze or touches it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target also contracts {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the Infection of all urban oozes for 1 hour and to {@disease Sewer Plague|XDMG} for 24 hours.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The ooze can climb difficult surface, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Poison damage, and the target is subjected to Infection
