action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Poison damage, and the target is subjected to Infection.

reaction.name: Diminish
entries: {@actTrigger} The ooze becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. {@actResponse} The ooze splits into two {@creature Urban Oozes|GrimHollowMG24}. Each new ooze acts on the original ooze's {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. The original ooze's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are divided evenly between the new oozes (round down).

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The minstrel casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d8 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Death Note
entries: {@atkr rs} {@hit 5}, range 30 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Psychic damage.

bonus.name: Danse Macabre (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The minstrel plays a magical requiem. Until the end of its next turn, Undead of the minstrel's choice within 30 feet that can see or hear the minstrel rolls {@dice 1d4} and adds the result to each ability check and saving throw it makes. This effect doesn't stack with others that grant similar bonuses, such as the {@spell Bless|XPHB} spell.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, the minstrel can extend the requiem until the end of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The dirgemaster casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

spellcasting.name: Counterspell (3/Day)
headerEntries: The dirgemaster casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Death Marked
entries: A creature that takes damage from the dirgemaster's attacks or spells can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the end of the dirgemaster's next turn.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Death Knell
entries: {@atkr rs} {@hit 7}, range 60 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d8)}) Psychic damage, or 26 ({@damage 4d12}) Psychic damage if the target has the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition.

bonus.name: Macabre Dirge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The dirgemaster plays a magical requiem. Each creature of the dirgemaster's choice that can see and hear it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, that creature must subtract {@dice 1d4} whenever it makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} for one minute. If the target is an allied Undead or Construct, it adds the result to its roll. Otherwise, it subtracts the result from its roll. A creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition is unaffected. This effect doesn't stack with others that grant similar bonuses or penalties, such as the {@spell Bless|XPHB} and {@spell Bane|XPHB} spells.

spellcasting.name: Blur (1/Day)
headerEntries: The disembodied commoner casts {@spell Blur|XPHB}, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.

spellcasting.name: Feather Fall
headerEntries: The disembodied commoner casts {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Fade Away (Recharges after a Long Rest)
entries: The disembodied commoner enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane. It can't affect or be affected by anything on the Material Plane. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the commoner uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end it.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The disembodied arcanist casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 6} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Feather Fall
headerEntries: The disembodied arcanist casts {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, uusing the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting and targeting only itself.

spellcasting.name: Shield (2/Day)
headerEntries: The disembodied arcanist casts {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Coded Speech
entries: The disembodied arcanist can speak in such a way that creatures it chooses hear a hidden meaning, but all others hear only what the arcanist says. {@actSave int} {@dc 14}, any creature that hears the arcanist's coded speech. {@actSaveSuccess} The target knows the arcanist's speech held a hidden message, but not what that message was.

trait.name: Occultation
entries: Any creature of the disembodied arcanist's choice that interacts with it for fewer than 10 minutes is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target forgets its interaction with the arcanist.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The disembodied arcanist makes three attacks, using Dagger or Frost Blast in any combination.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage and 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Lightning damage.

action.name: Frost Blast
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage, and the target's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of the disembodied arcanist's next turn.

action.name: Fade Away (Recharges after a Long Rest)
entries: The disembodied arcanist enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane. It can't affect or be affected by anything on the Material Plane. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the arcanist uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end it.

trait.name: Reckless
entries: At the start of its turn, the doom boar can gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all melee weapon attack rolls during that turn, but attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Two-Headed
entries: The doom boar has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks and on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The doom boar makes two Tusk attacks.

action.name: Tusk
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage. If the doom boar moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Slashing damage and, if it is Large or smaller, has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

If the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 9}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed, suffering a random effect from the {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB} spell. After 1 minute, the target can repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success but extending the curse's duration to 24 hours on a failure.
More vicious than a normal boar, the bite of the two-headed doom boar grants great unluck to those who survive it.

entries.name: Ill-Tempered
entries: The two-headed doom boars hate all life and vent their anger on any creature they can find. The mere sight of a creature drives them into a murderous rage as they try to tear their victim to shreds.

entries.name: Unlucky Wounds
entries: The tusks of a doom boar cause grievous wounds carrying a random malediction lasting from a minute to a day.

entries.name: Bone Collectors
entries: Doom boars find shelter in caves, under trees, or in hollows, but one sure sign of a doom boar's lair is the smell of rot and the carpet of bones that liter the area. Doom boars frequently take trophies from their victims that rot in their lair, leaving bones behind.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The tusks of a doom boar can be harvested and made into a powder. The powder can be brewed into a tea with 75 GP of rare herbs that if drunk within an hour of its creation allows the victim of a curse another saving throw against a curse currently affecting them. The tea has no affect against a curse that does not allow a saving throw.

Additionally, eight doom boars' worth of powder can be alchemically crafted into an elixir known as {@item Hogs' Wash|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)} by a creature with proficiency in {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, spending 24 hours and 500 GP worth of rare herbs and succeeding a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Wounds from a doom boar can bestow a random curse upon the target.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Doom boars fly into a reckless rage when they see other creatures.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A curse caused by a doom boar can be removed with a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or by the creation of a special tea made from the boar's powdered tusks.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The doomcaller casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 18}, {@hit 10} to spell attacks):
footerEntries: {@sup *}The doomcaller casts this spell on itself before combat.

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (3/Day)
headerEntries: The doomcaller casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Magic Mirror (1/Day)
headerEntries: The doomcaller casts {@spell Magic Mirror|GrimHollowPG24} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The doomcaller has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects

action.name: Flame Burst
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 120 ft. {@h}27 ({@damage 6d8}) Fire damage. If the target is an object that isn't being worn or carried, it ignites.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll. Additionally, the doomcaller's allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the target until the start of the doomcaller's next turn.

action.name: Summon Fiend (1/Day)
entries: The doomcaller chooses what to summon and attempts a magical summoning. A doomcaller has a {@chance 60|60 percent chance|Doomcaller|The Dommcaller summons fiends.|The doomcaller fails to summon fiends.} of summoning {@dice 1d6} {@creature Succubus|XMM|succubi} or {@dice 1d4} {@creature barbed devil|XMM|barbed devils}. A summoned fiend appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of the doomcaller, does as it pleases, and can't summon other fiends. A summoned fiend remains for 1 minute, until it or the doomcaller dies, or until the doomcaller dismisses it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

reaction.name: Ill Fortune (3/Day)
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the doomcaller can see makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}. {@actResponse} The doomcaller rolls a d20 and can choose to use this roll in place of the triggering creature's roll.
Despair, the end is nigh!

entries.name: Apocalyptic Prophet
entries: Wrapped in bandages and a cloak, the fiend plays at being a prophet predicting dark times ahead. With the presence of a doomcaller, its predictions are all too real.

entries.name: Tongue of Tongues
entries: When the doomcaller speaks, all understand, and it understands all that is said.

entries.name: One of Many
entries: When the doomcaller needs to reinforce its pronouncements of doom, it summons succubi or other fiends to spread fear and despair.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When slain, the eyes of a doomcaller harden into gems worth 2000 GP each.

When a creature holding one of these gems makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, they can consume a gem to improve their fortunes. After the roll has been made, but before the GM has announced the result of the roll, the player can expend one gem and reroll the roll. Once done, the player must use the new result, the gem shatters and becomes worthless.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Doomcallers are powerful spellcasting Fiends.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A doomcaller can summon {@creature Succubus|XMM|succubi} or {@creature Barbed Devil|XMM|barbed devils}.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Doomcallers have Resistance to Cold, Fire, and Lightning. They have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Acid and Poison.

spellcasting.name: Thaumaturge
headerEntries: The downcast mercenary casts {@spell Thaumaturgy|XPHB}, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Action Surge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The downcast mercenary can take an extra action on its turn.

trait.name: Indomitable (2/Day)
entries: If the downcast mercenary fails a saving throw, it can reroll the saving throw and use the new roll.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The downcast mercenary makes three Greatsword attacks

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage and 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Radiant damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The downcast apostate casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, {@hit 8} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Counterspell (2/Day)
headerEntries: The downcast apostate casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} (level 5 version) in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Innate Spellcasting.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The downcast apostate makes two attacks, using Morningstar or Holy Flame in any combination.

action.name: Morningstar
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Force damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Necrotic or Radiant damage (apostate's choice).

action.name: Holy Flame
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, one creature the downcast apostate can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 5d8}) Radiant damage. {@variantrule Cover|XPHB} grants no benefit against this saving throw.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The downcast sangromancer casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}, {@hit 7} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Blood Rush (2/Day)
headerEntries: The downcast sangromancer casts {@spell Blood Rush|GrimHollowPG24}, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Counterspell (2/Day)
headerEntries: The downcast sangromancer casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Theft of Vitae (2/Day)
headerEntries: The downcast sangromancer casts {@spell Theft of Vitae|GrimHollowPG24} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

bonus.name: Blood Wings
entries: The downcast sangromancer manifests wings of blood and gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet. The wings remain until the sangromancer dies, has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or dismisses them as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The downcast sangromancer make two attacks, using Dagger or Holy Flame in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Holy Flame
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature the downcast sangromancer can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 5d10}) Radiant damage. {@variantrule Cover|XPHB} grants no benefit against this saving throw.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The drab sludge can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The drab sludge can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Stench
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the drab sludge is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} in this way, the target is has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the drab sludge's Stench for 1 hour or until it uses Split, whichever comes first.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Acid damage.

reaction.name: Split
entries: {@actTrigger} The drab sludge becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. {@actResponse} The drab sludge splits into two new drab sludges. Each sludge has {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the original sludge's, rounded down. New sludges are one size smaller than the original sludge.
Their stench fills your nostrils and cloys in the mouth. I wish that were the worst thing about these disgusting sludges.

entries.name: Smelly Sliders
entries: It's difficult to describe the repulsive stench that emanates from a drab sludge. It's like something between a day's old corpse and a rancid latrine, and somehow worse. And the way this deep brownish-green muck sloshes upon surfaces, making a roiling and splashing sound akin to that produced by propelled vomit, only adds to its disgusting nature. These sludges seem more liquid than other oozes, but they can slosh on walls and ceilings in inexplicable ways, adding to their strange and revolting nature

entries.name: Unrelenting Splitters
entries: As if its rancid being weren't horrid enough, these oozes split into smaller oozes. When they do, their stench changes, as if sacks of fouler-smelling stuff are torn open in the process.

entries.name: Ooze Nature
entries: A drab sludge doesn't require sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The smell of a drab sludge is so powerful it can revive the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. Using the remains of a drab sludge, someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can make a {@item Resuscitation Bomb|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Doing so requires materials worth 50 GP, 4 hours of work, and a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: These sludges emit a terrible smell that sickens those who venture near.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Damage eventually causes a drab sludge to split, which unleashes an altered stench, forcing those around it to contend with smaller but nearly as potent oozes.

trait.name: Dreamwalking
entries: While asleep, the dreamer snoop can reach out and touch the dreams of others within 1 mile. After finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} during which the snoop slept, the snoop gains one skill or tool proficiency until it finishes another {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

trait.name: Dreamwalking Snoop
entries: When the dreamer snoop uses Dreamwalking, it can choose a creature it has seen before within 1 mile and cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (spell save {@dc 12}) once on it, acquiring information as if talking to the target. This use of Dreamwalking provides only this benefit.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The dreamer somnolist casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Dreamwalking
entries: While asleep, the dreamer somnolist can reach out and touch the dreams of others within 1 mile. After finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} during which the somnolist slept, the somnolist gains one skill or tool proficiency until it finishes another {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

trait.name: Dreamwalking Shaping
entries: When the dreamer somnolist uses Dreamwalking, it can choose a willing creature within 1 mile. The somnolist enters the target's dreams and helps the target according to its desires. The somnolist can cast spells within the dream, but the creature knows the general effect and must willingly fail any saving throw. The target awakens with {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. This use of Dreamwalking provides only these benefits.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dreamer somnolist makes two attacks, using Shortsword or Scathing Thoughts in any combination.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Scathing Thoughts
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}, one target within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The eagal sithe casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):
will: {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} (level 17 version; can be telepathic)

trait.name: Psychic Feed
entries: When the eagal sithe deals Psychic damage to a creature, it regains an amount of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Psychic damage dealt. Excess healing is gained as {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The eagal sithe makes two Bite attacks. It can replace one attack with Emotional Torment.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 3d4}) Psychic damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition. The target regards the eagal sithe as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected, taking its requests or actions in the most favorable way.

If the eagal sithe or its allies harm the target, it repeats its saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 24 hours. The effect ends early if the eagal sithe dies, is on a different plane than the target, or ends it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Emotional Torment
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 14}, one creature within 60 feet that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the eagal sithe. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Psychic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

bonus.name: Emotional Manipulation
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, one creature within 60 feet that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the eagal sithe. {@actSaveFail} The target must use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a weapon attack or cast a damaging cantrip against a target of the eagal sithe's choice. If the attack hits, it does an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Psychic damage.

bonus.name: Shadow Stealth
entries: In {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, the eagal sithe can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Flitting in the shadows, just out of most people's perception, these fey excel at sowing strife and ruining lives.

entries.name: Creepy Lurkers
entries: Eagal sithe are rarely seen in their true form. They scutter about like roaches, spying from crevices and shadows in search of their next victim. Patient and obsessive creatures, they savor such selection, like a gourmand of corruptible emotion. They learn routines, note traumas and petty frustrations, and then dig in. Once they do, they're hard to shake loose.

entries.name: Roachlike Fey
entries: Eagal sithe sport a rusty brown carapace that protects their wings, and their body is propelled by two pairs of spindly, insectoid appendages, driving it with incredible speed and creepy grace. Its flat upper body is a disgusting humanoid—squashed, sickly pale, and distorted—with a tiny, sneering mouth and large, dead-black eyes framed with constantly searching antennas.

entries.name: Subtle Manipulators
entries: Once their prey is chosen, an eagal sithe latches on with an insidious emotional bond, allowing them to manipulate their victim. They feed off negativity in a heady mix of psychic nourishment and emotional addiction. As the fey feeds, its power grows, and it bloats like a swelling parasite.

entries.name: Mental Scavengers
entries: This psychic feeding is debilitating and eventually fatal to the prey. But such a death releases a surge of emotional energy, elevating the eagal sithe to greater heights of power for a fleeting time. And once this surge dissipates, the fey moves on, searching for a new victim and starting the horrid process anew.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A dried and ground eagal sithe is a potent reagent for many potions, elixirs, poisons, and magic items that can {@condition Charmed|XPHB|charm}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB|frighten}, or affect the mind. When combined with such items' standard components, the DC of any effects requiring either a Charisma or Wisdom saving throw increases by 1. An eagal sithe is typically worth 50 GP to a person knowing its value.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature} or {@skill Arcana}):
entries: These malevolent fey create a bond that allows them to manipulate others' emotions. The more it feeds off its prey's negative emotions, the more powerful the fey becomes.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A dead eagal sithe is worth a fair amount of gold to an alchemist or crafter of magic, but only if the corpse is less than a week old.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The eater casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):

trait.name: Fiendish Palaver
entries: If the eater has consumed a Humanoid's eye, the eater can apply its {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to any Charisma check to impersonate that Humanoid. If the {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} already applies, the eater gains {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} instead.

trait.name: Fiendish Precision
entries: When the eater doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on a melee weapon attack and hits the target, the eater deals 3 extra dice of the weapon's damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Fiendish Sight
entries: Magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} doesn't impede the eater's Darkvision.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The eater makes two Rapier attacks.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage, or 16 ({@damage 3d8 + 3}) Piercing damage if the eater doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack. {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}: The eater extracts one of the target's eyes.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The eater shape-shifts into the Humanoid whose eye it last ate, or reverts to its true form. Its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
entries: The eater takes the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action

reaction.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the eater can see hits it with an attack. {@actResponse} The eater halves the attack's damage.
With a fiendish grin, the urchin pops the merchant's eye into his mouth, and then transforms into the dead man.

entries.name: Servants to Warlocks
entries: Some warlocks ritualistically infuse their followers with demonic humors to give the underlings fiendish power. Those who survive become operatives with extraordinary abilities. Some of the most powerful of these subjects become eaters of orbs.

Working backward from the conclusion that the eyes are windows to the soul, eaters of orbs are trained to extract the essence of a being through the consumption of their eyes. With this abominable exchange, an eater of orbs trained in stealth, impersonation, and assassination can become a top-notch agent and spy.

entries.name: Fiendish Infiltrators
entries: An eater of orbs is unlikely to engage in direct violence unless they have their victim in a position to kill them outright and take their identity. After taking an identity, the eater impersonates the victim as long as needed, taking advantage of opportunities the charade grants. The eater avoids confrontation while disguised, sending allies or minions to deal with threats. When cornered, however, an eater of orbs doesn't hesitate to fight.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A spellcaster that has at least one level 3 spell slot can fashion the scalp of an eater of orbs that has eaten an eye within the last 24 hours into a {@item Hat of Disguise|XDMG}. This process takes 8 hours, materials worth 100 GP, and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: An eater of orbs is a humanoid made fiendish by an eye-consuming ritual. This creature can't be charmed. If it eats a person's eye, the eater of orbs can change into that person's shape.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Any humanoid creature that might serve a warlock can be turned into an eater of orbs by giving them the ability to extract eyes and then change shape after eating them. An eaten eye would heal 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} per CR.

name: Ebon Knight
languages: the languages it knew in life

trait.name: Aura of Smoke
entries: The ebon knight is surrounded by sulfurous black fumes. A creature more than 5 feet from the ebon knight has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against it.

trait.name: Mounted Tactics
entries: The ebon knight and its steed act on the same {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. The steed acts after the ebon knight and has no restrictions on its actions. The ebon knight can force an attack that targets the steed to target the ebon knight instead. If the ebon knight's steed is destroyed, the ebon knight is dismounted but lands on its feed in a space of its choice within 5 feet of where the mount died.

trait.name: Turning Bond
entries: While within 30 feet of its mount, the ebon knight has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being turned. Also, the knight can't be turned unless the same effect also turns the steed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ebon knight makes two Lance attacks.

action.name: Lance
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d12 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Necrotic damage, and if the ebon knight is mounted, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the ebon knight moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 6 ({@damage 1d12}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Summon Steed (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: An {@creature Ebon Knight Steed|GrimHollowMG24} bound to the ebon knight appears in an unoccupied space the ebon knight can see within 30 feet. When summoned, this steed is restored to its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. The ebon knight can dismiss the steed as an action, causing it to disappear. If the knight enters an encounter riding the steed, this action has already been expended.

reaction.name: Set Lance
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature enters the knight's reach while it wields a lance. {@actResponse} The knight makes a Lance attack.
They looked like clouds of dark smoke rolling across the ground toward us. But those hoofbeats and ebony lances were real as death.

entries.name: Evil Martyrs
entries: Paladins who bow to unholy powers serve with fanaticism in life. Those who lay down their lives for their wicked masters return to serve in death as ebon knights. They move wreathed in sulfurous smoke that makes them appear, from a distance, as ghostly or fiendish beings.

entries.name: Death Steeds
entries: The bond an ebon knight has to its steed carries over into death. These steeds emanate smoke like that of their masters. The two fight in unholy synchronicity fostered by their simultaneous demise.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The plate armor of an ebon knight roils with the energy of undying evil. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} can melt the armor of three ebon knights to make {@item Ebon Armor of Invulnerability|GrimHollowMG24|Armor of Invulnerability} that also grants {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. However, this wicked armor requires an attuned wearer to sacrifice life force to it. After the wearer finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, or the first time they put the armor on after having not worn it while finishing one or more Long Rests, they must either give up one-quarter of their remaining Hit Dice to the armor (rounded up) or increase their {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level by 1. Someone proficient with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} takes 30 days to make this armor, which requires other materials worth 10,000 GP to craft. The intended first wearer must give blood each day, losing Hit Dice or taking {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels as if wearing the armor. The process fails, consuming half the materials, if the wearer doesn't feed the armor as it's made. If this being then fails to wear and feed the armor daily for 30 days after it's complete, it disintegrates into ash and smoke.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Ebon knights seek goodness to snuff out. These beings were evil paladins who sacrificed their lives to their unholy masters. Each has an unnatural bond with an undead steed.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The ebon knight and steed are much stronger together. They are all but immune to being turned when in proximity to one another.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: To up the challenge for a powerful party, make it impossible for the ebon knight to drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} if its steed is still alive, and vice versa. Force the characters to find a way to kill both knight and steed on the same attack.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Want to tease your player's a bit? When they defeat an ebon knight, have the steed remain alive. A player may want their character to bond with this powerful steed. But then what happens when the soul of the ebon knight living within the steed decides to make its presence known?

name: Ebon Knight Steed
languages: understands one language the ebon knight speaks but can't speak
telepathy 1 mile (with its ebon knight only)

trait.name: Aura of Smoke
entries: The ebon knight steed is surrounded by sulfurous black fumes. A creature more than 5 feet from the ebon knight steed has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against it.

trait.name: Dissipate
entries: When the ebon knight steed is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it disappears, leaving no corpse.

trait.name: Turning Bond
entries: While within 30 feet of its {@creature ebon knight|GrimHollowMG24}, the ebon knight steed can't be turned unless the same effect also turns the knight.

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Trample
entries: The ebon knight steed makes a Hooves attack against a creature that has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The hag casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Drain Vigor
entries: A creature that takes Psychic damage from the hag is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by the amount of Psychic damage dealt, and the hag regains an equal number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The reduction lasts for 1 minute.

The hag can't reduce the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum to 0, but if a Humanoid with a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum of 1 is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is stabilized. When the target awakens, it is permanently cursed, losing the ability to speak. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or similar magic restores the creature's voice.

trait.name: Immutable Seeming
entries: No effect can change the hag's form, and an illusion can disguise her only if the illusion grants her the Invisible condition.

trait.name: Stolen Voices
entries: The hag can perfectly mimic the voice of anyone cursed by her to lose their voice.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Mocking Words
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

variant.name: Red Hag Coven
entries: Red hags form covens, although few other hags are willing to work with red hags, and so such a coven is usually of three red hags. Red hags are more cooperative than other hags, so their coven can function more cohesively and efficiently.

entries.name: Shared Spellcasting
headerEntries: While all three members of a hag coven are within 30 feet of one another, they can each cast the following spells from the wizard's spell list. For casting these spells, each hag is a 10th-level spellcaster that uses Intelligence as her spellcasting ability. The spell save DC is 11 + the hag's Intelligence modifier, and the spell attack bonus is 3 + her Intelligence modifier. The three hags share the indicated spell slots among them:

entries.name: Steal Body
entries: A red hag coven can allow one of its members to steal a humanoid's body. The target of this ritual must be a humanoid one of the hags cursed to be voiceless, and only the hag who stole that voice can take the body. The ritual requires the target to have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, and the red hag taking the body is {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} during the ritual, which takes 1 hour to complete.

Any magic that protects the target from possession prevents the ritual from succeeding. The target can also make a {@dc 14} Charisma saving throw, preventing the ritual's completion on a success. A successful save also means the target is immune to the effects of the ritual for 24 hours.

If the ritual works, the target's soul departs the body, the red hag's body dies, and her soul possesses the target's body. The hag has the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution, but otherwise, she retains her statistics. The hag's new body has 3 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels when the ritual ends, and each level can be removed only by a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Further, until this {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, any effect that ends or prevents possession causes the new body to become {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} for the effect's duration as the hag's mental connection to the body breaks.

Once the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, the hag's soul and the new body unite. Over the course of three years and three days, the new body changes back into the hag's original form. The hag still gains the benefit of the body's age when she took possession of it.

items.name: Shared Spellcasting (Coven Only)
headerEntries: While all three members of a hag coven are within 30 feet of one another, they can each cast the following spells from the wizard's spell list. For casting these spells, each hag is a 10th-level spellcaster that uses Intelligence as her spellcasting ability. The spell save DC is 11 + the hag's Intelligence modifier, and the spell attack bonus is 3 + her Intelligence modifier. The three hags share the indicated spell slots among them:

items.name: Steal Body (Coven Only)
entries: A red hag coven can allow one of its members to steal a humanoid's body. The target of this ritual must be a humanoid one of the hags cursed to be voiceless, and only the hag who stole that voice can take the body. The ritual requires the target to have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, and the red hag taking the body is {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} during the ritual, which takes 1 hour to complete.

Any magic that protects the target from possession prevents the ritual from succeeding. The target can also make a {@dc 14} Charisma saving throw, preventing the ritual's completion on a success. A successful save also means the target is immune to the effects of the ritual for 24 hours.

If the ritual works, the target's soul departs the body, the red hag's body dies, and her soul possesses the target's body. The hag has the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution, but otherwise, she retains her statistics. The hag's new body has 3 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels when the ritual ends, and each level can be removed only by a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Further, until this {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, any effect that ends or prevents possession causes the new body to become {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} for the effect's duration as the hag's mental connection to the body breaks.

Once the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, the hag's soul and the new body unite. Over the course of three years and three days, the new body changes back into the hag's original form. The hag still gains the benefit of the body's age when she took possession of it.
Those three ladies who own the new tavern are so friendly! It's become my favorite drinking spot.

entries.name: Hag Schism
entries: Long ago, folk believed a few hags were kind, that most hags bared their fangs, but others lent a hand. This inspired the notion that some hags could blend into mortal society. In truth, the "nice" hags learned to catch more flies with honey—a little kindness goes a long way when deceiving mortals.

A schism formed among hags. A majority of hags saw those who pretended to be kind as an anathema. Covens convened to perform one of the most unholy curses hags ever produced. This curse set a hag who transgressed apart and made her mortal, marking her in scarlet: a red hag.

entries.name: Unchanging Form
entries: A red hag can't change her form. She knows no magic to disguise herself. She must get along in her natural form, that of a middle-aged human. Unable to trick mortals using deceptive magic, they instead rely on more common deceptions and wit. Once a red hag feels she has pushed her luck in one settlement, risking revealing her true nature, she moves on to the next.

entries.name: Life and Voice Thieves
entries: A red hag subtly manipulates people to gain trust and friendship before preying on a target. To do so, the hag uses magic to {@condition Charmed|XPHB|charm} the target, then to make the target forget it was {@condition Charmed|XPHB}. Over time, the process makes a creature feel genuine fondness for the hag, or more.

The hag's touch saps the will to live and express, energizing the hag and extending her life. If a red hag all but kills a target with this draining, the creature can lose their voice to the hag forever. The hag can speak in the voices she has stolen.

entries.name: Red Covens
entries: As with other hags, red hags seek hag partners to form covens and increase their magic. Such covens usually involve only red hags, and they often create a situation or seek work that brings them into contact with mortals vulnerable to manipulation. Coven members can also perform a ritual that allows a coven member to take a mortal's body. The hag's curse makes even this "transformation" temporary, but the theft gives the red hag opportunities she lacks in her normal form. And a youthful body can further stave off the hag's mortal decline.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Red hags maintain readiness to flee their current living arrangements. They carry their most precious belongings with them. These objects are treasures that might have some malevolent emotional value to the hag, like a trophy. Red hags are willing to use this wealth to bargain with attackers or other beings.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A red hag is a mortal fey cursed to absorb life from people to avoid aging and dying. This kind of hag can drain a person's vigor to heal herself.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Red hags are subtle rather than mighty foes. Their enchantments are potent, and a red hag can make a victim forget they were {@condition Charmed|XPHB}. These hags rarely attack directly when manipulation can work. And those the hag drains can lose their voices, which the hag keeps and uses.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Three red hags can form a coven that puts more magic at each member's disposal. A red hag coven can perform a ritual to steal the body of a mortal, sending that person's soul to the afterlife as the hag's soul possesses it. Red hags enact this ritual most often to stave off aging. The hag's curse causes her to slowly transform back into herself.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The hag casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Drain Vigor
entries: A creature that takes Psychic damage from the hag is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by the amount of Psychic damage dealt, and the hag regains an equal number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The hag gains any excess healing as {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, which last for 24 hours. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The hag can't reduce the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum to 0, but if a Humanoid with a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum of 1 is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is stabilized. When the target awakens, it is permanently cursed, losing the ability to speak. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or similar magic restores the creature's voice.

trait.name: Immutable Seeming
entries: No effect can change the hag's form, and an illusion can disguise her only if the illusion grants her the Invisible condition.

trait.name: Stolen Voices
entries: The hag can perfectly mimic the voice of anyone cursed by her to lose their voice.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hag makes two attacks, using Claws or Touch in any combination. She can replace one attack with Mocking Words.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Slashing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Touch
entries: {@atkr ms} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 3d4}) Psychic damage, and the target can't take Reactions until the end of the hag's next turn.

action.name: Mocking Words
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

action.name: Charming Banter (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 13}, one creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or magically influenced by the hag that can hear her. {@actSaveFail} When the condition or magical influence ends on the target, it forgets magic was used to influence it.

variant.name: Red Hag Coven
entries: Red hags form covens, although few other hags are willing to work with red hags, and so such a coven is usually of three red hags. Red hags are more cooperative than other hags, so their coven can function more cohesively and efficiently.

entries.name: Shared Spellcasting
headerEntries: While all three members of a hag coven are within 30 feet of one another, they can each cast the following spells from the wizard's spell list. For casting these spells, each hag is a 10th-level spellcaster that uses Intelligence as her spellcasting ability. The spell save DC is 11 + the hag's Intelligence modifier, and the spell attack bonus is 3 + her Intelligence modifier. The three hags share the indicated spell slots among them:

entries.name: Steal Body
entries: A red hag coven can allow one of its members to steal a humanoid's body. The target of this ritual must be a humanoid one of the hags cursed to be voiceless, and only the hag who stole that voice can take the body. The ritual requires the target to have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, and the red hag taking the body is {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} during the ritual, which takes 1 hour to complete.

Any magic that protects the target from possession prevents the ritual from succeeding. The target can also make a {@dc 14} Charisma saving throw, preventing the ritual's completion on a success. A successful save also means the target is immune to the effects of the ritual for 24 hours.

If the ritual works, the target's soul departs the body, the red hag's body dies, and her soul possesses the target's body. The hag has the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution, but otherwise, she retains her statistics. The hag's new body has 3 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels when the ritual ends, and each level can be removed only by a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Further, until this {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, any effect that ends or prevents possession causes the new body to become {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} for the effect's duration as the hag's mental connection to the body breaks.

Once the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} ends, the hag's soul and the new body unite. Over the course of three years and three days, the new body changes back into the hag's original form. The hag still gains the benefit of the body's age when she took possession of it.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The herald casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 6} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Otherworldly Calm
entries: The herald has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions, and its thoughts can't be read. A creature that attempts to read the herald's thoughts is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The herald makes three attacks, using Handaxe or Psychic Burst in any combination.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage plus 6 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Psychic Burst
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft or range 60 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

action.name: Prophecy of Doom (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within 120 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target is subjected to a random effect from the {@table Eldritch Effects|GrimHollowMG24} table. All targets are subjected to the same effect. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats its save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The priest casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit 4} to spell attacks):

action.name: Greatclub
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Psychic Burst
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft or range 60 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

action.name: Prophecy of Doom (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 12}, each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within 120 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target is subjected to a random effect from the {@table Eldritch Effects|GrimHollowMG24} table. All targets are subjected to the same effect. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats its save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

trait.name: Death Throes
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the brazen bull when it dies. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Fire damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Radiant damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

trait.name: Soulfire Nimbus
entries: At the start of each of the brazen bull's turns, each creature within 5 feet of it takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Radiant damage. A creature that touches the brazen bull or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Radiant damage.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The Empyrean brazen bull deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The brazen bull makes two attacks, using Bite or Hooves in any combination. It can replace one attack with Gore.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 10 ft. {@h}24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 20}). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and the brazen bull can't Bite another target.

action.name: Gore
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 10 ft. {@h}27 ({@damage 3d12 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage. If the brazen bull moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and the brazen bull can make a Bite or Hooves attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 5 feet. {@h}24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Swallow
entries: The brazen bull makes one Bite attack against a Medium or smaller creature it has {@condition Grappled|XPHB} with its Bite. {@h}The target takes the Bite attack's damage, no longer has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, and is swallowed. While swallowed, the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from effects that originate outside the brazen bull. It takes 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Fire damage at the start of each of the brazen bull's turns.

If the brazen bull takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the brazen bull must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the swallowed creature, which lands in a space within 10 feet of the brazen bull and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the brazen bull dies, the swallowed creature no longer has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and can escape the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

The smell of smoke and incense consumed the castle walls, and we heard the furious and gleeful bellows of the most immense bull we'd ever seen. As our battlements burned and crumbled, we knew all was lost.

entries.name: The Golden Bull
entries: This golden metallic bull is filled with divine fire. A nimbus of soul fire dances around it, emanating from its glowing and intelligent amber eyes, and flaming hoof tracks follow in its wake.

entries.name: Beast with a Burden
entries: The stomachs of this divine bovine are full of soulfire, and all that it eats is consumed in its heavenly absolution. A soul of pure celestial energy inhabits its divine and golden metal trappings. It delights in the cleansing of evil, steadfast in its purpose, and stubborn in its execution of its duty.

entries.name: 'Mooving' and Shaking
entries: The brazen bull was used by the celestial armies as a formation breaker and siege engine. It can charge through the enemy, break down fortresses, and, if it is felled in battle, take more than a few opponents as the fire in its belly explodes.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The exploded metal hide of the Empyrean brazen bull can be harvested to make gleaming and radiant {@item Brazen Armor|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}. A proficient armor smith can make a suit of {@item Brazen Armor|GrimHollowMG24} by succeeding on a {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check and using 2500 GP of components. This process takes 20 days to complete.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Wildfires that seem to begin with hoofprints are sometimes found during the dry season in farmland, and bright spots on the horizon that look like a massive cow are often reported at the same time.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The Empyrean brazen bull is a beast of burden for angels, used for besieging enemies.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The Empyrean brazen bull explodes when it dies, and luck be with all in the wake of the blast.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: The Empyrean brazen bull is obviously a strong force on the side of law and good, and evil or chaotic characters could easily find themselves getting the horns if they mess with the bull. However, just like any other creatures, brazen bulls can be tricked into working against their own interests. They can also be manipulated or corrupted by agents of evil to work against good characters.

Brazen bulls can be altered to take other forms as well. Other forms might have different modes of movement to match their environment, and they might have different types of natural weapons. Regardless of the form they take, however, their attacks and traits should remain the same. An Empyreus brazen dragon or whale, for example, might be able to fly or swim, but they'll still be able to charge, swallow, damage with their aura, and explode when defeated.

trait.name: Ever Observant
entries: This celestial has reduced itself to individual floating eyes that never stop watching. It cannot be surprised.

action.name: Flash of Light
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the eye. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Radiant damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it automatically succeeds. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The eye has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition and can teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 feet.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The knight doesn't provoke an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The knight has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Only Forward
entries: The knight is unable to flee from battle until all its enemies are destroyed or it is.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The knight makes two Longsword attacks.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 4}) Force damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Peacemaking
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 14}, up to four {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creatures the bloodied can see. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and weeps uncontrollably until another creature takes an action to shake it out of its trance.

action.name: Shared Sacrifice
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 16}, one creature within 60 feet that the bloodied can see. {@actSaveFail} Until the end of the bloodied next turn, the bloodied has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage, and whenever the bloodied takes damage, the target takes the same amount.

reaction.name: Ultimate End
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 60 feet of the bloodied targets it with an attack. {@actResponse}—{@actSave wis} {@dc 16}. {@actSaveFail} The target takes Force damage equal to the bloodied's remaining {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and the bloodied dies. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage, and the damage can't reduce the target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If the creature would be reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

trait.name: Plant Stride {@recharge 5}
entries: If within 5 feet of a Large or bigger area of plants, the epachrach can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second Large or bigger area of plants that is within 60 feet of the previous area. These plants can be animate creatures, such as a treant, or magical, such as the plants the Entangle spell calls forth.

trait.name: Relentless (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: If the epachrach takes 30 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The epachrach deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Tusk
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft. {@h}25 ({@damage 4d8 + 7}) Slashing damage. If the epachrach moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and the epachrach can make a Hooves attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Hooves
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft. one {@condition Prone|XPHB} creature. {@h}29 ({@damage 4d10 + 7}) Piercing damage.
Beware the epachrach, an enormous fey tusker. They make giant boars seem friendly and warm.

entries.name: Fey Fury
entries: An epachrach is a creature of fey fury and might. Empowered by the strength of ancient oaks, it crashes through the forest, seeking those who defile places of primal power. It can abruptly manifest, like a sudden storm of woody skin and twisting tusks, bringing pain and death.

entries.name: Primal Guardian
entries: Epachrachs seem like forces of uncontrolled rage, but their wrath has purpose. Each epachrach, or a herd of such creatures, guards a sacred natural place. Powerful druids bind some to protect sacred groves from enemies. Other epachrachs defend a place where primal forces naturally gather. Whatever the nature of this spot, the epachrachs guard it with their lives.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The leaves and bark that form an epachrach's skin are as durable as steel but much lighter and more flexible, making them ideal for creating {@item Scale Mail|XPHB}. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB} can use the hide to craft {@item Scale Mail|XPHB} that allows a wearer a maximum Dexterity bonus to AC of +3 and doesn't cause the wearer to have disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks. This armor takes 10 days to make, requires other materials worth 250 GP, and weighs 25 pounds.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: This plantlike boar is really a fey creature and guardian of places of primal power. Its woody hide has Vulnerability to Fire and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing attacks.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Legends say that epachrachs can disappear suddenly or appear from nowhere. The truth is that they can teleport through areas of living plants.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Several tales tell of those who stumble into an area epachrachs watch over. Leaving the guarded area or proving no harmful intent saved wily heroes in those stories.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: In general, monsters that knock characters prone are best paired with monsters that perform melee rather than ranged attacks, since ranged attacks against prone targets are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

Creating encounter areas where prone creatures are grabbed by creeping vines and restrained until they escape is a great way to increase the challenge of an encounter with epachrachs. This also gives the epachrachs plenty of opportunities to use their Plant Stride ability.

trait.name: Fey Touched
entries: Magic can't put the faevlin to sleep. Only a Fey creature can cause the faevlin to have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, and a faevlin always knows when a non-Fey creature attempts to impose the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition on it.

action.name: Scimitar
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Shortbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4}, range 80/320 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Sneaky
entries: The faevlin takes the Hide action.

reaction.name: Fey Fade
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature misses the faevlin with an attack. {@actResponse} The faevlin can teleport up to 30 feet in a random direction, appearing in an unoccupied space.
Never make a deal with the fey. Never make a deal with a goblin. And if you ever meet a faevlin, you'll know why.

entries.name: Fey Goblin
entries: Faevlins are what happen when a group of goblins makes deals with the fey that they can't keep. In poor lighting, a faevlin can be mistaken for a goblin. However, faevlins are unmistakable in the light. They have teal skin, and a faevlin's head is upside down. Faevlins work for stronger fey or guard places where the veil between the mortal world and the land of fairies is weak.

entries.name: Broken Promises
entries: As the story goes, in ancient times, a clan of goblins made a deal with a fey lady to gain power. The goblins thought they could break the rules of the deal if no fey were watching. They were wrong. Fey magic swept the clan away. When they returned, they were faevlins. Some say these faevlins escaped, and others claim the fey sent them back to the mortal world to cause trouble. Still others say their servitude ended because they were more trouble than they were worth.

entries.name: Uncharmed Life
entries: Faevlins willingly work with other creatures, often for mischief and crime, and can be bullied by stronger, wicked beings. They can't be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by creatures other than fey. But a faevlin might pretend to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} to get the drop on an enemy.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Faevlins love to collect objects that increase their personal prestige and power. Every faevlin is likely to have a few personal trinkets like this, along with the occasional item of real worth.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A faevlin can teleport away from attackers but does so in a manner even the faevlin can't predict.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Faevlins are goblins cursed by powerful fey magic.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A faevlin can't be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by nonfey, but they have been known to pretend to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} to trick the enchanter.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The inquisitor hunter casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 11}):

spellcasting.name: Hunter's Mark (1/Day)
headerEntries: The inquisitor hunter casts {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} using the same spellcasting ability as in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Inquisitor's Awareness
entries: The inquisitor hunter can spend 1 minute maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} to learn whether any arcane or innate spellcasters, Aberrations, Fey, and Fiends are within 1 mile. This trait doesn't reveal the creatures' locations or numbers.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The inquisitor hunter makes two Shortsword attacks, provided it has a Shortsword in each hand.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage, or 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Psychic damage if the target is maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell.

action.name: Longbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4}, ranged 150/600 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage, or 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Psychic damage if the target is maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The inquisitor priest casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

spellcasting.name: Spiritual Weapon (1/Day)
headerEntries: The inquisitor priest casts the {@spell Spiritual Weapon|XPHB} spell, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

trait.name: Ward
entries: When the inquisitor priest casts a spell that causes creatures to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the priest can choose one of the spell's targets and end the effects of one spell affecting it. The effect must be from a spell of equal or lower level to the priest's healing spell.

action.name: Warhammer
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Force damage, or 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Force damage if the target is maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell.

trait.name: Brave
entries: The inquisitor knight has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Discerning
entries: The inquisitor knight has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against illusions.

trait.name: Mark
entries: When the inquisitor knight hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, it Marks the target until the end of the inquisitor knight's next turn. The Mark ends early if the knight has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition or dies, or another creature Marks the same target. While the Marked creature is within the inquisitor knight's reach, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than the inquisitor knight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The inquisitor knight makes two attacks, using Longsword or Javelin in any combination.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage, or 8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Slashing damage if wielded with two hands. The inquisitor knight Marks the target.

action.name: Javelin
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage. If the attack was a melee attack, the inquisitor knight Marks the target.

reaction.name: Marked Control
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature Marked by the inquisitor knight moves while within 5 feet of the inquisitor knight. {@actResponse} The inquisitor knight makes a Longsword attack against the triggering creature. {@h}In addition to the Longsword damage, the creature's Speed becomes 0 until the end of its turn.

headerEntries: The inquisitor warder casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

trait.name: Ward
entries: When the inquisitor warder casts a spell that causes creatures to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the warder can choose one of the spell's targets and end the effects of one spell affecting it. The effect must be from a spell of equal or lower level to the warder's healing spell.

entries: The inquisitor warder makes three Warhammer attacks.

action.name: Warhammer
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Force damage, or 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Force damage if the target is maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell.

headerEntries: The Inquisitor Judge casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Aura of Clarity
entries: While conscious, the inquisitor judge emits a 10- foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of clarifying magic. Each creature in the area of the judge's choice can't have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and the judge chooses whether creatures and objects in the area can have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Smite
entries: Once per turn, when the inquisitor judge hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, it can expend a spell from its Spellcasting action. The spell has no effect, and the attack deals an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage for a 2/Day spell or 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Radiant damage for a 1/Day spell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The inquisitor judge makes three Greatsword attacks.

action.name: Greatsword

trait.name: Seven Shades of Sitri
entries: A Humanoid that touches the Sitri cat or takes damage from its Claws attack is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target is infected with a disease called the {@disease Seven Shades of Sitri|GrimHollowPG24}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the disease for 24 hours.

An infected target is overwhelmed with carnal urges. When the target interacts with a non-{@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} Humanoid, it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the Humanoid or its allies harm the target. Every 24 hours, the target repeats the save, ending the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition but not the disease on a success. The disease ends after the target succeeds on five saves.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Slashing damage, and the target is subjected to the Seven Shades of Sitri.

trait.name: Faith Cough
entries: A Humanoid that touches the faith finch or takes damage from its Talons attack is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target is infected with a disease called {@disease Faith Cough|GrimHollowPG24}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the disease for 24 hours.

An infected target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks and Constitution saving throws. Every 24 hours, the target repeats its save. The disease ends after the target succeeds on seven saves.

trait.name: Inspired Presence
