entries: The laneshi soldier can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The laneshi soldier makes two melee Pike attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Net.

action.name: Pike
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 10 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d10 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Net
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 11}, one Large or smaller creature the laneshi soldier can see within 15 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The target can take an action to free itself or another creature trapped by a Net with a successful {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. Dealing 5 Slashing damage to the Net (AC 10) frees the target and destroys the Net.

bonus.name: Skirmisher
entries: The laneshi soldier takes the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The laneshi necromancer casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, +6 to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Healing Word (3/Day)
headerEntries: The laneshi necromancer casts {@spell Healing Word|XPHB}, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The laneshi necromancer can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Death Strike (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: When the laneshi necromancer hits with a melee attack, the target takes 27 ({@damage 5d10}) Necrotic damage in addition to the attack's effects. A Humanoid slain by this damage rises at the start of the necromancer's next turn as a zombie under the necromancer's command.

trait.name: Duality of Spirit
entries: The laneshi necromancer has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws and spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Necrotic Mastery
entries: Necrotic damage dealt by the laneshi necromancer ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The laneshi necromancer makes two attacks, using Spear or Ghostly Hand in any combination.

action.name: Spear
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Ghostly Hand
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 6}, range 60 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d10}) Necrotic damage, and the target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the end of the laneshi necromancer's next turn.

name: Leeching Willow
languages: understands Deep Speech and all languages those infected by it knew but it cannot speak

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The leeching willow casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 18}):

trait.name: Bell Weakness
entries: A bell rung within 30 feet of the tree forces it to uproot, disrupting its False Appearance and suppressing the effects of its Leeching Spores. A loud bell rung near a creature kills any Leeching Spores inside of it.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the leeching willow remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.

trait.name: Leeching Spores
entries: TThe leeching willow emits spores from its body in a 1,000-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Each creature that breathes in the leeching willow's spores is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 18}. {@actSaveFail} The spores take root in the target's body, infecting it. {@actSaveSuccess} The creature is immune to being infected for 1 minute, but still has spores inside its body.

An infected target's body feeds vigor to the leeching willow. The target gets minimal rest from sleeping, suffering a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} every 7 days (to a maximum of 4 levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}). These {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels can't be removed by taking a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} until the spores are removed from the creature's body.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The leeching willow deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The leeching willow makes three attacks, using Slam or Rock in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Psychic Spike.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 5d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage

action.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 10}, range 60/180 ft. {@h}28 ({@damage 4d10 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage

action.name: Psychic Spike
entries: Intelligence Saving Throw: {@dc 18}, one creature with Leeching Spores in its body. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 5d10}) Psychic damage, and the target can't take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. On the target's next turn, it must choose whether it can move, take an action, or take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}; it only gets one of the three. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Psychic Slam (1/Day)
entries: The leeching willow uses Psychic Spike against each creature with Leeching Spores in its body within 1,000 feet. This special use of Psychic Spike deals 45 ({@damage 13d6}) Psychic damage, kills any Leeching Spores in the target's body, and suppresses the leeching willow's Leeching Spores trait for 1 round. If this damage kills a target, its head explodes, if it has one.
Don't seek out the wood of a willow tree for your fuel or building material. For you might accidentally run afoul of a leeching willow.

entries.name: Hidden Aberration
entries: The leeching willow looks like a normal willow tree. Hidden inside, however, is a powerful aberration, a massive brain with a nerve and circulatory system that runs throughout the tree. The brain and the tree are interconnected through every branch and root.

entries.name: Leeching Spores
entries: Instead of feeding through the sun or roots, the leeching willow feeds using psychic spores breathed in by creatures around it. The spores enter through the olfactory system and move into the brain. From there the leeching willow feeds on the electrical energies of the brain. The feeding process is slow and requires multiple sentient creatures infested for it to sustain the creature. Further, this process weakens those infected as their vigor is sapped and their mental energies drained.

entries.name: Cancerous Infiltrator
entries: The leeching willow can manipulate the memories of those infected, turning them into unwitting participants in the aberration's feeding. By using its basic motor functions, the aberration sneaks into humanoid villages and settlements, planting itself right in the center of the community in the middle of the night. Then it uses its memory-altering spores to trick the humanoids into thinking it's always been there.

entries.name: Unwitting Allies
entries: Humanoids infected by the leeching spores become irrationally defensive about all trees in the area, specifically the leeching willow itself. They look perpetually tired, disregard their own hygiene, barely eat, and become sedentary. Communities infested by leeching spores die over the course of a few years as they wither away, attempting to blame their ills on exterior sources.

entries.name: Fear of Vibration
entries: The leeching spores require very delicate brain waves and psychic vibrations to survive and transfer the mental energies to the aberration. Strong external vibrations can disrupt the delicate connection between the aberration and the subject, potentially killing the spores within the brain and freeing the infested. These vibrations are strongest when they form harmonical vibrations that sound like ringing, especially that of bells.

entries.name: Ring That Bell
entries: The ring of a large bell instantly disrupts all connections from the infested who can hear the ringing, destroying all spores within the same radius. For this reason, subconsciously, the leeching willow imparts memories onto the infested of strong hatred toward anything that can ring or vibrate in such a manner. All bells are gathered up and hidden far away where they cannot be heard (destroying them is difficult without making them ring). Common objects like silver utensils or glass are discarded and not used anywhere on the settlement either, for fear of any form of ringing.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A leeching willow is potent and powerful while inside of its protective tree form, but when severed from it and extracted, it's as weak and feeble as newborn lamb. The greatest treasure one can get from the aberration is the incredible font of knowledge it possesses about humanoids it has fed from.

A book made from the pulp of the tree containing the aberration can be made into a {@item Tome of Clear Thought|XDMG}. This process requires a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check from a proficient bookmaker or sage, as well as 5000 GP of ink and other rare components used over 15 days.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}):
entries: The air around you is sweet and delectable, it feels fresh as if you were high on a mountain. It's not a fragrance you recognize, and it doesn't smell like any food you have experience before, but it smells delicious all the same.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}):
entries: The villager you see looks sickly and tired, as if they haven't got a good night's rest in over a week. Their muscles have deteriorated from lack of use, and they show no motivation for life or work.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The spores in the air are magical in nature, and they give a psychic connection between those infected by the spores and the tree that emits the spores.

trait.name: Berserk
entries: Whenever the lenchtahg starts its turn with the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 1, the lenchtahg recalls its former life and current agony, going berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the lenchtahg attacks the nearest creature it can see. It treats all creatures as {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} and makes any {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} it can. Also, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, but all attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the lenchtahg moves as far as it can toward the closest creature.

Once the lenchtahg goes berserk, it remains so until it is destroyed or it loses the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition. A Fiend can take an action to calm the lenchtahg with a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, suppressing this trait for 10 minutes.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The lenchtahg has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Radiant Absorption
entries: Whenever the lenchtahg is targeted by Radiant damage from a source other than a lenchtahg, it takes no damage and instead regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the Radiant damage dealt.

trait.name: Rejuvenation
entries: If the lenchtahg's head survives its demise, the lenchtahg reappears in 6 days in a fiery explosion. {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the lenchtahg when it rejuvenates. {@actSaveFail} 28 ({@damage 8d6)} Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

If the lenchtahg's severed head is targeted by a {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB} spell or doused in holy water and ritually consecrated in a 1-hour ritual, it doesn't rejuvenate. The head can't rejuvenate on consecrated ground, like that created by a holy {@spell Hallow|XPHB} spell.

trait.name: Water Aversion
entries: If drenched in 5 gallons or more of water, or any amount of {@item Holy Water|XPHB}, the lenchtahg has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lenchtahg makes two attacks, using Claw or Radiant Gaze in any combination.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Fire damage.

action.name: Radiant Gaze
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature the lenchtahg can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Radiant damage. {@variantrule Cover|XPHB} provides the target no benefit for this save.
The smoky, fiery form hisses and shrieks in a cacophony of anger and confusion. There's something almost holy in the sound.

entries.name: Corrupted Seraphs
entries: Arch Daemon Malikir, corrupter of all that is good, crafted the first lenchtahg from the seraphic body of a captured member of Arch Seraph Empyreus's court. Taking glee in twisting a follower of the so-called "Unbroken Seraph," the Arch Daemon killed the Seraph, distorted its spirit, and transformed it into a construct of smoke and flame, a being in constant agony, compelled to obey its demonic overlords.

entries.name: Endless Pain
entries: A lenchtahg has lost its former identity, but Malikir's cruel design ensures that it remains sapient and in constant pain, aware of its enslavement. Malikir even went to the trouble of ensuring that a lenchtahg might recall memories of its past life as a further torment, though this trait drives the lenchtahg into bouts of uncontrolled rage.

entries.name: Useful Minions
entries: Lenchtahgs possess many useful properties, such as magic resistance, rejuvenation, and the ability to absorb holy power to heal themselves. This latter trait is useful against the forces of the Seraphs. However, a lenchtahg is difficult to create. Even if capturing a Seraph alive were a straightforward task, the effort expended in transforming it into a lenchtahg is almost prohibitive, a luxury only afforded to Arch Daemons and their most powerful followers.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The severed head of a lenchtahg is a potent magic object. To the right buyer—a necromancer, a daemon cultist, an evil alchemist, and the like—a lenchtahg head is worth 750 GP. The servants of the Arch Daemon Malikir guard the secrets of binding a lenchtahg, but hags and other wicked creatures with magical skills possess knowledge to convert a lenchtahg head into a construct with similar unholy power.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Radiant damage heals a lenchtahg, which still has the flesh of a Seraph.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Dowsing a Lenchtahg with a lot of water or any {@item Holy Water|XPHB} can temporarily weaken it.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The lenchtahg's head must be consecrated in a holy ceremony or otherwise rid of its evil to avoid the lenchtahg's rejuvenation. But those with the right knowledge can use the head to craft a magical servitor.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Those who use lenchtahg as troops in battle will use Radiant magic to damage foes while at the same time healing the lenchtahg. This greatly heightens the strength of these monsters.

name: Lich Troll
languages: the languages it knew in life and Giant

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The lich troll casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, +8 to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (2/Day)
headerEntries: The lich troll casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Protective Magic (4/Day)
headerEntries: The lich troll casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} (level 4 version) or {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries: If the lich troll fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The lich troll regains 15 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of its turn. If the lich troll takes Acid or Radiant damage, this trait doesn't function until the start of the lich troll's next turn. The lich troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lich troll makes three attacks, using Claw, Frost Beam, or Grave Beam in any combination.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Frost Beam
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 8}, reach 60 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Cold damage, and the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the start of the lich troll's next turn.

action.name: Grave Beam
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 8}, reach 60 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d10)}) Necrotic damage, and the target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the end of the lich troll's next turn.

legendary.name: Evasive Attack
entries: The lich troll uses {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} and makes a Claw, Frost Beam, or Grave Beam attack. If it is out of uses of {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, it just makes the attack.
Running away from a troll is smart. Running away from a troll that casts spells is wishful thinking.

entries.name: Botched Experiment
entries: Before research led to the creation of the first soul vessel and lich, desperate wizards made many failed attempts in the pursuit of immortality. Given that trolls return to a hale, hearty state after most injuries, some wizards decided inserting the soul into a troll's body might be the right course. The results were poor.

entries.name: Obscene Amalgamation
entries: Most lich trolls look like a humanoid skull with burning eyes atop a troll's body. Due to the imperfect process, the creature lost some of its arcane power. It gained the benefit of the body of a regenerating giant.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB} can fashion the skull of a lich troll into a {@item Ring of Regeneration|XDMG}. Doing so takes materials worth 5,000 GP, 10 days of work, and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. Somebody must also cast {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} on the ring each day during the process. If the ring's wearer dies while wearing the ring, the soul of the lich has a {@chance 75|25 percent chance|Lich Ring|Nothing occurs.|The Lich's soul takes over the body of the ring's wearer.} to take over the corpse and use it as a new body. But if the ring is created entirely in the area of a {@spell Hallow|XPHB} spell with the everlasting rest effect, the tie to the lich's soul is broken

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The lich troll is remnants of early attempts of powerful spellcasters to transfer their souls into trolls.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The lich troll has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. It regenerates and can be killed only by Acid, Fire, or Radiant damage.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The zombie troll regains 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of its turn. If the zombie troll takes Acid or Radiant damage, this trait doesn't function until the start of the zombie troll's next turn. The zombie troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The zombie troll makes two Morningstar attacks. If a target is hit by both attacks, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Morningstar
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Disease {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}
entries: The lindwyrm has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all nonmagical diseases.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day or 4/Day in Lair)
entries: If the lindwyrm fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lindwyrm makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks. It can replace one Claw attack with Swallow.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 15 ft. {@h}22 ({@damage 3d10 + 6}) Piercing damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 18}). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and the lindwyrm can't Bite another target. {@actSave con} {@dc 18}. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Poison damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 10 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Swallow
entries: The lindwyrm makes one Bite attack against a Huge or smaller creature it has {@condition Grappled|XPHB} with its Bite. {@h} The target takes the Bite attack's Piercing damage (but not the Poison damage), no longer has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, and is swallowed. While swallowed, the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from effects that originate outside the lindwyrm. It takes 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Acid damage at the start of each of the lindwyrm's turns. The lindwyrm can only have one target swallowed at a time.

If the lindwyrm takes 40 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the lindwyrm must succeed on a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the swallowed creature, which lands in a space within 10 feet of the lindwyrm and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the lindwyrm dies, the swallowed creature no longer has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and can escape the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
entries: The lindwyrm makes a Claw attack.

legendary.name: Burrowing Rush
entries: The lindwyrm burrows up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, coming up beneath a target touching the ground and making a Bite attack against it. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. The lindwyrm can't use this action again until the start of its next turn.

My great grandfather spoke of the lindwyrm terrorizing the countryside and devouring whole villages. But it's been so long since anyone has seen the beast, it's likely the creature is long dead. Thank Miklas!

entries.name: Century's Sleep
entries: After a few months of gorging itself, a lindwyrm burrows deep into its underground lair where it slumbers, only stirring if something disturbs it. But in another hundred years, its hunger wakens it again.

entries.name: Adventurous Eater
entries: Lindwyrms are voracious eaters, consuming all manner of crops, livestock, and people. If it can swallow it, it does, and lindwyrms have very big mouths.

entries.name: Burrowing Terror
entries: With their long serpentine bodies and two large claws, lindwyrms can burrow nearly as fast as they can run above ground. Tremors can be a sign of an approaching lindwyrm.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A dose of {@item Lindwyrm Venom|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)} can be harvested by someone proficient with a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB} and succeeds on a {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check, but this must be done within 1 hour of the lindwyrm's death. If the check fails by 5 or more, the harvester instead poisons themselves. This Injury Poison is worth 1,000 GP.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Lindwyrms sleep for 100 years and when they waken are devastating to communities in its hunting area.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Lindwyrms have a poisonous bite and may swallow creatures they bite.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Lindwyrms can sense vibrations in the ground from as far away as 120 ft.

name: Lithobel
languages: understands Infernal and the languages it knew in life but can't speak

trait.name: Two Heads
entries: The lithobel has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lithobel makes four attacks using Battleaxe, Mace, Shield Bash, or Spear in any combination.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) Force damage.

action.name: Mace
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) Force damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Shield Bash
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) Force damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it is pushed 10 feet away from the lithobel.

action.name: Spear
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}19 ({@damage 4d6 + 5}) Force damage. {@hom} If thrown, the spear reappears in the lithobel's hand immediately after the attack.

bonus.name: Rampage
entries: After reducing a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a melee attack, the lithobel moves up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes a melee attack.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the lithobel can see hits it with an attack. {@actResponse} The lithobel adds 4 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.
The two-headed, four-armed, blood-covered statue moves forward, weapons at the ready.

entries.name: Duels in Tormach's Honor
entries: With the rise of the Cult of Tormach throughout Unterland, the bloody ambitions of Speaker Schlei have come to fruition more and more. Under his orders, cultists devoted to the demented Arch Daemon of war fight one another to the death in single combat as an offering of sacrificial bloodshed. If both combatants die from their wounds and their combat is glorious, Tormach grants the devotees special favor.

entries.name: Commemorated for Eternity
entries: Tormach grafts combatants honored for their bloodthirsty sacrifice, together forming a four-armed, two-headed creature known as a lithobel. The creature's skin is transmuted into rough stone, and it is granted massive stone weapons capable of slaughtering a draft horse in a single swing. The hulking creature is then turned loose on the hapless population of Etharis, possessing only the drive to maim and kill any living creature unlucky enough to cross its path.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The powdered stone of a lithobel's heads can be used in place of diamond dust for the {@spell Stoneskin|XPHB} spell. One lithobel produces powder worth 1,000 GP.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: This foul creature is the result of a battle to the death between two followers of Tormach. It wants only blood. Poison is ineffective, and nonmagical attacks do the creature less harm.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The living toxin can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Toxic Nature
entries: When the living toxin or the host of its Toxic Invasion is subjected to an effect that ends the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, the living toxin takes 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Necrotic damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Necrotic damage per level of the effect, if any.

action.name: Touch
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Poison damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 13}). Until this grapple ends, the living toxin can't Touch another target.

action.name: Toxic Invasion
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the living toxin. {@actSaveFail} The living toxin invades the target's body. While inside a host, the living toxin has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from effects that originate outside the host. The host has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and takes 10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Poison damage at the start of each of the living toxin's turns.

At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. The effect ends early if the host dies or is subjected to any effect that ends the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. When the effect ends, the living toxin leaves the host, landing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet.
Makes me sick just thinking about it. The blasted thing swept right up into the smithy, and next thing we knew, she was on the ground, rolling and screaming.

entries.name: Manufactured Menaces
entries: A living toxin is an ooze at the pinnacle of the poisoner's art. It's poison that delivers itself to the victim. Living toxins are usually found around cities, hiding in sewers, and sliding along back alleys.

Each living toxin begins as a mixture of poisons and alchemical ingredients. Whether by accident or ill intent, the mixture gains a semblance of life and often turns on its creator. The ooze escapes through the nearest grating or window, seeking out places to hide and hunt.

entries.name: Invasive Species
entries: When a living creature comes along, the ooze displays its most sinister trait. It launches itself at its victim's face and tries to force its way inside their body. Once there, the toxin attacks the body from within. After the interior is liquefied, the ooze escapes from the corpse.

entries.name: Ooze Nature
entries: A living toxin doesn't require sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A living toxin breaks down into harmless goo once slain. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} can combine the goo with other reagents or herbs worth 50 GP to create two doses of {@item Keoghtom's Ointment|XDMG|Restorative Ointment}. Doing so requires 8 hours of work and a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence or Wisdom check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Living toxins are poisonous mixtures given life. A living toxin attempts to force itself inside a host, attacking from within.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Effects that cure poisoning are highly effective against a living toxin.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: It's not too difficult to imagine the existence of a sentient living toxin, capable of infecting a host but choosing when to inflict the poison damage instead of doing so automatically. Such a creature, if given the ability to communicate with a host telepathically, could blackmail a host into doing its bidding. Such creatures could serve evil masters.

name: Lupilisk
languages: can learn languages but can't speak

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The lupilisk has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the lupilisk's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}. First {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. At the end of its next turn, the target repeats the save. Second {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition instead of the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. After 24 hours, the target repeats the save. Third {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition permanently. If the target succeeds on any of its saves, the effect ends for it.
If you find a statue in the wild with its mouth open in a scream, flee. Best case, it's an artist working out their twisted ideas. Worst case, you'll be a statue soon.

entries.name: Petrifying Predators
entries: The fiendish lupilisks can be found in woodland areas or amid an infernal army. their impressive strength and agility, as well as their size, makes them perfect mounts for infernal cavalry. And their keen instincts mark them as an apex predator.

Lupilisks prefer to play with their food, chasing and tormenting it before turning it to stone. The lupilisk then eats the rocky remains. As with a basilisk, the lupilisk's gullet reverses the petrification, turning stone to flesh once it reaches the creature's stomach.

entries.name: Family Pack
entries: In the wild, lupilisks gather in packs. A dominant elder couple leads the pack, and other pack members are that couple's offspring. Juvenile males seek mates from other packs, while juvenile females decide whether to take visiting males as mates. A lupilisk pack is a family, its adult children leaving to form new packs.

entries.name: Trained Mounts
entries: A lupilisk is more beast than fiend. They're aggressive and cruel, but they can be controlled if trained with firm discipline.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can take four lupilisk venom fangs, or just the two fangs of one lupilisk elder, and treat them with reagents worth 250 GP per tooth for 3 days. A successful treatment requires the alchemist to succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. During the treatment time, somebody must also cast {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} on the fangs. After a successful treatment, someone who has proficiency with {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB} can fashion the fangs, now blackened, into a necklace, creating a {@item Periapt of Proof Against Poison and Petrified|GrimHollowMG24|Periapt of Proof Against Poison}. If the wearer attunes to the periapt, the amulet also provides that wearer {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A lupilisk's bite imparts a petrifying venom to prey. This magic toxin grows more potent as the lupilisk ages.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Lupilisks live in packs with an elder couple in the lead. This couple are the parents of most other pack members.

name: Lupilisk Elder
languages: can learn languages but can't speak

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The lupilisk has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the lupilisk's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Poison damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. At the end of its next turn, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition permanently instead of the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Pack Attack {@recharge 5}
entries: One lupilisk or lupilisk whelp the lupilisk elder can see within 30 feet can use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make a Bite attack. The target must be able to see or hear the lupilisk elder. Then the lupilisk elder makes a Bite attack.

name: Lupilisk Whelp
languages: can learn languages but can't speak

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The lupilisk has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the lupilisk's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Poison damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. At the end of its next turn, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition instead of the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. The effect ends after 1 minute.

trait.name: Grappler
entries: The werewolf has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against {@condition Grappled|XPHB} targets. Its attacks deal an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage against a creature it has {@condition Grappled|XPHB}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The werewolf makes two melee attacks, using Claw or Shortsword in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Bite.

action.name: Bite (Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) Piercing damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it gains the {@charoption Lycanthrope|GrimHollowPG24|Lycanthrope Transformation}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this werewolf's curse for 24 hours.

action.name: Claw (Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m}

{@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 14}) if it is Medium or smaller. It can grapple one creature at a time, and it cannot use Claw attacks against other targets when grappling a creature.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The werewolf shape-shifts into a wolf-humanoid hybrid or back into its true form, which is humanoid. Any armor it is wearing merges into its hybrid form.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The werebear casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}, +6 to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Healing Word (3/Day)
headerEntries: The werebear casts {@spell Healing Word|XPHB} using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The werebear makes three Claw attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Bite

action.name: Bite (Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d8 + 3}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 15}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it gains the {@charoption Lycanthrope|GrimHollowPG24|Lycanthrope Transformation}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this werebear's curse for 24 hours.

action.name: Claw (Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The werebear shape-shifts into a bear-humanoid hybrid, a bear, or back into its true form, which is humanoid. Any armor it is wearing merges into its hybrid form.

The werebear's kindred bear form is a Large bear. In this form, it can speak to and understand bears, can't take any {@variantrule Action|XPHB|Actions} that require hands, and adds its Constitution modifier to any saving throw it makes. The werebear gains 25 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} the first time it assumes its bear form each day. In bear form, it uses the same attacks as the Hybrid form.

trait.name: Earthbound
entries: The lyfaren must stay surrounded by earth. If the lyfaren starts its turn with its entire Gargantuan body removed from the ground, it takes 36 ({@damage 8d8}) Force damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lyfaren uses Bite, and if it has a creature grappled, it uses Swallow.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 15 ft. {@h}42 ({@damage 8d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 18}).

action.name: Swallow
entries: The lyfaren swallows a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by it. While swallowed, the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions, has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} against attacks and other effects originating from outside the lyfaren, and the target takes 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the lyfaren's turns. A lyfaren can have up to four Large or smaller creatures swallowed at a time.
If the path fades out beneath your feet, be careful where you look to find it again. Following the wrong trail marker might be your last steps.

entries.name: Underground Bound
entries: Lyfaren are enormous burrowing creatures, looking like a massive rocky leach, that spend their lives surrounded by dirt, rock, and rubble. They can't see, but rather perceive the world through vibrations with their antenna, the only part of their bodies which can survive in open air. Lyfaren can sense the movement of an earthworm, as well as the feet of the bird that briefly landed to acquire that snack.

entries.name: Off-Trail Tricks
entries: Like the anglerfish and many other creatures, lyfaren lure in their preferred prey, humanoids, with the temptation of safety or curiosity. Their antenna closely resembles stacks of rock that we would call a cairn: a manmade stone marker indicating a trail or other location of interest. But as soon as you're within a few paces, they swallow you whole, leaving nothing to see.

entries.name: Imprecise But Deadly
entries: While slow and easy to avoid if you know what you're looking for, the lyfaren swallows even the strongest adventurers before they can fight back.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The "rocks" that form the lyfaren's antenna can be cracked open, revealing what looks like beautiful crystals, much like a geode. There is a {@chance 25|25% chance|Lyfaren|The antenna can be turned into an elemental gem.|The antenna cannot be used to create an elemental gem.} that a lyfaren has an antenna that can be turned into a yellow diamond {@item Elemental Gem, Yellow Diamond|XDMG|Elemental Gem}. This transformation requires someone proficient in the {@skill Nature} skill to succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check while using 50 GP of other components. The process takes 4 hours.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Only the antennae and the maw of the lyfaren can survive outside of the earth. However, the maw can easily swallow up creatures the size of a horse, pulling it into its rock-filled gullet.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: When trying to figure out if a cairn is manmade or deadly, look for a leaf, feather, or small piece of ribbon between the rocks. Man-made cairns are often decorated, while a lyfaren antenna may have bones or blood near it.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A lyfaren needs the pressure of being surrounded by dirt to survive, find a way to unearth one and the fight is over.

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

trait.name: Corrode Magic
entries: Any magical weapon that hits the ooze has some of its magic stripped away. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a cumulative −1 penalty to attack and damage rolls. If the penalty reaches −3, the weapon permanently becomes a mundane version of that weapon type. A weapon affected by this magical draining reduces the penalty by 1 every 24 hours. Magical ammunition that hits the ooze becomes mundane immediately after dealing damage.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the ooze remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an oily pool or wet rock.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 36 ({@damage 8d8}) Force damage. If the target is wearing magical armor, the armor is stripped of some power and takes a cumulative −1 penalty to the AC it offers. If the penalty reaches −3, the armor permanently becomes a mundane version of that armor type. Armor affected by this magical draining reduces the penalty by 1 every 24 hours.

reaction.name: Feed
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature deals damage to the ooze with a spell. {@actResponse} The ooze reduces the damage dealt by that attack to 0, and instead regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the amount of damage it would've taken.
For every action, there's an equal and opposite reaction by an angry wizard.

entries.name: Made for Spite
entries: Magebane oozes were created by an irritable wizard to wreak havoc on rivals. Unfortunately for him, his creations got loose before he could unleash them, making him their first victim.

entries.name: Devourers of Magic
entries: Magebane oozes feed on magical energies. Although they can survive for years without feeding, they do so by going dormant. An active ooze shrivels quickly if it lacks a source of magic.

entries.name: Unusually Intelligent
entries: Because their creator intended them to attack other wizards, he experimented to provide them greater intellect than most oozes. As a result, they strategize and can set traps for their prey.

entries.name: Inquisition Tool
entries: The Arcanist Inquisition has recently learned of the existence of magebane oozes, and inquisitors are in the process of capturing the strange oozes to use against their magic-wielding foes.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Magebane oozes are a terrifying risk for even well-equipped adventurers. Even in death, some of their corrosive properties persist. Someone who makes a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check can carefully collect the remaining potent ooze into a vial. This can be turned into a {@item Magebane Bomb|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}. Making this item requires a proficient arcanist to spend 4 hours, use 100 GP of components, and succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Magebane oozes feed on magic and quickly reduce magical weapons and armor to regular, non-magical versions of those weapons.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Magebane oozes were created by a vengeful wizard who lost control of them before he could unleash them on his rivals.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Some arcanists speak in hushed whispers of a particular mutation that occurs after magebane oozes have managed to devour enough magic. These magebane evolutions are nearly indestructible and can not only strip away magic, but store and then direct it back at the unlucky caster who loosed it.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Magic is such a powerful force in the game that twisting it to use against characters can sometimes seem to be the only thing that can scare a character. A more powerful form of magebane ooze that collects and harnesses the destructive nature of magic used against them would be a terrifying prospect for high-level magic-wielding characters.

trait.name: Enamoring Scent
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the maiden's hair is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. Every minute, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 hour. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the maiden hair's Enamoring Scent for 24 hours.

While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions. The target uses its movement on each of its turns to approach the maiden's hair. It doesn't avoid danger, but before moving into damaging terrain and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the maiden's hair, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A strong wind (such as one created by {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB}) suppresses the scent for the wind's duration.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the maiden's hair remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary plant.

action.name: Tendril
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and takes 6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns, and the maiden's hair can't make Tendril attacks against other creatures.

trait.name: Enamoring Scent
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the maiden's hair is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. Every minute, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 hour. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the maiden hair's Enamoring Scent for 24 hours.

While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions. The target uses its movement on each of its turns to approach the maiden's hair. It doesn't avoid danger, but before moving into damaging terrain and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the maiden's hair, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A strong wind (such as one created by {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB}) suppresses the scent for the wind's duration.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the maiden's hair remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary plant.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The maiden's hair makes two tendril attacks.

action.name: Tendril
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 10 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and takes 11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The maiden's hair can grapple up to two creatures at a time.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The malcinder makes two attacks, using Claw or Tail Flame in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Bite.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the malcinder moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and the malcinder can make a Bite attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Tail Flame
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or ranged 30/120 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 2d4}) Fire damage.
A shadowy form moves silently toward its prey, stalking with precision. Sudden flames erupt as the malcinder roars and leaps into the air to crush its target to the ground.

entries.name: Infernal Hunters
entries: Malcinders sometimes escaped the Netherworld, forming small hunting packs found in every region. They suppress their infernal nature when hunting and resting for stealth, dusky skin concealing them in the darkness.

entries.name: Born in Flames
entries: When a malcinder attacks, its body hardens like cooling lava, and flames glow through its skull. It harnesses this infernal fire within its whiplike tail to hurl flame.

entries.name: Burning Leader
entries: The strongest of malcinders leads a pack. This alpha is the largest in the group and the best hunter. A malcinder alpha draws attention so the pack can attack from all sides.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When a malcinder dies, the flames within its body go out, and the corpse hardens like volcanic rock. The claws and fangs from one malcinder corpse make a powder that someone who has proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can make into a {@item Potion of Speed|XDMG}. Doing so requires other reagents worth 1,000 GP, 8 hours of work, and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Malcinders are Fiends with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A malcinder alpha coordinates its pack efficiently. Slaying this leader can make the pack much less dangerous.
Malcinders are prone to following stronger fiends. Therefore, a creature with fiendish ancestry can tame a malcinder.

trait.name: Fiery Body
entries: A creature that touches the malcinder alpha or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Fire damage.

trait.name: Pack Leader
entries: The malcinder alpha and each {@creature malcinder|GrimHollowMG24} within 30 feet of it gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against a creature if at least one other allied malcinder is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The malcinder alpha makes three attacks, using Claw or Tail Flame in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Bite

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the malcinder alpha moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and the malcinder alpha can make a Bite attack against it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Tail Flame
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or ranged 30/120 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) Fire damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The malefic broker casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

spellcasting.name: Shield (1/Day)
headerEntries: The malefic broker casts {@spell Shield|XPHB} (level 1) in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The malefic broker has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Soul Shards
entries: The malefic broker has six soul shards. It can cast an expended spell from Spellcasting or Shield by spending soul shards equal to the spell's level, as listed in those actions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The malefic broker uses Mindfire twice and Puppeteer once.

action.name: Mindfire
entries: {@atkr ms,rs} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. or range 30/60 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Fire damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Psychic damage, and the target ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the target, it takes 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Fire damage and 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Psychic damage at the start of each of its turns.

action.name: Puppeteer
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15}, one creature the malefic broker can see within 120 feet. {@actSaveFail} The creature has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the end of the malefic broker's turn. The target must immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack or cast a damaging cantrip against a creature or object of the broker's choice. If the target is ignited by Mindfire, its attack or cantrip deals an extra 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Fire damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Psychic damage.

reaction.name: Soul Siphon
entries: {@actTrigger} A living creature dies within 30 feet of the malefic broker. {@actResponse} The malefic broker gains one soul shard.
The sound of coins clanking together is music to the ears of some. In the hands of a malefic broker, it's a death knell.

entries.name: Disciples of Gorodyn
entries: A rare fiend, the malefic broker is an example of a diabolic middleman. Taking the form of a humanoid, the malefic broker hones its skills in negotiation and acquisition rather than its fiendish might. Greed motivates a malefic broker, who scrambles to acquire more souls for Gorodyn through deception and persuasion.

entries.name: Soul Shards
entries: Despite a disdain for mortal wealth, a malefic broker carries gems, which the fiend uses to siphon pieces of souls fleeing the dying. When cornered, a malefic broker consumes these soul shards to gain eldritch might it can use to defend itself.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Soul shards taken from the malefic broker fetch 250 GP each, or more, from rich collectors and arcanists. If crushed, added to water, and imbibed, each soul shard acts as a {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG}. A malefic broker carries jewels worth at least 500 GP to turn into more soul shards.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Malefic brokers collect souls, either through fiendish contracts or being near those who die. The soul shards they carry can power their fiendish abilities.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The imp casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Creeping Corruption
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the imp is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 12} (a creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition automatically succeeds). First {@actSaveFail} The creature acts in accordance with its most selfish, venal, and ruthless impulses to the best of its ability. After 24 hours, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second {@actSaveFail} The compulsion lasts until removed by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The imp has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit -1}, reach 0 ft. {@h}1 ({@damage 1d4 - 2}) Piercing damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 10}. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage.
I can give you anything, mortal. Riches? Accolades? To be important, for once? Whisper your secrets to me. I will tell you the secrets of your rivals. They all dance with me.

entries.name: Prideful Purpose
entries: A minor daemon of Malikir, Arch Daemon of Pride, the Malikirian imp was created to tempt mortals into acting on their base desires and soothe their guilty consciouses with rapturous feelings of entitlement and certainty. It is said the Angel of Empyreus keeps one chained to elicit confessions and goad mortals into the very acts of sin the Angel of Empyreus seeks to punish.

entries.name: A Decrepit Devil
entries: The imp is a wretched, bruised, shriveled creature that would almost inspire pity, were it not unmistakably fiendish. Its diminutive head resembles the skull of a bighorn sheep, and its sinuous body is covered in cracked and haggard scales.

entries.name: Infernal Intelligence
entries: Before the Godswar, these imps would be exchanged as gifts and familiars by agents of Malikir to influential mages or court advisors to inspire selfishness, war, and hunger for power. They are s pies experts at gaining secrets and revealing them for maximum damage.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: If caught alone with a hostile foe, the imp pleads for its life and pledges to serve its new master. It gives its name, which a caster can use when casting {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} to summon and bind the imp as their familiar.

An imp's scales and bones can be used to create a {@item Imp Potion of Fire Resistance|GrimHollowMG24|Potion of Fire Resistance} with a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) ability check from a character proficient in {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}. This takes 2 hours and 10 GP of materials. However, there's a {@chance 90|10% chance|Imp|The potion acts normally|The potion imparts fulnerability to all damage except fire.} that the person taking the potion will have Vulnerability to all other damage.
Eating the Malikirian imp's heart grants the ability to cast {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} once without using a spell slot. The {@variantrule Difficulty Class|XPHB|DC} to resist this spell is 10.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Beware the multitudinous throngs of Malikir's progeny, for they can corrupt even the most pure-hearted and spur them to acts of sin and moral decay.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Many a foolish warlock thought they had the upper hand when they received such a pathetic creature as their familiar, but they underestimated the imp at their peril.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Despite archmages' divinations, no one quite knows how the Angel of Empyreus came to hold the chains of a Malikirian imp. This cannot be good news.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Play the Malikirian imp as the master manipulator it is. Its main weapon is its enemy's greed, so dig deep into whatever might tempt a character, and keep digging until you find a weakness. Often even if a character isn't greedy, the player is.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The marra casts one of the following spells, requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The marra has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The marra makes three Claws attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Crushing Presence.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Crushing Presence
entries: {@atkr ms} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft., one {@condition Prone|XPHB} creature. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d6 + 3}) Psychic damage and the marra enters the target's space and sits on its chest. The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 14}) and is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. First {@actSaveFail} While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. If the target is still {@condition Restrained|XPHB} at the end of its next turn, it repeats the save. Second {@actSaveFail} While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Until the grapple ends, the target takes 13 ({@damage 3d6 + 3}) Psychic damage at the end of each of the target's turns.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The marra shape-shifts into a Tiny moth or back into its true form. In moth form, the marra has a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 5 feet, a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|Flying Speed} of 40 feet, and can't speak. Otherwise, its game statistics are the same in each form. Anything the marra is wearing or carrying transforms with it.
Marras are literally the stuff of nightmares.

entries.name: Nightmare Spirits
entries: These nocturnal visitors sit on a sleeping victim's chest, drawing out personal fears and driving poor souls to panic before suffocating them. Those who have survived a marra attack testified that when the creature came to visit, the victim felt a heavy weight on their chest before losing the ability to move.
Survivor accounts also report the marra can shapechange, often becoming moths. In this form, a marra can enter rooms through keyholes or other tiny openings.

entries.name: Night Riders
entries: Marra steal horses and other mounts, riding off into the twilight in search of victims. The animals are left exhausted and covered in sweat by dawn.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A nightmare pine grows in the marra's wake. A proficient {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB} can fashion a {@item Nightmare Staff|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)} from this stunted tree. Doing so takes 5 days of work, materials worth 100 GP, and someone to cast {@spell Phantasmal Force|XPHB} on the staff each day.
Near where a marra is slain, there is a {@chance 50|50% chance|Marra|An Adder Stone is nearby.|There is no item nearby.} of finding an {@item Adder Stone|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A marra is a fiend with power over dreams and sleep. It is immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and it can polymorph into a moth.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A {@condition Prone} or sleeping target is vulnerable to a marra's crushing psychic weight.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The maskenmagier casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}, {@hit 9} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Counterspell (3/Day)
headerEntries: The maskenmagier casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Devour Soul
entries: maskenmagier can consume the soul of a Humanoid it has killed in the past hour by spending 10 minutes adjacent to its corpse. The target's soul is trapped in the maskenmagier for 24 hours. If the maskenmagier dies or the soul is raised from the dead before this duration ends, the soul is freed. Otherwise, it is digested and no mortal magic can restore it. The maskenmagier can digest only one soul at a time.
After digesting a soul, the maskenmagier gains a soul mask in the likeness of the devoured soul. The maskenmagier can use this mask with its Shape-Shift action for 13 days.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The maskenmagier has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Teleport {@recharge 4}
entries: As its movement, the maskenmagier can teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 feet.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The maskenmagier makes three attacks, using Claws or Soul Bolt in any combination

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 28 ({@damage 8d6}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Soul Bolt
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, reach 60 ft. {@h}26 ({@damage 4d12}) Necrotic damage, or 39 ({@damage 6d12}) Necrotic damage while the maskenmagier is digesting a soul. The target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of the maskenmagier's next turn.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The maskenmagier shape-shifts into a Small or Medium Humanoid or reverts to its true form. Other than its Size, its game statistics are the same in each form. If the maskenmagier has a soul mask in the likeness of the Humanoid it is shape-shifting into, it gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception}) checks to impersonate the Humanoid and instinctively knows the Humanoid's quirks and behaviors. Besides the soul mask, any equipment the maskenmagier is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

bonus.name: Quick Casting
entries: The maskenmagier makes a Soul Bolt attack or casts an at-will spell from Spellcasting.
A mask can hide who you are. Careful lest you forget who you are.

entries.name: Feline Fiend
entries: The maskenmagier can alter its appearance to take any humanoid form, but it is a cat-headed fiend with a humanoid body. Driven by a desire to grow more powerful, the maskenmagier makes masks and consumes souls.

entries.name: Magical Masks
entries: Carved from wood and painted with natural pigments on a neutral base of glue and crushed seashell, the masks a maskenmagier offers portray a beast. Each mask allows the wearer to transform into that animal.

A maskenmagier is a clever spellcaster artful at negotiation and hungry for power. It offers people the opportunity to escape life's troubles through mask magic. A deal consists of a proposal that covers the terms each party expects. Accepting the mask seals the agreement and makes the contract binding.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Those who defeat a maskenmagier discover a {@item Mask of the Maestro|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The maskenmagier is immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} and {@condition Charmed|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The masks that the maskenmagier offers are cursed.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: A maskenmagier can devour a Humanoid's soul, allowing the fiend to take on an uncanny copy of the person's form.

trait.name: Rider's Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries: The outlaw deals an extra 10 ({@damage 3d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the outlaw that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and the outlaw doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll. The outlaw can also deal this extra damage if it has moved 20+ feet this turn before making the attack, including on a mount.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Blackpowder Pistol
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5}, range 25/100 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Mobile
entries: Both the outlaw and its mount takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

reaction.name: Uncanny Riding
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the outlaw can see hits it or its mount with an attack. {@actResponse} The outlaw halves the attack's damage against itself or its mount.
Stick to the roads to avoid the monsters of the wild, they tell you. The roads aren't all that safe, I reply!

entries.name: Roads of Etharis
entries: Travel in Etharis is a dangerous proposition. Those who venture beyond the safety of city walls often stick to the network of roads laid down during the Bürach Empire's heyday. These roads have their own perils, however, as evidenced by the outlaws who've made highway robbery their trade.

entries.name: Flamboyant Thievery
entries: Outlaws of the road differ from usual thieving ruffians in several ways. Traversing the roads quickly and keeping pace with carriages and wagons means that this breed of bandit relies on horses or other mounts. Riding in on horseback makes stealth less of an option, so this path attracts those with a flair for the dramatic. When a traveler hears a gunshot and a boisterous laugh, an outlaw won't be far off.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The {@item Blackpowder Pistol|GrimHollowPG24|Blackpowder Pistols} that outlaws favor are extremely rare and valuable. However, rough use and poor upkeep comes with a robber lifestyle, which means that the pistol requires maintenance before it can be used reliably. This maintenance costs 100 GP and must be performed by someone who has proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}. Without this refurbishing, the pistol breaks beyond repair the next time a shooter using it rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll. This catastrophe occurs before any other trait can mitigate it unless the GM rules otherwise.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Outlaws rely on speed and a decisive first strike to demoralize their quarry. Those in this profession often love a flamboyant lifestyle and the thrill of riding into danger.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Outlaws prefer to use {@item Blackpowder Pistol|GrimHollowPG24|Blackpowder Pistols} for an initial strike. The powerful attack and the loud noise strengthen the impact of the outlaw's arrival, causing many to give up without a further fight.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Hit and run tactics are a mainstay of outlaw tactics. Any outlaw worth their weight in blackpowder always has a contingency plan for when circumstances don't favor them. Using mounts means they can escape more easily, and often the paths they take while escaping are lined with traps that they can easily avoid, while pursuers must contend with them.

trait.name: Opening Shot
entries: If the master outlaw hits a target with a ranged weapon attack during the first round of combat, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes against the same target before the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Rider's Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries: The master outlaw deals an extra 21 ({@damage 6d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the master outlaw that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and the master outlaw doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll. The master outlaw can also deal this extra damage if it has moved 20+ feet this turn before making the attack, including on a mount.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The master outlaw makes two attacks, using Rapier or Blackpowder Pistol in any combination.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Blackpowder Pistol
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 7}, range 25/100 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Mobile
entries: Both the master outlaw and its mount take the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

bonus.name: Quick Loader
entries: The master outlaw loads a bullet into its Blackpowder Pistol or another ranged weapon with the {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} property.

reaction.name: Uncanny Riding
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the master outlaw can see hits it or its mount with an attack. {@actResponse} The master outlaw halves the attack's damage against itself or its mount.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The plague doctor casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit 5} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Good Medicine (1/Day)
entries: The plague doctor carries a concoction that, if consumed as an action, restores 13 ({@dice 3d8}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and cures any disease.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Poison damage.

action.name: Bad Medicine
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, each creature in a 10- foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point the plague doctor can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, the target takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Poison damage each time it takes an action. The target can take an action to repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.
Those who hold power over life and death are dangerous for exactly that reason.

entries.name: Medical Calling
entries: When the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} spread in Liesech, the call went out for any mage or physician who might be able to develop a cure for this horrible blight. This call led to an influx of healers and wizards, many hoping to gain fame and glory by solving the riddle of this new disease. They were unprepared for the situation that awaited them.

entries.name: Forged by Disaster
entries: Liesech was in a horrible state. The disease swept from person to person unhindered by treatments that science and magic could bring to bear. In desperation, the few healers who managed to avoid succumbing to the disease developed entirely new branches of magical alchemy in hopes of stemming the tide.

Two groups emerged from this plague-ridden metropolis. One is the Morbus Doctore, who claimed victory over the disease with a secretive and costly cure. The other is an ununified host of would-be saviors, some twisted by the horrors they witnessed.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Plague doctors are experts at medicinal arts and possess {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB|Healer's Kits}, and {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB|Herbalism Kkits}. Once they progress into the more specialized alchemy, they might also have several concoctions, including many potions that mimic spells. See the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Plague Doctor wizard tradition|Plague Doctor|GrimHollowPG24} {@homebrew |in chapter 5 of Grim Hollow: The Players Guide} for more information on what a plague doctor might have or how these NPCs might be customized.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: In the wake of the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}, many mages and scholars delved into the study of diseases. Those who learned the secrets of blending science and magic into alchemical concoctions are known as plague doctors.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Medicine}):
entries: The repeated failures and deaths during the search for a cure for the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} led to a new epidemic of unhinged magical alchemists. Some still seek to ply their trade, curing whatever sicknesses they come across. Others now see life itself as a disease in need of a cure.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Inured to disease and suffering, some former physicians turned their alchemical concoctions to combat uses. They can heal themselves and throw volatile magical grenades that can afflict foes with disease symptoms.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: For maximum surprise and effectiveness in challenging the characters, plague doctors are best used when the characters trust them. Perhaps the characters are relying on a doctor to help them in a situation where diseases are ravaging an area. A plague doctor is as likely to kill a character suffering from a disease (in the name of medicine, of course) than heal them.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The plague doctor casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}, {@hit 7} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Conditioned Immunity
entries: The plague doctor has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to disease and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Good Medicine (2/Day)
entries: The plague doctor carries a concoction that, if consumed as an action, restores 22 ({@dice 5d8}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and cures any disease.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Bad Medicine
