As part of the curse, a poppet has a cherry-sized stone heart within its torso. When the doll is slain and the curse is removed, the seams tear or the poppet vanishes, and the heart clatters to the ground amid a bloodlike fluid. Properly treated, this gem is a potent talisman against fear (see Salvage).

entries.name: Talking Doll
entries: A poppet can talk, saying simple phrases that have sinister meaning in context or with hindsight. The doll speaks when a situation calls for it. Whenever a particular poppet is about to attack, for instance, it might say, "It's time to play."

When a person, usually a child, bonds with a poppet, the doll uses telepathy to converse with that person. Amused adults think the child is talking to an imaginary friend, not recognizing the real threat it slowly turns its owner toward evil.

When the opportunity presents itself, a poppet fiend strikes a deal. It makes a contract for that coveted pony, revenge on a bully, or getting out of chores. With each agreement, the owner descends further into wickedness.

entries.name: Lifelong Friend
entries: If the true nature of the poppet fiend remains undiscovered, it reveals its true nature when it believes its owner might accept this revelation. Stories tell of corrupted people working with a poppet fiend to continue the cycle of deceit and obtain their desires.

entries.name: Constructed Nature
entries: A poppet that is a construct doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Embedded in a poppet is a {@item Telltale Heart|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}. The faint whisper of the possessing spirit's memories, whether ghost or fiend, lives on in this bloodstone the size of a large cherry. For the stone to work, the poppet it was attached to must have been truly dispatched, its curse ended.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: These possessed dolls have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to attacks that aren't adamantine or silvered.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Some poppets are possessed by unquiet spirits but others are fiendish. All are cursed.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Embedded within a poppet is a bloodstone heart that can't be found until the poppet's curse is lifted.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the poppet fiend remains motionless, it's indistinguishable from an ordinary doll.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The poppet fiend has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Poison damage, and the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

action.name: Shape-Shift
entries: The poppet fiend shape-shifts into a doll or reverts to its true form, that of a Tiny imp-like devil. Its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell cast on it while it is {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} or dead forcibly reverts it to its true form, then causes it to vanish in a puff of vile smoke.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The potbelly makes two Slam attacks. It can replace one attack with Boil.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft. {@h}19 ({@damage 4d6 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the potbelly can halve the attack's damage and cause the target to have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 16}). The potbelly can grapple up to two creatures at a time.

action.name: Boil
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 16}, one Medium or smaller creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the potbelly. {@actSaveFail} The grapple ends and the target is plopped into the potbelly's belly pot. The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from effects that originate outside the potbelly. It takes 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Fire damage immediately and at the start of each of the potbelly's turns. The potbelly can have up to two creatures boiling at a time.

The target can take an action to escape with a successful {@dc 16} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check, landing in a space within 5 feet of the potbelly. If the potbelly dies, the target is no longer {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and can escape from the corpse using 10 feet of its movement.

action.name: Snack
entries: The potbelly grabs the corpse of a Fey, Giant, or Humanoid that died no longer than 1 minute ago in its belly pot and takes a bite, regaining 25 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The potbelly can gain this benefit only once from each corpse.
Our invader does nothing but laugh at our pain. Someone, anyone, save our little town!

entries.name: Cursed Giant
entries: A potbelly is a giant cursed by unseelie fey. What remains is the mockery of a giant filled with the desire to cook and consume other living beings. The giant's name comes from its new appearance. A cauldron hangs in the giant's abdomen. It contains a bizarre boiling oil, and the potbelly can use this vessel to cook foes.

entries.name: Gleeful Mayhem
entries: A potbelly always smiles and joyfully goes about murdering and cooking other creatures. It happily snacks on fried corpses from its belly pot while crushing other foes. Even at the edge of death, a potbelly keeps up this twisted good cheer.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The cooking fluid in a potbelly's cauldron cools and evaporates quickly after the potbelly dies. Someone proficient with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can preserve some of the fluid within 1 minute of the fey giant's death. This sample can be used to create a {@item Sizzling Serum|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Brewing this serum takes 4 hours and reagents worth 50 GP, and it requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A potbelly is a giant cursed by fey magic. It can grab smaller creatures and cook them in its belly pot.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A potbelly receives a supernatural boost from eating those who died in the giant's stomach cauldron.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The puck casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Fey Evasion
entries: If the puck is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, the puck instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The puck has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Plant Bond
entries: If the puck remains within 20 feet of a Huge or smaller plant for 8 hours, it can use special dust to form a bond with the plant, granting it sapience as if by the Awaken spell. The target gains the ability to understand Sylvan and becomes a puck version of an animated plant, such as a puck tree or puck shrub.

The puck can have only one plant {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way at a time. The condition ends if the puck harms the plant, and the plant can make a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw to end the condition if a request from the puck guarantees the plant's destruction. Plants freed from the charm leave the puck's grove, becoming inanimate again after 24 hours. Otherwise, the plant is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the puck for 30 days, after which the plant becomes the puck's willing servant.

The puck is emotionally bonded with each plant it has animated, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, and enthralled. Provided such a plant is within 1 mile, the puck is aware when the plant takes damage and knows its location. If such a plant is destroyed, the puck has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn as it grieves.

action.name: Superior Invisibility
entries: The puck magically becomes {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until its {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends. Any equipment the puck wears or carries is {@condition Invisible|XPHB} with it.

bonus.name: Plant Manifestation
entries: The puck causes a plantlike duplicate of itself to emerge from a Plant within 120 feet that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or enthralled by it. The puck can act through this duplicate until the end of its turn, at which point the duplicate disappears.

reaction.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature the puck can see hits it with an attack. {@actResponse} The puck halves the damage it takes from the attack.

legendary.name: Illusionary Menace
entries: Six images of the puck appear in multiple locations, each moving and speaking independently during the puck's turn. At the start and end of the puck's turn, and one time during the puck's movement, it can teleport to the location of one of these images. The images remain until the next round.

legendary.name: Hostile Nature
entries: Grasping vines and roots manifest in the lair. Strength or {@actSave dex} {@dc 10}, each creature {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to the puck in the lair. {@actSaveFail} The target is moved up to 20 feet to another unoccupied space in the lair and gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

legendary.name: Illusionary Menace
entries: Inanimate plants in the lair twist and sprout thorns. The area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} to creatures {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to the puck until the next round, and are subject to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 10}, when a creature moves more than half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (as dictated by the {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}) in the area. {@actSaveFail} The creature gains the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. {@actSaveSuccess} the creature is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the Poisonous Plants effect for 24 hours.
I've heard pixie dust is beautiful, magical stuff. The dust I saw was definitely magical, but it wasn't beautiful.

entries.name: Crushed Spirit
entries: A puck is a pixie whose hopes and dreams, loves and playfulness, have been erased by mistreatment, betrayal, or loss. Once a beautiful and merry being, a puck is now a sad, twisted monster. Once the transformation happens, the pixie's dust dissipates. Without pixie dust, a pixie can't fly, can't use its magic, and can't turn invisible. They lose their ability to commune with nature.

entries.name: Puck Dust
entries: Taking the place of pixie dust, puck dust allows the puck to retain magical powers that resemble those of a pixie. The substance corrupts soil, vegetation, and beast, and it enthralls plants and trees to do the puck's bidding. Plants under the dust's influence become telepathically and emotionally bonded to the puck. Despair drives these plants. Each feels the harm done to one.

entries.name: Corpse Gardener
entries: Pucks farm their glittering soil, using animals and other living creatures to produce fertilizer. The puck force feeds the grove's dead material and soil to animals and humanoids. After a ripening time, the puck opens these unfortunates up to take refined soil from their innards. The puck keeps the creatures alive until this grisly harvest, earning the terrible epithet "corpse gardener."

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A slain puck produces up to six pinches of puck dust, which are magical but less effective in the hands of a non-puck. Each dose can be used in one of two ways. Puck dust dispersed on a plant creature within reach of the disperser forces the plant to succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw as if {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB} were cast upon it by the disperser. If the dust is dispersed on an inanimate shrub, it becomes an {@creature puck shrub|GrimHollowMG24|evil awakened shrub with an Intelligence and Charisma score of 3}. Three doses scattered on a tree make it an {@creature puck tree|GrimHollowMG24|evil awakened tree with an Intelligence and Charisma score of 3}. Either use of puck dust animates the plant for only 1 hour.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The veil between the world and the fey world is thin here. A dark fey spirit has corrupted this place.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The trees themselves are hindering your steps. They are in cahoots with a fey spirit. Anything you say or do is probably sensed by the spirit. Your senses might become targeted by the spirit. Do not trust anything you see.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: You are within the domain of a puck, pitiful creatures who scorn humanity and dominate nature. It uses plants as its weapons and concealment as its defense. Finding it may prove difficult, as the forest will protect it, but once found, it is frail.

entries.name: A Puck's Lair
entries: Soil within a puck's lair occasionally twinkles as if filled with sparkling fertilizer. Many of the trees and plants are likely to be the puck's thralls, and allied plant creatures might also dwell there. Within the lair, only creatures of the puck's choice leave tracks. Tracking such creatures is possible only with magic.

A puck makes their hidden home in small crevices beneath the interlaced roots of plant thralls. These roots act as labyrinthine hallways connecting all parts of the grove, which the puck uses to sneak around. While hidden in this maze, the puck whispers to the trees and telepathically commands them. Hiding and commanding the plants to protect the puck is crucial, for it knows that despite its great power, it is physically frail.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the puck shrub remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a thorny shrub.

action.name: Brambles
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Slashing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the puck shrub can halve the attack's damage and cause the target to have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). Until the grapple ends, the puck shrub can't make Brambles attacks against another target.

action.name: Hurl Thorns
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 3}, Range 30/60 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the puck tree remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a tree.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The puck tree deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d6 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the puck tree can halve the attack's damage and cause the target to have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 15}). The puck tree can grapple up to two creatures at a time.

action.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 7}, range 30/60 ft. {@h}32 ({@damage 5d10 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Fling
entries: The puck tree throws a Medium or smaller creature it has {@condition Grappled|XPHB} up to 30 feet horizontally. The target takes {@damage 1d10} Bludgeoning damage per 10 feet it travels and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take the same damage and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

reaction.name: Deadfall
entries: {@actTrigger} The puck tree is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. {@actResponse}—{@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 15- foot long, 5-foot wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Bludgeoning damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Acid damage.

action.name: Spit
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4}, range 10/30 ft. Hit:7 ({@damage 2d6}) Acid damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}. First {@actSaveFail} The target has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that takes an action to pour water on the spit grants the target {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its saving throws. Subsequent Failures: The target takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Acid damage.
While all slugs and such slick sliders are creepy, one type in particular transforms other creatures to something even more disgusting.

entries.name: Repulsively Quick
entries: Slithering along faster than you'd expect on a glistening trail as clumpy and green as plague victim's snot, the putrefaction slug's brownish-red bodies writhe unnaturally, as if their innards are itching to escape. Their slithering mass vibrates and shakes loose a strange and dusty yellow miasma just before they spit, emitting a sulfuric stench.

entries.name: Fates Worse than Death
entries: Slugs target their victims with bile-colored spit, causing unfortunates to dissolve in a matter of moments. A slug's hunger is also its weakness. Once they've spewed their digestive juices and flesh begins to putrefy, a slug's instincts take over, and it begins to feed. That's not good for the victim, but the slug focuses on little other than the eating, which is an excellent time to strike for the kill.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Putrefaction slugs ignore what they can't devour, making any treasure they possess incidental. But the glands that generate their digestive acid are prized by alchemists.

Removing an intact slug gland requires a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check. Once removed, the gland must be stored in alcohol or similar preservative agents. Using four such glands, a person can create a more potent version of acid that renders a target that takes damage from the acid have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage until the end of the thrower's next turn.

These enhanced acids are called {@item slugger (vial)|GrimHollowMG24|sluggers}, cost 40 GP, and weigh the same as a standard {@item Acid|XPHB|vial of acid}. Creating a {@item Slugger (vial)|GrimHollowMG24|slugger} requires proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} and a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence check to use them in a process that takes 4 hours. Failure creates normal acid, while failure by 5 or more renders a useless result.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A putrefaction slug spits acid. This acid can dissolve a creature into a puddle of goo.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The slug's digestive acid softens tissue, making it vulnerable to crushing and tearing. Water helps dilute this acid.

trait.name: Pox Euphoria
entries: The putrid giant rolls {@dice 1d4} and adds the result to ability checks other than Intelligence checks, and saving throws other than Constitution saving throws.

trait.name: Weeping Pox
entries: A Humanoid that comes within 5 feet of the putrid giant or anything it has recently held is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 15}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} for 24 hours. {@actSaveFail} The target is infected with the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. Every 24 hours, the target repeats the save, suffering an {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure. This {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} can't be reduced until the disease is cured, and the disease can only be cured by magic.

Until the first {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level sets in, the target has sharpened senses and a sense of wellbeing. The target can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the result to any ability check or saving throw it makes, except saving throws to resist the disease.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The putrid giant makes two Greatclub attacks.

action.name: Greatclub
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}24 ({@damage 4d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is subjected to Weeping Pox.
Beware a giant with pustules and sloughing skin. Hill giants respond differently to the pox. It rots their flesh and instills them with deadly mania.

entries.name: Infected, Unrestrained
entries: {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} is deadly to most creatures, but it can manifest differently. When a hill giant becomes infected, the fever sharpens the senses and creates a manic euphoria that never dissipates. Pustules form, and the flesh necrotizes, some sloughing off in strips and patches, but the disease doesn't kill the giant. Accompanying exhilaration pushes the sick giant to greater violence and depravity.

The new flurry of mental activity impedes what little logic the giant had. This state makes the giant more arrogant. It believes no one can best it, physically or intellectually. Only death can convince the giant it's mistaken.

entries.name: Disease Seekers
entries: Putrid giants believe the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} is a boon. They seek out those who have the pox or died from it. The giants consume infected flesh, believing doing so bolsters their power. No evidence supports this view, but reasoning with a healthy hill giant would be a challenge.

Putrid giants kill and eat most other creatures. But their laziness competes with their depravity. A putrid giant might attract a following of {@creature Morbus Kobold|GrimHollowMG24|morbus kobolds}, who see the giant as a living representative of the Filth Grazer. This misbegotten clan serves the giant as further spreaders of its ailment, and the giant allows this service, likely eating only enough kobolds to keep the others servile.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A putrid giant is such a haven for the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} that its gear and trinkets pose risk of exposure to the disease. It's best to burn the body and flee the area the giant inhabited with care and haste. However, the possessions of those the giant killed are scattered about its lair.

A successful {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check allows one to carefully remove the brain of a putrid giant. This brain, if treated with 200 GP worth of magical components, can be turned into a meal for 4 people. For 8 hours after eating the brain, a creature gains {@dice 4d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A putrid giant looks like it's undead, but it's still living and under the strange power of the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. Contact with the giant can infect other creatures, as can touching objects the giant has recently handled.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: The strange effect the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} has on hill giants might mutate them even further, including giving them a high enough Intelligence to allow them to start casting spells and reasoning much better than normal. Imagine a hill giant chieftain who figures this out: they would seek out the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} for all of their followers!

spellcasting.name: Fear (3/Day)
headerEntries: The quiet one casts {@spell Fear|XPHB} (spell save {@dc 14}), requiring no Material components.

trait.name: Silent
entries: The quiet one emits a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} with the effects of a {@spell Silence|XPHB} spell. It does not require {@status Concentration|XPHB} and, if dispelled, the quiet one can restore it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The quiet one makes two Claw attacks and one Bite attack.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@dice 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Psychic damage. If the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it takes an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Psychic damage and the quiet one gains{@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the extra Psychic damage dealt.
When you can't hear anything, you've heard them coming.

entries.name: Horrifying Appearance
entries: A quiet one is horrifying to behold. They are vaguely humanoid with grey pebbled skin, a large ovoid head, sharp claws, and a massive, fanged maw.

entries.name: Silent Hunters
entries: Quiet ones always generate an aura of absolute silence.

entries.name: Feed On Fear
entries: Quiet ones eat fear and seek to panic their victims as much as possible before killing them.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The brain of a quiet one can be made into a meal for three people with a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence check by someone proficient with {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}. Consuming the brain within 24 hours of the quiet one's death gives the eater {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against effects that cause the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 week. Crafting this meal takes 2 hours and costs 20 GP.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Quiet ones are so named for the constant aura of silence they generate.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A quiet one has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Psychic and Thunder damage.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Quiet ones feed on fear and gain{@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from those with the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The rabenhex doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

action.name: Talons
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Slashing damage. If the target is cursed by a rabenhex's Hex, it takes an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Hex (Recharges when the Hex Ends)
entries: The rabenhex places a curse on a creature it can see within 60 feet. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against rabenhexes and hags. The curse lasts for 1 minute, until the target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or until the rabenhex attacks a different creature, has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or dies. If the rabenhex is {@condition Invisible|XPHB}, using this trait doesn't reveal its location.
Sing a song of rabenhex,
A hanging garlic braid,
Three and ten years bad luck
For those who never prayed.

entries.name: Bird of Ill Omen
entries: A rabenhex haunts the woods where witches are said to dwell. This ravenlike bird has black feathers tinged with flecks of red. Its beak and talons are also red, making it look bloody.

entries.name: Magical Gift
entries: Many believe killing a rabenhex brings bad luck, but much the opposite is true. Rarely, a rabenhex bears one golden feather. This enchanted feather is said to remove curses.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A rabenhex has a {@chance 10|10 percent chance|Rabenhex|The Rabenhex has a enchanted feather.|The Rabenhex has no special feathers.} of having an {@item Enchanted Feather|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)} growing from its body.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A rabenhex is swift in flight and doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A rabenhex can curse a creature within 60 feet of it. This curse makes it harder the rabenhex or hags it might serve

trait.name: Baneful Attack
entries: The raven of ill omen has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature with a bane from Affect Fortunes.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The raven of ill omen doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The raven of ill omen can mimic voices and other sounds it has heard. A creature that hears the mimicked sounds can tell they are an imitation with a successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The raven of ill omen makes one Beak attack and one Talons attack.

action.name: Beak
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Talons
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Slashing damage.

bonus.name: Affect Fortunes
entries: The raven of ill omen chooses up to six creatures it can see within 60 feet. The raven assigns each creature a bane or boon for 1 minute, until the raven dies, or until it uses this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} again. These effects don't stack with similar effects, such as the Bane and Bless spells.

items.name: Boon
entries: The target can roll a {@dice d4} and add the result to each ability check and saving throw it makes for the duration.

items.name: Bane
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} The target must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the result from each ability check and saving throw it makes for the duration.
Ravens can be a sign of bad tidings, but their monarchs bring mischief and upheaval.

entries.name: Raven "Rulers"
entries: Ravens of ill omen are larger than normal ravens. A plume of feathers, red and white, and alabaster eyes set it further apart from its kin. These regal ravens also have magical influence over fortune. This prescience causes misfortune for the raven's enemies and good luck for fellow corvids.
Ravens are harbingers of misfortune. A raven of ill omen is the embodiment of this belief. When one appears, battlefield deaths increase, pestilence spreads quickly, and misery abounds.

entries.name: Cunning Deceivers
entries: Contrary to popular superstition, ravens of ill omen aren't beasts. These mischievous creatures are fey who actively spread misfortune. They influence ravens and sometimes ally with other fey, drawing unwitting creatures into traps and nasty schemes through mimicry and other tricks.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Many people believe the crown feather of the raven of ill omen bestows good fortune, while others insist the opposite is true. Someone can sit with such a feather for 1 hour and attempt to attune to it, making a {@dc 10} Charisma check. On a success, the feather acts as a {@item Stone of Good Luck|XDMG}. On a failure, the feather seems to be a {@item Stone of Good Luck|XDMG}, but the GM secretly subtracts 2 from ability checks and saving throws after the player adds the "luckstone's" +1. The ill-fortune feather is cursed. Until the curse is removed, the attuned user can't discard it. The good-fortune feather crumbles to dust if the user rolls a 1 on a Death Saving Throw. The ill-fortune feather crumbles, ending the curse, if the user rolls a 20 on a Death Saving Throw.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The raven of ill omen is a creature that can speak and mimic sounds and voices. Those the raven deems enemies might quickly find that luck has abandoned them.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: This raven is no beast, but rather a devious fey keen to bestow misfortune on mortals.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The Remorseful Storm casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

trait.name: Adamant Panoply
entries: Any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against the Remorseful Storm becomes a normal hit.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The Remorseful Storm can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Relentless Zeal
entries: The first time the Remorseful Storm is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed, it does not fall unconscious and it does not die. Instead, it is filled with an enduring radiance that allows it to keep fighting with the following benefits until the end of its next turn:

items: The Remorseful Storm sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius.

At the start of each of the Remorseful Storm's turns, each creature within 5 feet of it takes 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage. A creature that touches the Remorseful Storm or hit it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage.
The Remorseful Storm has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on weapon attacks.

entries: At the end of its turn, if the Remorseful Storm hit a creature with a melee attack, the Remorseful Storm regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}. Otherwise, it dies.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Remorseful Storm makes two Greataxe attacks

action.name: Greataxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 14}, reach 10 ft. {@h}35 ({@damage 4d12 + 9}) Force damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Lightning damage.

action.name: Lightning Strike {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, each creature within 10 feet of a point the Remorseful Storm can see within 500 feet. {@actSaveFail} 54 ({@damage 12d8}) Lightning damage, and the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

reaction.name: Retaliate
entries: {@actTrigger} The Remorseful Storm takes damage from a creature within 10 feet of it. {@actResponse} The Remorseful Storm makes a melee attack against that creature.
If you venture into the Unterland province and hear a sound that's a terrible cacophony of thunder and wailing—RUN.

entries.name: A Storm Unleashed
entries: This storm giant took up Maligant's call to arms during the war between the Four Divines. Once part of a celestial host, it's now a lost veteran and skilled holy warrior who hunts down fiends and anyone who gets in its path. People who've seen it call it the "Remorseful Storm."

entries.name: Depraved Paladin
entries: Driven by a strict adherence to its own unmoored sense of morality, it tracks down and faces its rivals at any cost. It wanders the Unterland province, seeking to find and destroy followers of Tormach. And often it believes everyone follows Tormach.

entries.name: Rampages of Regret
entries: The Remorseful Storm's morals have become corrupted by its solitude as deeply as its sorrow has intensified. Its remorse for divine loss results in lashing out, while often apologizing as it does.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who collects the tears of the Remorseful Storm can drink the liquid, which acts as a {@item Potion of Lightning Resistance|XDMG}.

With a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check, a proficient alchemist can spend 8 hours and use 100 GP of components to create a {@item Grenade of Remorse|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The Remorseful Storm seeks to battle fiends and is reluctant to believe that anything it encounters isn't complicit with them.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Due to its storm giant nature, the Remorseful Storm has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Lightning and Thunder, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Remorseful Storm cannot be killed as long as it is still landing blows on its enemy.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: The Remorseful Storm might gain followers who share its mania for chasing down supposed evil-doers. It might provide a benefit similar to its Relentless Zeal to them, giving the characters a hint at what they might face later.

trait.name: Hold Breath
entries: The restless lumberer can hold its breath indefinitely while conscious.

trait.name: Lurker's Patience
entries: The restless lumberer has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks it makes while motionless.

trait.name: Vice Grip
entries: Any creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the restless lumberer also has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The restless lumberer makes three attacks, using Grab or Slam in any combination.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 15 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 3d10 + 7}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Grab
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 15 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 2d10 + 7}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 22}). The lumberer can grapple up to two creatures at a time, and can't make Slam attacks against other targets with a hand it is using to grapple.

reaction.name: Psychic Scar
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 20}, one or two grappled creatures. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Psychic damage, and the target is {@condition Stunned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} No damage.
Huge thumps from across the street woke me. All night long, I swear. Next day, I go to say something to the noisy thumpers. Everyone there was dead, and strange arcane marks covered the walls.

entries.name: Dream Protectors
entries: Lanky, long-limbed, and stooped, a restless lumberer is a giant scarred by contact with the Aetheric Kindred. Restless lumberers once cast their slumbering minds abroad into the far reaches of the multiverse, communing with cosmic beings in somnolent bliss. This left them vulnerable to the nightmares of the Kindred as they waged war on the gods of Etharis, which shattered the minds of the restless lumberers.

Having seen cosmic horrors firsthand, some restless lumberers seeks to thwart the Kindred's influence by denying them the dreams of mortals. Other restless lumberers work to restore the Kindred, seeing resistance to their immense power as pointless. They collect strange sleepers for this purpose.

entries.name: Literal Sleepers
entries: The most infamous restless lumberer dwelt in the abandoned vaults of Stehlenwald in the Rauland province of the Bürach Empire. Other cities house restless lumberers, but they largely keep to themselves. The different factions are, however, known to fight each other, causing minor earthquakes and sinkholes. They lair in old cellars, bricked-up vaults, and derelict tunnels, often burying themselves in sleepless hibernation, contemplating the collections of strange objects and items of eldritch significance taken from dreamers' homes that predict when the Kindred's dreams seep into the nightmares of mortal sleepers.

entries.name: No Sleep for the Dreamers
entries: Lumberers who fight against the Kindred keep dreamers awake by rattling foundations, knocking on walls, or shouting to prevent them from sleeping until the dreams pass. They may kidnap sleeping people out of their beds, taking them to their lair. Restless lumberer devotees of M'rorcameleth are particularly fond of people with peculiar or mystical dreams.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A restless lumberer's lair is home to its collection of arcane curios and eldritch paraphernalia and might contain any number of spell components, spell foci, or magic scrolls.

The brain of a restless lumberer has been molded and washed over by countless waves of psychic energy from the Aetheric Kindred. A proficient jeweler can take the powdered brain of a restless lumberer and combine it with 1000 GP of components to create a {@item Ring of Nightmares|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}. This requires 5 days of work and a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Local sightings report hearing houses groaning and rattling and feeling the ground thump with an irregular beat.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The merchants league found their secure vault empty recently, including their collection of ancient temple scrolls. The entire floor was gone and a gaping tunnel leading deep into the undercity left in its place.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Legend says the lumberer was once a dream-walking giant who witnessed a gods' death and now lurks in forgotten vaults beneath the city collecting interesting dreamers.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The horror regains 15 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of its turn. If the horror takes Fire or Radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the horror's next turn. The horror is destroyed only if it starts its turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and doesn't regenerate.

trait.name: Turn Resistance
entries: The horror has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

trait.name: Unerring Direction
entries: The horror knows the distance to and direction of the creature whose return to life spawned it, even if the creature and the horror are on different planes of existence. If the creature being tracked by the horror dies, the horror dies.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The horror makes three Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 13}, reach 10 ft. {@h}27 ({@damage 3d12 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Bone Storm
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 40- foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Piercing damage plus 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Necrotic damage, and the target has the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowPG24} condition {@homebrew |(see Grim Hollow Campaign Guide pg. 28)}. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.
Sometimes it's better to stay dead. Something always tries to balance the scales.

entries.name: Price to Be Paid
entries: A resurrection horror is spawned the midnight after a creature who died on unhallowed ground is returned to life. The horror seeks to return the resurrected creature to death.

entries.name: Swath of Destruction
entries: Resurrection horrors unerringly move toward the resurrected creature, no matter how far away they may be, killing anything that tries to interfere.

entries.name: Spawned of the Grave
entries: Resurrection horrors are massive undead built of the bones of many bodies and the unhallowed dirt the returned creature died upon.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The grave dirt of a resurrection horror can be refined to create a pouch of dirt that when sprinkled as an action works as a {@i Scroll of} {@spell Protection from Energy|XPHB|Protection from Necrotic Energy} and {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB} with a 30-minute duration. The process requires a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check by someone proficient in the {@skill Religion} skill who works for 8 hours and uses 300 GP worth of additional components.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Resurrection horrors appear when someone who died on unhallowed ground is later magically returned to life. The horror hunts down and attempts to kill the being returned to life.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Resurrection horrors have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold, Necrotic, and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Resurrection horrors can unleash a blast of bone shards and dirt that does Piercing and Necrotic damaged and causes those damage by it to bleed uncontrollably.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The returned hunter casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

spellcasting.name: Hunter Magic (3/Day)
headerEntries: The returned hunter casts {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} or {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Fey Touched
entries: The returned hunter has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions and magic that would impede its movement or put it to sleep.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The returned hunter makes three Shortsword attacks or two Longbow attacks.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Longbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5}, range 150/600 ft. Hit:7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Psychic damage.

bonus.name: Vanish
entries: The returned hunter takes the {@action Hide|XPHB} action.
Those taken by the fey come back changed. Rarely for the better.

entries.name: Escaped Fey Captives
entries: Powerful fey abduct mortals, dragging them into the fey realm to serve as entertainers, servants, or adopted family. Most mortals taken this way are never heard from again, but a rare few manage to escape the clutches of their fairy kidnappers and find their way back. These changed people, the returned, come back to a life that has moved on without them.

The returned cope with their trauma in many ways. Some wage a personal war against the fey, while others struggle to take back the life stolen from them. In either case, the returned passionately pursue their goals and recruit others to help.

entries.name: Irreversible Changes
entries: Mortals who spend extensive time in the fey realms change irreversibly. The most obvious signs are physical or cosmetic, such as iridescent irises or footsteps that sound like distant thunder, but the alterations run deeper. Magic of the fey realms seeps into the soul of a returned, whether they want it or not. Many returned enjoy these magical powers. Others limit their use of fey magic, afraid they might attract the attention of their abductors. A few turn their eldritch skills to revenge, including imparting a psychic resonance that allows weapons to harm the body and mind.

entries.name: Mutable Form
entries: The fear returned have about using magic has some foundation in fact. Each time a returned casts a spell, a cosmetic trait, such as eye color or the sound of the voice, changes randomly and permanently.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The bones, hair, and sinew of a returned retain magic antithetical to the fey. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} can spend 3 days working with these materials, along with reagents an alchemist recommends worth 250 GP. If the artisan succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check, they can build {@item Dimensional Shackles|XDMG} that work only on the fey.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Those abducted by the fey and later escape back to the mortal world are known as the returned. Time in the fey realms makes such people prone to cosmetic changes and able to use fey magic.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: An old story tells of a prince who was stolen by the fey only to fight his way back to his kingdom. After his return, he went decades without cutting his hair. When he died an old king, his daughter cut his hair and used it to bind the fey who long ago kidnapped her father.

name: Rime Hunger
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but can't speak

trait.name: Fed Fortitude
entries: For 1 minute after the rime hunger regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, when damage reduces the rime hunger to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can make a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Fire, Radiant, or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a successful save, the rime hunger drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 12}). The rime hunger can only grapple one target at a time.

action.name: Sapping Grasp
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 13}, one creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the rime hunger. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage, and the rime hunger regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the Cold damage dealt. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.
You almost feel sorry for them. Freezing to death is a bad way to go, but they did something to cause their state. And they hunger for warm flesh. I think you get my point.

entries.name: Rime-Covered Corpses
entries: Rarely straying far from where they died and never willingly wandering into areas of warmth and sunlight, rime hungers are frostcovered, sickly blue corpses that haunt frozen regions in continuous search for victims.

entries.name: Hungry Dead
entries: Rime hungers devour all forms of living flesh but crave that of sapient creatures. It's believed their undead state is a curse brought on by cannibalism they engaged in to stave off their original demise.

entries.name: Persistent Shamblers
entries: While they are slow and will not follow their prey into warm lands, rime hungers track prey with the persistence of the dead while in colder lands.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A rime hunger doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Rime hungers sometimes carry the treasures they had in life. Some sages claim a rime hunger tongue dissolves in a {@item Potion of Cold Resistance|XDMG}, doubling the potion's duration. However, many alchemists consider this claim to be bunk.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A rime hunger has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire and Poison.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: One should avoid the grasp of rime hungers. They can feed on the life and warmth of creatures they hold, which strengthens the rime hunger.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The rougaugh deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Spiney Defense
entries: A creature adjacent to the rougaugh that attacks it with a melee weapon attack takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Piercing damage, regardless of whether the attack hits or misses.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The rougaugh makes three attacks: one with its Headbutt and two with its Spines.

action.name: Head Butt
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Spines
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d6 + 6}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Spine Splinter {@recharge}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the rougaugh ({@condition Prone|XPHB} creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}). {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 5d10}) Piercing damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.
The rage of remembering its lost life quivers in the very spines of the great beast, and the evil intelligence that shines in its eyes can freeze your soul.

entries.name: Children of the Beast
entries: Rougaugh are mutated creatures that fell prey to the transformative powers of the Beast. These aberrations were once humanoids, but as they lay dying at the feet of the Beast, they were reborn into something out of a nightmare. They took a quadrupedal form, and their ribcages grew into vicious spines emerging from their backs. Yet their heads and faces still have a resemblance to their old selves.

entries.name: Beasts of Destruction
entries: Rougaugh are created by the Beast for the sole purpose of destroying and pillaging heavily populated areas. Imbued with an unholy strength, rougaugh can use their head to batter down doors or their spines to tear flesh from bone. They do not eat their victims, as they lap up the blood to sustain themselves.

entries.name: Filled with Rage
entries: The intelligence that was once present within the rougaugh has been horribly twisted. With hatred and madness fueling its actions, a rougaugh destroys anything put before it, but it also knows when to retreat from a battle it cannot win, using tactics seemingly beyond such a bestial creature.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The rougaugh's thick purple blood carries a powerful enhancement. Someone who gathers the blood from two rougaugh can create an {@item Oil of Sharpness|XDMG} by a proficient alchemist who succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. Crafting this item takes 16 hours and requires 400 GP of components.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The spines of the rougaugh were what is left of its ribcage before its transformation, and these spines can be expelled with great force to damage foes.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: It is rumored that rougaugh were once humanoids who died in the presence of the Beast, and now they seek to destroy anything natural and beautiful in the world.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: The rougaugh has a natural defense in its spines, making attacking one in melee combat a dangerous proposition.

trait.name: Brute
entries: A weapon deals two extra dice of its damage when Runa hits with it (included in her attack).

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: Runa is immune to any effect that would alter her form.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
entries: If Runa fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Rejuvenation
entries: If destroyed while her memento skull remains intact, Runa's body reforms in {@dice 2d4} days, regaining all her {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Her new body appears within 5 feet of the memento skull.

trait.name: Turn Immunity
entries: Runa is immune to effects that Turn Undead.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: When not wearing armor, Runa's {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 10 + her Dexterity modifier + her Constitution modifier. She can use a {@item Shield|XPHB} while gaining this benefit.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Runa uses Stunning Presence and makes four attacks with {@item Coldrazor|GrimHollowMG24}. She can use Wall of Fire in place of one attack.

action.name: Coldrazor (+3 Handaxe)
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 15}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d6 + 8}) Slashing damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Cold damage. {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}: 32 ({@damage 7d6 + 8}) Slashing damage plus 24 ({@damage 8d6}) Cold damage. {@hom} Coldrazor returns to Runa's hand immediately after being thrown

action.name: Stunning Presence
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 120-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from Runa that is aware of her. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute. If the target succeeds on its save or the effect ends for it, it is immune to Runa's Stunning Presence for 24 hours.

action.name: Wall of Fire {@recharge 5}
entries: Runa casts {@spell Wall of Fire|XPHB} (level 9 version, spell save {@dc 18}). This special version of the spell lasts until the start of Runa's next turn and doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

reaction.name: Rampage
entries: {@actTrigger} Runa reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a Coldrazor attack. {@actResponse} Runa can move up to her {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and makes a Coldrazor attack. Special: Runa regains her {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} before and after using this ability.

reaction.name: Retaliate
entries: {@actTrigger} Runa takes damage from a creature within 5 feet of her. {@actResponse} Runa makes a melee weapon attack against that creature.

legendary.name: Attack
entries: Runa makes a {@item Coldrazor|GrimHollowMG24} attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Runa moves up to her {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

legendary.name: Curse of Cowardice
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 18}, one {@condition Stunned|XPHB} creature Runa can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed. While {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws and takes an extra 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage from Runa's weapon attacks. This effect ends when the creature is no longer {@condition Stunned|XPHB}. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Runa can't use this action again until the start of her next turn.

legendary.name: Siphon Vitality {@recharge}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from Runa. {@actSaveFail} 39 ({@damage 6d12}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.
Pull up a chair and hear the story of Runa Banasár. She proved that with enough willpower, you can overcome the cold of death as easily as the cold of the North.

entries.name: Revered Leader
entries: Runa Banasár was the leader of a northern tribe in time long forgotten. She lived for the thrill of the hunt, and her rare skills kept her clan fed for many years. Runa grew bored hunting wild game and left her home many times, exploring farther and farther to find bigger challenges. She returned home months or years later with the trophies from countless monsters and beasts.

entries.name: Path to Undeath
entries: During her travels, Runa learned the ritual to become a {@creature Memori Lich|GrimHollowMG24}. She feared aging and death. To become immortal and avoid frailty, Runa was willing to do whatever was required. She eventually slaughtered her clan to become a lich and maintain that status. Runa still travels the world, looking for fierce enemies and souls to maintain her undeath.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: "I can conquer anything, including death."

entries.name: Bond
entries: "My strength has carried me from life to immortality. I'll meet any challenge."

entries.name: Flaw
entries: "I'm no coward. I'll never back down from a fight."

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Runa's prized possession is her {@item +3 Handaxe|XDMG}, which she calls {@item Coldrazor|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. From her wanderings, she also carries trinkets worth at least 10,000 GP whether in raw value or to collectors.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Runa Banasár belonged to the Stál clan and was one of the most powerful warriors who ever walked the North. Her axe, {@item Coldrazor|GrimHollowMG24}, is almost as legendary as she is.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Folklore says that, because of her cruel slaughtering of her kin, Runa sacrificed her shapechanging ability and instead channels death and fiery rage. In fact, her form is unchangeable.

trait.name: Desert Hardened
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against {@hazard Dehydration|XPHB}, thirst, and hunger, and it needs half as much food and water as a normal creature of its size. Also, the giant is adapted to {@hazard Extreme Heat|XDMG} and {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG|Cold}.

trait.name: Desert Stride
entries: The giant ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} due to sand, rubble, or similar debris.

trait.name: Sand Camouflage
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB} in sandy or sandstone terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant makes two attacks, using Longsword or Rock in any combination.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}19 ({@damage 3d8 + 6}) Slashing damage, or 22 ({@damage 3d10 + 6}) Slashing damage if wielded with two hands.

action.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, reach 60/240 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
At least if you die in a sandstorm, you don't end up spending your time in chains, serving the whims of wicked giants.

entries.name: Wasteland Masters
entries: Sand giants live in nomadic tribes, each ruled by a monarch and spiritual leaders dubbed callers. They scavenge materials from anything left in the desert, and they rob and hunt as they move from one oasis to the next. Sand giant raiders rarely kill creatures the giants can force to labor for the tribe. But death might be preferable to servitude in the wastelands.

entries.name: Hearty Navigators
entries: Born into the lands of shifting dunes, sandstorms, and unforgiving temperature extremes, sand giants have adapted to survive. They navigate with all their senses and rarely become lost. A lifetime of crossing shifting dunes makes sand giants nimble in rough terrain. Sand giants can also go for long periods without food and water, and their skin is conditioned to natural heat and cold.

entries.name: Traveled Traders
entries: Sand giants travel far to pursue trade. They respect the laws of the lands they journey in, but they believe they are entitled to anything they can win through might and skill. A sand giant avoids costly battles, however, whether the price is being banned from a trading hub or death at the hands of a stronger foe.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Sand giants value shows of wealth, and they carry their belongings in ornate packs. Every sand giant has valuable personal effects worth at least 100 GP in their packs.

Sand giants are also expert cartographers, carrying detailed maps of the areas that they travel. A sand giant monarch carries maps worth up to 500 GP. Some might be more valuable to anyone interested in mapmaking, trade, or travel. One or more of these maps might show locations of potential treasure, such as ancient ruins in the desert.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Having adapted to the hot desert, sand giants are inured to many of its travails, from temperature swings and too little sustenance to {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Their coloration and skill make them good at hiding in sandy landscapes despite their size.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Sand giants enslave weaker creatures they encounter, forcing them to cook, clean, and haul spoils.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: {@creature Efreeti|XMM|Efreet} have a long history of enslaving sand giants. In retribution, sand giants attack {@creature Efreeti|XMM|Efreet} on sight and leave no survivors.

trait.name: Desert Hardened
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against {@hazard Dehydration|XPHB}, thirst, and hunger, and it needs half as much food and water as a normal creature of its size. Also, the giant is adapted to {@hazard Extreme Heat|XDMG} and {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG|Cold}.

trait.name: Desert Stride
entries: The giant ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} due to sand, rubble, or similar debris.

trait.name: Sand Camouflage
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB} in sandy or sandstone terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant makes three attacks. It can replace one attack with War Command even if the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} is not recharged.

action.name: Scimitar
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}20 ({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 10}, reach 60/240 ft. {@h}20 ({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

bonus.name: War Command {@recharge 5}
entries: The giant chooses an ally of CR 9 or less that can hear and understand it, commanding it to attack a creature the giant attacked this turn. The ally can use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against the designated creature, adding the giant's {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the damage roll.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The giant casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):
footerEntries: 3/Each Day (Level 5 Versions)

trait.name: Desert Hardened
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against {@hazard Dehydration|XPHB}, thirst, and hunger, and it needs half as much food and water as a normal creature of its size. Also, the giant is adapted to {@hazard Extreme Heat|XDMG} and {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG|Cold}.

trait.name: Desert Stride
entries: The giant ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} due to sand, rubble, or similar debris.

trait.name: Sand Camouflage
entries: The giant has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB} in sandy or sandstone terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant makes three attacks, using Greatclub or Sun Bolt in any combination.

action.name: Greatclub
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Sun Bolt
entries: {@atkr rs} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 4d6}) Radiant damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks and can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the end of the giant's next turn.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The scream thief can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

action.name: Life Drain
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d8}) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by an amount equal to half the damage taken.

action.name: Silence the Living {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}, a Humanoid within 30 feet of the scream thief. {@actSaveFail} 19 ({@damage 3d12}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, the target can't vocalize a sound of any kind. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

reaction.name: Fragment the Spirit
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature is killed by the scream thief. {@actResponse} The target's spirit rises as 3 ({@damage 1d6}) psychic fragments in the nearest unoccupied space to its corpse. The fragments are under the scream thief's control.

It appeared from the darkness: a faceless wraith whose outstretched arms sought purchase on my mortal frame. In desperation, I cried to my companions for aid, but my voice was silent. When it stole my words, I knew my doom was at hand.

entries.name: Retribution
entries: A scream thief springs forth when a human dies while stopping another creature from fulfilling an important goal. The phantom is cursed to an eternal undeath of having memories lie torturously out of reach, but the weight of their desire to remember their lives incites violence against mortals who intrude on their immortal prison.

entries.name: Cursed Locations
entries: The site of their death is tainted with hate and regret. Psychic fragments, souls of the creatures the scream thief has killed, linger nearby, taunting the spirit with nonsensical murmurings.

entries.name: Spiritual Victims
entries: When a scream thief kills an intelligent creature, tortured fragments of its spirit linger as vaporous orbs. The touch of these haunting forms withers the flesh, potentially adding another death to a cursed location.

entries.name: Uncanny Voices
entries: Psychic fragments call to the living. They yearn to join their fractured essence with a complete soul. They utter nonsensical words or phrases once spoken in life.

entries.name: Maddening Gatherings
entries: When a scream thief lingers in one location, the fragments of the many spirits it has killed can swarm together, creating a frightening ghostly orb. A mind-numbing chattering of the individual fragments can confound the unwary.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The bones of a mortal transformed into a scream thief remain imbued with its undead aura. A skilled magic item crafter using 200 GP of magical regents, and spending at least 5 days of effort, can create a {@item Wand of Silence|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)} if they succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

A spellcaster can capture a psychic fragment's essence before it dissipates after death. The spellcaster requires a container worth at least 100 GP. Anyone who succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check can capture a portion of the defeated psychic fragment. The container can store up to 10 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} worth of undead essence for 8 hours before they dissipate.

As a Magic action, a container holding this spiritual essence can be thrown up to 20 feet, shattering on impact. All creatures within 5 feet of the broken container must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. A failed saving throw results in {@dice 1d4} Necrotic damage per {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Die of essence stored, while a success deals half as much damage.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The scream thief and psychic fragments have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic and Poison damage. They are also resistant to Acid, Cold, and Fire damage.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The touch of a scream thief drains life that magic cannot heal; only time and rest can.
A scream thief remains trapped in its place of death, often accompanied by spirit fragments of the creatures it has killed.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The psychic fragment can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The psychic fragment can mimic a single word or phrase it spoke in life. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

action.name: Withering Touch
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) Necrotic damage.

name: Psychic Fragment Swarm
languages: can repeat one phrase it knew in life

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The swarm can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Maddening Voices
entries: The swarm constantly emits a babble of words and phrases spoken in life by its many undead spirits. A creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the swarm is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave wis} {@dc 12}. {@actSaveFail} The creature has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The creature is immune to Maddening Voices for 24 hours.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa. The swarm can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain{@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

action.name: Withering Touch
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}21 ({@damage 6d6}) Necrotic damage, or 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage if the swarm has the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Shadow Shape
entries: In {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, the shadow mauler can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

trait.name: Sunlight Vulnerability
entries: While in sunlight, the shadow mauler loses its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}. It also has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The shadow mauler makes two Bite attacks.

action.name: Bites
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 10 ft. {@h}19 ({@damage 3d10 + 3}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Shadow Escape
entries: In {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, the shadow mauler can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
The worst monsters are those you don't see coming.

entries.name: Shadow Predator
entries: Shadow maulers are weird predators with multiple eyes and multiple fanged mouths that can extend from the body on ephemeral flesh. They conceal themselves in the dark, waiting to kill any living creature that crosses their path. Cruel and calculating, a shadow mauler prefers to attack creatures alone or isolated from a group.

entries.name: Born to Darkness
entries: Sunlight is the bane of a shadow mauler. The monsters might have originated from a place without such light. They dwell in lightless spots to avoid sunlight, which hinders their abilities, preventing them from being effective hunters.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The ephemeral flesh of a shadow mauler is a silklike substance that appears to be made of shadow. Someone who has proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB} can fashion a {@item Cloak of Elvenkind|XDMG} from this material. Doing so takes 3 days and other materials worth 50 GP. This cloak loses its magic if exposed to sunlight for 8 hours or more.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Shadow maulers are most potent in shadows. In sunlight, they become more solid and easier to hurt. They also have a hard time seeing, fighting, escaping, and hiding.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The shadow mauler weakness to sunlight extends to a {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The Shadowsteel ghoul has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Shadowsteel Coat
entries: The ghoul is coated in metal armor made of Shadowsteel.

trait.name: Shadowsteel Hunger
entries: The Shadowsteel ghoul has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures carrying or wearing Shadowsteel.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Shadowsteel ghoul makes two Claw attacks.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Necrotic damage. A cursed target must make an Escalation Check. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and it isn't already cursed, roll {@dice 1d4} to determine which curse it is afflicted with: 1–2 {@spell Curse of Damned Aging|GrimHollowPG24}, 3–4 {@spell Curse of Foul Blight|GrimHollowPG24}. {@homebrew |(See Grim Hollow Campaign Guide for information on curses and escalation.)}
Shards of dark metal pierce the skin of the foul creature. The metal pushes out from within the abomination rather than the other way.

entries.name: Shadowsteel Toxicity
entries: Cursing an enemy requires an enormous amount of work and personal power. However, these efforts are for naught without the inclusion of the forbidden metal known as Shadowsteel. The frequent use of Shadowsteel takes its toll upon the mage handling it. In using it, the mage binds their soul, a bit at a time, to the energies of the fell metal. Those who use Shadowsteel can end up feeling its effects even after death.

entries.name: Cold Afterlife
entries: Sometime between a week and a year after a mage steeped in the use of Shadowsteel dies, their body rises, reinforced with shards of the metal. A Shadowsteel ghoul is no flesh-eater, but it resembles a ghoul with its gangly limbs and hairless, hunched body. Undeath has given the Shadowsteel ghoul a cruel nature and a strong desire to infect living creatures with the curses it carries. A Shadowsteel ghoul instinctively seeks out carriers of Shadowsteel, hoping to consume their supply of the substance.

entries.name: Ghast Form
entries: Once a Shadowsteel ghoul has amassed and absorbed enough Shadowsteel, the creature's physiology changes. The cursed metal brings back memories and mental acuity, allowing the fallen mage to reclaim some of their arcane power. The Shadowsteel shards embedded in the ghast's skin grow, forming gleaming plates. A miasma follows the creature, an extension of their magic resistance, diminishing the resistances of others around the ghast. More potent curses are transmitted through the ghast's claws.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Taking 1 hour to extract the shards of Shadowsteel from a Shadowsteel ghoul, someone can collect an amount worth 250 GP. A Shadowsteel ghast yields a quantity worth 500 GP.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Those who use Shadowsteel to power curses can become Shadowsteel ghouls upon death. These undead creatures seek out more of the metal. As the creature ages, it can regain a semblance of the arcane power it had in life, empowering similar creatures and cursing nearby foes.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The ghast casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit 5} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (3/Day)
headerEntries: The ghast casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Protective Magic (5/Day)
headerEntries: The ghast casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} or {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The ghast has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Shadowsteel Coat
entries: The ghast is coated in metal armor made of Shadowsteel.

trait.name: Shadowsteel Miasma
entries: Any creature of the ghast's choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of the ghast must roll {@dice 1d4} and subtract the result from any attack roll or saving throw it makes until the start of its next turn. Only one miasma can affect a given creature at a time. A creature that rolls a natural 20 on any attack roll or saving throw while in a Shadowsteel Miasma is immune to the miasma of any shadowsteel ghast for 1 hour.

trait.name: Turning Defiance
entries: The ghast and any shadowsteel ghouls within 30 feet of it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against effects that turn undead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ghast makes two Claw attacks. It can replace one attack with Grave Surge.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Necrotic damage. A cursed target must make an Escalation Check. If a target drops to 0 hit points due to this damage and isn't already cursed, it is afflicted with a random curse of the GM's choice from the {@filter Grim Hollow Player's Guide|spells|source=gh|subschool=curse}.

name: Shatter Corpse
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but can't speak

trait.name: Glass Spikes
