entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 12}, each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the thornhost. {@actSaveFail} 12 ({@damage 4d4 + 2}) Piercing damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The thornhust dies.
I always carry a knife around these parts. Some of the plants around here have poison thorns, sure, but others have something far worse.

entries.name: Grisly Puppeteers
entries: Often mistaken for zombies, thornhosts are parasitic plants that propagate through burrowing thorns. Once the thorns sink into flesh, they spread roots throughout the body, eventually controlling the still-living but brain-dead body of the host. This body withers as if from a wasting disease, and a thorny mass forms in the abdomen.

entries.name: Walking Bomb
entries: Once a thornhost has matured, the central mass swells and becomes unstable. The plant forces the body toward areas of high population, seeking to maximize the number of potential hosts. When its life becomes endangered, the plant bursts, shooting thorny seeds in all directions.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Thorns from a thornhost can be fashioned into {@item Dart|XPHB|Darts} or {@item Needle|XPHB|Blowgun Needles}. Each thornhost produces {@dice 4d4} thorns useful for this purpose. Someone proficient with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB} can make the darts or needles. A creature struck by one of these darts or needles must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw at the end of their next turn or take {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage as the semiliving thorn burrows in. A creature can prevent the extra damage by taking an action to remove the clinging dart point or needle. Each dart or needle functions this way only once and is ruined after use, its point missing.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A thornhost is a plant creature that infests and controls a humanoid body. The thornhost's thorns burrow into a victim to grow a new plant.

entries.name: {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: When in danger or among numerous potential hosts, the plant can explode, spreading thorns over a wide area.

action.name: Blood Drink
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage, and the trennensel attaches to the target. While attached, the trennensel uses its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to drain blood, and the target loses 2 ({@damage 1d4}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

The trennensel can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to detach the trennensel with a successful {@dc 9} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. It detaches automatically if it dies or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.
The cattle lows mournfully as the twisted shape, batlike and somehow childlike, drinks deeply of the bovine's blood. The farmer blanches before dropping his pitchfork and fleeing in terror.

entries.name: Flying Blood Drinkers
entries: Trennensels are batlike and hairless. They come in a variety of skin colors, and they can be mistaken for flying humanoids. They drink blood. Due to their lack of hair, they need to consume more to maintain body heat.

A trennensel prefers to feed on livestock, making the creatures pests to ranchers. They roost in caves by day and hunt at dusk. Trennensels spread out from their lair to feed, but careless spelunkers could rouse a whole colony of these creatures.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone proficient with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can mix refined trennensel guano with other reagents worth 25 GP to make one dose of {@item Oil of Slipperiness|XDMG}. Acquiring enough guano to refine, a few pounds, likely involves venturing into a trennensel colony cave. Making the oil requires 4 hours of work and a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A trennensel can't use its {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} while it has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

name: Unfinished
languages: understands all languages it knew in life but can't speak

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The unfinished casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, {@hit 8} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Semi-Corporeal
entries: Parts of the unfinished fade in and out of the Material Plane. The unfinished has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Prone|XPHB}, and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions. It makes another save at the beginning of its turns for an effect that causes any of these conditions, whether it normally allows a saving throw or not.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The unfinished makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage plus 17 ({@damage 3d8 + 4}) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is pushed 10 feet and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
The unfinished are angry ghosts akin to poltergeists, but partially solid, and throwing much bigger objects.

entries.name: Not Fully Manifested
entries: A creature known as an "unfinished" looks as it did at the moment of their death, but with parts of their body fading in and out of corporeality.

entries.name: Unfinished Business
entries: An unfinished is held on the mortal plane by its guilt over unfinished business.

entries.name: Strong Will
entries: An unfinished exerts its will, allowing it to move heavy objects, often using them as weapons.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: If an unfinished's unfinished business can be completed in the presence of the unfinished, it is bound to serve the one who aided it for 24 hours.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Like many Undead, unfinished have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic and Poison damage. They also have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, and Thunder.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: An unfinished is animated by guilt over unfinished business, but it promises to serve anyone for one day that it witnesses complete its undone task.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Unfinished can cast {@spell Bigby's Hand|XPHB|Arcane Hand}, {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, and {@spell Telekinesis|XPHB}.

name: Vessel Shard
languages: understands one national language and three others but can't speak

trait.name: Spirit Absorption
entries: When a creature dies or is destroyed within 30 feet of the vessel shard, the vessel shard absorbs part of the departing spiritual energy, regaining 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or the dead creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, whichever is less.

trait.name: Turn Resistance
entries: The vessel shard has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

trait.name: Unhallowed Aura
entries: Unless the vessel shard has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, it emits a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of desecration. Undead creatures of its choice in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} roll {@dice 1d4} and add that number to attack rolls and saving throws. Halve the number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} a living creature regains while within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

A Humanoid that dies in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} reanimates as a {@creature Zombie|XMM} at the start of its next turn, provided enough of its body is intact. The vessel shard controls this {@creature Zombie|XMM}.

action.name: Sepulchral Touch
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. or ranged 120 ft. {@h}28 ({@damage 8d6)}) Necrotic damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of the vessel shard's next turn, and each creature of the shard vessel's choice within 5 ft. of the target takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Putrefy {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in the vessel shard's Unhallowed Aura. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Necrotic damage, and the target takes another 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the ongoing damage on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

action.name: Shattered Spirits (1/Day)
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, each creature in the vessel shard's Unhallowed Aura. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage, and the target is cursed. While cursed, the target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by the amount of Necrotic damage taken until the curse ends. It also suffers one of the following delusions (roll {@dice 1d6}), or a similar delusion of the GM's choice:

rows: Only I matter. Others are disposable.
All other creatures should serve me.
Living beings are weak and not to be trusted.
No risk is too great for my personal glory.
I must never put myself in danger of dying.
To survive, I must eat only little creatures that are still alive.

entries: Every 24 hours, the target repeats the save, ending the curse on a success. {@actSaveFail} The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is further reduced by 10 ({@damage 3d6}). If this effect kills the target, it rises as a zombie under the vessel shard's control. The zombie approaches the vessel shard until it is in the vessel shard's Unhallowed Aura, attacking any creature that prevents it from doing so.

The curse can be removed by effects that turn undead or end possession. If the effect calls for a saving throw, the curse has a +4 bonus on its save. The curse can also be removed by keeping the target on hallowed ground and in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} for 24 hours, but the curse compels the target to escape these conditions if possible.

bonus.name: Consume Spirit
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, one Undead creature the vessel shard can see within 30 feet (this is considered an effect that turns undead). {@actSaveFail} The target loses 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and is destroyed if this effect reduces it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The vessel shard regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the amount the target lost.

reaction.name: Arcane Shield ({@recharge})
entries: {@actTrigger} The vessel shard is hit by an attack or fails a Dexterity saving throw. {@actResponse} The vessel shard adds 5 to its {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB|AC} against that attack or to the result of its saving throw.
This ornate vessel gives off cold menace as it hovers in the air among shambling corpses.

entries.name: Failed Lichdom
entries: Many necromancers dream of transcending death and entering lichdom, but only a handful attempt the process. Fewer still succeed. Of the failures, a tiny percentage become vessel shards, incomplete, damaged souls trapped within a lich's soul vessel.

entries.name: No Body, Many Bodies
entries: Unlike a complete lich, a vessel shard does not retain control of its original body. The entirety of its being is housed within the failure of a soul vessel. The vessel shard can see, hear, and smell out of this vessel, and it can fly for movement. But it has no corporeality beyond the confines of this vessel.

However, a vessel shard remains a fearsome commander of lesser undead, able to summon and bend them to its will. A vessel shard is rarely found without a small detachment of zombies, skeletons, ghouls, or the like serving it. A poetic student of undeath might consider these creatures to be the vessel shard's bodies, in a certain regard.

entries.name: A Hungry Soul
entries: Most people would agree that anyone who wishes to enter lichdom must be maladjusted. That said, magical mishaps that tear the would-be lich's soul into pieces and imprisons them in a damaged soul vessel create a form of obsession. Unlike liches, who can exist in relative peace and isolation for centuries, vessel shards are driven to kill and then consume the souls of living things.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: The vessel shard is undead; it requires no air, sleep, food, or drink.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: If the essence of a defeated vessel shard is dissolved in a {@item Holy Water|XPHB}, the water transforms into an elixir that can be poured into a corpse's mouth, acting as a {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} spell that requires no other components. The corpse understands anything asked of it in any language, and the corpse's responses can be understood by any who can hear it.
Also, a vessel shard usually contains a jewel that is flawed but still worth at least 50 GP.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion} or {@skill Arcana}):
entries: A vessel shard bolsters undead near it, making them better at fighting and more resistant.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion} or {@skill Arcana}):
entries: vessel shard can expel fragments of spirits to possess nearby victims. (Those who know this fact also know how to treat the cursed possession.)

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion} or {@skill Arcana}):
entries: A vessel shard can raise undead by various means. It can also consume the power of death to regain vitality.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: A vessel shard might be inconspicuous at first, hiding its true nature by seeming to be a bit of treasure from an area infested with undead. Unsuspecting characters might even carry it back to a populated area and sell it to a merchant. After a few days, the vessel shard could devastate that town, building a veritable undead army because of the characters' carelessness.

skill.special: Proficient in up to three skills from its past life

trait.name: Unnatural Life
entries: The vitebriate suffers none of the frailty of old age.

trait.name: Vitebriance
entries: While on the same plane of existence as a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by it, the vitebriate can reduce the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by 1 each day. This reduction lasts until the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition ends and the target rests for 7 days without this reduction.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The vitebriate makes two Dagger attacks.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Dominate Person
entries: The vitebriate casts {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} (save {@dc 13}), requiring no components and using Charisma as its spellcasting ability. Once the vitebriate chooses a target, it can't target other creatures with {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} for 24 hours. The spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}, but ends early if the vitebriate is killed or knocked {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} against its will (trancing or sleeping doesn't end the spell). If the target has been {@condition Charmed|XPHB} for at least 1 hour, it no longer repeats the save when it takes damage.

reaction.name: Life Shield (1/Day)
entries: {@actTrigger} The vitebriate takes damage. {@actResponse} The triggering damage is instead dealt to a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the vitebriate. Any damage in excess of the creature's remaining {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} is dealt to the vitebriate.
I swear I've seen that kid before, years ago, when I was just a kid myself! But she hasn't aged a day.

entries.name: Life Drinkers
entries: Vitebriates, sometimes called "life drinkers," are the result of horrible experiments or prayers answered by dark powers. When a mother loses a child to needless accident or horrible malice, or when a powerful mage seeks to bless an apprentice or servant with a longer life, a vitebriate is sometimes the result.

entries.name: Immortal Parasites
entries: A vitebriate looks like a humanoid —often a child—but that is merely an appearance. These monstrosities feed on the life force of other humanoids, masquerading as an innocent while dominating and feeding off the unsuspecting. They retain their look of youth and vigor, and they manifest the power to continue harvesting humanoids.

entries.name: Magical Control
entries: Vitebriates are capable of magically dominating humanoids. Often, these dominated people are forced to pose as a caretaker or invalid. The vitebriate uses it's thrall to interact with adults or blend into the fabric of a community.

entries.name: Memory and Forgetfulness
entries: Curiously, vitebriates have memories of their prior lives, except for any magical or martial skills. A talented wizard or powerful squire transformed into a vitebriate must start such pursuits anew if they wish to master such arts. On the other hand, musicians, conversationalists, acrobats—even doctors— all seem to be able to recall and use their prior skills without diminution.

entries.name: Haunted and Obsessed
entries: Vitebriates are haunted by their past lives and obsessed with reliving some small part of it. For example, a child who died of drowning and awoke as a vitebriate may be compelled to drown others or might simply feel drawn to live by water. Regardless, the greatest obsession of every vitebriate is always to feed and to control.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When a vitebriate dies, it crumbles into a swarm of harmless crawling roaches.

If these roaches are mixed with seawater, a Potion of {@spell False Life|XPHB} results. The creation of this potion can be completed with a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check by someone proficient with an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}. This process takes 1 hour.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: A vitebriate can only have a single thrall at a time and can transfer some of its damage to its thrall.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Vitebriates have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison, and they require a thrall to stay alive.

trait.name: Ethereal Sight
entries: The vooran can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane when on other planes, and vice versa.

trait.name: Etherealness
entries: The vooran lives entirely on the Ethereal Plane and can only enter other planes by possessing a Beast. It is not visible outside of the Ethereal Plane.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The vooran can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. It takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Familiar
entries: vooran can connect with another creature to serve as a familiar, forming a telepathic bond with its willing master. While the two are bonded, the master can sense what the vooran senses if they are within 1 mile of each other. When bonded, the master can see the vooran as a ghostly form.

action.name: Animal Possession (1/Day)
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 12}, one Beast of {@filter beast of CR 1/8 or lower|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&0;&1/8]|type=beast} that the vooran can see within 5 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target is possessed by the vooran. The vooran disappears, and the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and loses control of its body. The vooran now controls the body, but the target retains awareness. The vooran can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that specifically target Fey. The vooran's game statistics are the same, except it uses the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, as well as the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers.

The possession lasts for 1 hour, ending early if the body drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or the vooran ends it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When the possession ends, the vooran is forced back into the Ethereal Plane, and the target is immune to this vooran's Animal Possession for 24 hours. If an animal is killed while the vooran possesses it, the vooran must succeed on a {@dc 10} Charisma saving throw or it is permanently destroyed.
{@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this vooran's Possession for 24 hours.
When your pet stares at you, you never know if you are looking into the eyes of your beloved companion or the eyes of a vooran.

entries.name: Flesh Riding
entries: Vooran are uncontrollable incorporeal woodland spirits that experience the world by possessing small animals, causing those usually harmless creatures to behave strangely, even tamed ones.

entries.name: Familiars
entries: Voorans can serve as familiars, though they generally only do so for those who offer it different animals to inhabit.

entries.name: Ethereal Hedonist
entries: Voorans naturally inhabit the Ethereal plane and can only affect the mortal world for one hour a day while possessing a small animal; an hour they use to live life to the fullest.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: If a vooran is destroyed while possessing an animal, the animal's blood takes on an opalescent hue and gains momentary magical properties. If a living creature drinks the creature's blood within 1 minute of its death, it acts as a {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Vooran are fey spirits from the Ethereal Plane that possess small animals.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: Vooran are nearly indestructible on the Material plane and make excellent spies.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: A spellcaster capable of casting {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} can form a bond with a vooran.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The wandering head casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit 5} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Counterspell (2/Day)
headerEntries: The wandering head casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability in Spellcasting.

trait.name: Off Balance
entries: The wandering head has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wandering head makes one Bite attack and one Slam attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d4 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage.
Ugly brutes, aye, but one offered me a magic necklace to take care of a merchant what stiffed him on a deal, so they can't be all bad. Strangest thing though, I can't seem to take it off...

entries.name: All Head
entries: Wandering heads are grotesque beings that roam the wilderness in search of travelers to torment. The creature is a horse-sized head balanced on two spindly legs with arms that protrude from gaps in its teeth. Wandering heads carry sacks filled with objects they use in deceitful bargaining, always trying to twist the deal.

entries.name: Crafty Bargainers
entries: A wandering head's first instinct is to bargain. They approach and use divination magic to offer others what they need most. In exchange, the head asks for treasure or a favor. Cunning as they are, wandering heads attempt to trick others into committing an evil act or losing badly on the deal in some other way.

entries.name: Corrupted Giants
entries: Enuil Stonetongue, a follower of Malikir, once sought to turn hill giants to his master's service. The giants proved too dim to adequately follow orders, so Enuil vowed that if they could not make good use of their heads he would. His curse warped and twisted those giants into the first wandering heads. Enuil taught these heads wizardry.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A wandering head carries tools and trinkets to tempt travelers into making deals. At least one magic item can be found in the head's sack, although such items are often cursed.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Wandering heads are the warped heads of giants, detached and given new life.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: These monsters are highly intelligent and capable of wizardry.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Beware any deal a wandering head offers. They love tricking others into evil deeds.

trait.name: Artificial Form
entries: The wechselkind has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and is immune to disease. It doesn't need to eat, drink, or breathe.

trait.name: Childish Agility
entries: The wechselkind can move through the space of any creature larger than it.

trait.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries: The wechselkind deals an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the wechselkind that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and the wechselkind doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Faerie Glamour
entries: The wechselkind casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} (save {@dc 11}), requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. When it does so, it can disguise itself only as the child it was created to replace.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
entries: The wechselkind takes the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The wechselkind casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit 4} to spell attacks):

trait.name: Artificial Form
entries: The wechselkind has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and is immune to disease. It doesn't need to eat, drink, or breathe.

trait.name: Childish Agility
entries: The wechselkind can move through the space of any creature larger than it.

trait.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries: The wechselkind deals an extra 17 ({@damage 5d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the wechselkind that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and the wechselkind doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Faerie Glamour
entries: The wechselkind casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} (save {@dc 12}), requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. When it does so, it can disguise itself only as the humanoid child it was created to replace.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
entries: The wechselkind takes the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The wechselkind casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 6} to spell attacks):
footerEntries: 3/Day (Level 5 Versions)

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (2/Day)
headerEntries: The wechselkind casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (2/Day)
headerEntries: The wechselkind casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

trait.name: Artificial Form
entries: The wechselkind has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and is immune to disease. It doesn't need to eat, drink, or breathe.

trait.name: Childish Agility
entries: The wechselkind can move through the space of any creature larger than it.

action.name: Multiattack.
entries: The wechselkind makes three attacks, using Dagger or Force Ray in any combination.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Force damage.

action.name: Force Ray
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 6}, range 120 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d10}) Force damage.

action.name: Faerie Glamour
entries: The wechselkind casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}(save {@dc 11}), requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. When it does so, it can disguise itself only as the humanoid child it was created to replace.

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the weeping zombie to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a success, the weeping zombie drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

trait.name: Weeping Pox
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, a Humanoid that comes within 5 feet of the weeping zombie. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} for 24 hours. {@actSaveFail} The target contracts {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. The target repeats the save every 24 hours, suffering an {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure. This {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} can't be removed until the disease is cured with magic.

Until the first {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level sets in, the target has sharpened senses. Whenever the target makes an ability check or saving throw against anything other than the disease, it rolls a d4 and adds the result to its roll.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is subjected to Weeping Pox.

A mother clutches her three young daughters in the hallway, outside a bedroom where a male voice rants in gibberish. She lets a masked figure into the room. A shriek precedes silence. She thinks she has solved the problem, but a bigger problem will rise and return home.

entries.name: Evil Begets Evil
entries: Weeping zombies are the risen corpses of {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} victims murdered before the disease claimed their life. The evil enacted against them attracts death energy, and they rise with the need to spread the plague for revenge. They have no personality or memory of their former lives.

entries.name: Diseased Transformation
entries: Deep lesions score a weeping zombie, especially around the mouth. This orifice hangs open, dry and shriveled, and the zombie gasps unintelligible words as it moves. Once near a living body, the weeping zombie rushes in and attempts an embrace to spread the disease and consume flesh.
The transformation from the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} gives a weeping zombie more agility than other undead. A weeping zombie also rots much more slowly than regular zombies.

entries.name: Magic Contagion
entries: People who practice arcane magic can become a weeping zombie with some memory intact. These weeping lords can command weeping zombies and use them to extract revenge, even if the weeping lord doesn't remember why.
A weeping lord's eyes have rotted away, leaving streams of pus-like tears behind. In undeath, it needs no eyes to find the living.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A weeping zombie doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone proficient in {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB} can fashion the ashes of four weeping lords and other materials worth 500 GP into a glass jewel and necklace of precious metal, forming an {@item Amulet of Health|XDMG}. Doing so requires 10 days of work and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. Somebody must cast the bear's endurance version of {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} on the jewel three times during the process.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}):
entries: Rumors say that a person who was murdered for having the {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} might rise from the grave for vengeance.

name: Weeping Lord
languages: understands the languages it spoke in life but can't speak

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The weeping lord casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit 5} to spell attacks):

spellcasting.name: Shield (3/Day)
headerEntries: The weeping lord casts {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using the spellcasting ability from Innate Spellcasting.

trait.name: Command Weeping Zombies
entries: The weeping lord directs weeping zombies within 120 feet of it using a form of limited telepathy.

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the weeping zombie to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a success, the weeping zombie drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

trait.name: Weeping Pox
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, a Humanoid that comes within 5 feet of the weeping zombie. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24} for 24 hours. {@actSaveFail} The target contracts {@disease Weeping Pox|GrimHollowCG24}. The target repeats the save every 24 hours, suffering an {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure. This {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} can't be removed until the disease is cured with magic.

Until the first {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level sets in, the target has sharpened senses. Whenever the target makes an ability check or saving throw against anything other than the disease, it rolls a {@dice d4} and adds the result to its roll.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is subjected to Weeping Pox.

action.name: Grave Miasma
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5}, reach 50 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) Necrotic damage. The target is subjected to Weeping Pox and can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of the weeping lord's next turn.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the whelmer remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a pool of water.

trait.name: Freeze
entries: If the whelmer takes Cold damage, it partially freezes, reducing its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Undertow
entries: The whelmer's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is normal when it moves a {@condition Grappled|XPHB} target.

trait.name: Water Form
entries: The whelmer can enter a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 13}). Until this grapple ends, the target can't breathe and the whelmer can't Slam another target.

action.name: Illusory Distress (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The whelmer creates an illusion of a drowning Humanoid in a space it can see within 120 feet of it. The illusion seems completely real, including sounds, smells, and temperature. The whelmer can use its action to move the illusion to another spot in range and change its sensory aspects. The elemental can change minor aspects, such as sounds, without using an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, as creatures and objects can pass through it. A creature that uses its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to examine the image can determine that it's an illusion with a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.
Helping people is all well and good on dry land, but you won't see me diving to the rescue of anyone in the water. Not after last time.

entries.name: Illusory Lure
entries: A corrupted water elemental, a whelmer likes to lurk in or near a body of water close to areas inhabited by humanoids. When people pass, a whelmer creates the illusion of a drowning person. Rather than wait in the water, the whelmer might rest motionless on a path to a beach or lake, waiting to ensnare would-be rescuers.

entries.name: Fey Ties
entries: The whelmers' powers of illusion stem from fey ties. Some water elementals wanted to meddle in the realms of mortals. Curious about these strange creatures, fey saw a chance for mischief and taught these rogue elementals how to lure people with illusions.

entries.name: Elemental Nature
entries: A whelmer doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: If somebody casts {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} on the remains of a whelmer within 1 minute, someone proficient with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can boil the water down over 1 hour and add other materials worth 25 GP. If the alchemist succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check, the result is one {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Whelmers are evil elementals that drag their victims into water to drown them. These elementals are stealthy and lie in wait as still pools of water.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Whelmers lure their prey with illusions of drowning humanoids.

name: Witch Owl
languages: understands one national language but can't speak

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The witch owl doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The witch owl can mimic owl sounds and Humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they're imitations with a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The witch owl makes two attacks: one with its Bite and one with its Talons.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Talons
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 2d4 + 1}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed to become a witch owl.
This enormous owl's face looks strangely human, framed by long black hair. The rest of its body is all owl, its legs ending in large talons.

entries.name: Cursed Creation
entries: A witch owl is a vengeful creature, searching nightly to eat its fill of humanoids. Folklore says that the first witch owl was once a person punished for practicing magic.

This story might be true, but the condition is a curse that can affect anyone. Three days after suffering a scratch from a witch owl, feathers begin to grow on a victim's body. Each day, the unfortunate becomes more owl-like, until they completely transform seven days later. The transformation can be reversed with a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell up to nine months after it takes hold, at which point only a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell can reverse the curse.

entries.name: Patient Hunters
entries: Witch owls often hunt alone at night. They attract curious prey by hooting and mimicking voices, encouraging followers for several miles. Hopeful folk might think the witch owl is leading them to treasure or some other good. Most are instead lured to the witch owl's nest and slain.

Witch owls also have long memories. If prey escapes, the witch owl searches for weeks to make the kill. If its nest is disturbed, it tracks interlopers for many miles, waiting for an opportunity to attack.

entries.name: Odd Followers
entries: The stories and mystery of witch owls have led to a small following of cultists, who believe that worship might bestow them feathered wings. These cultists have been known to kidnap others as offerings to witch owls, leaving victims at nests as a sacrifice.

entries.name: Aged Power
entries: Some witch owls live long enough to learn how to mimic their prey and become a witch owl hexta, mastering the ability to draw on old magic to appear human. These illusions don't make the witch owl capable of speech, so the monster often beckons for help. The wisest of these hextas use others, such as cultist sacrifices, to trick rescuers to coming to the hexta's nest.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone proficient with an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} or {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can grind the talons of a witch owl into powder and combine them with herbs to create a paste. Creating the paste takes a successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check and 4 hours of work. Eating the paste as an action grants the effects of {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} for 3 hours.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A witch owl can be found hunting at night. During the day, they usually hide in their lairs.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Stories tell of people becoming witch owls after surviving an attack by one of these monsters.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Older, wiser witch owls can disguise themselves with illusions.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Any creature might become a servant of a witch owl—magical compulsion is not needed. An entire hamlet might serve a witch owl hexta nesting in an old church spire.

name: Witch Owl Cultist
languages: One national language and one other language

trait.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries: The witch owl cultist deals an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the cultist that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, and the cultist doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

bonus.name: Nimble Escape
entries: The witch owl cultist takes the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

name: Witch Owl Hexta
languages: understands one national language but can't speak

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The witch owl hexta doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Keen Hearing and Sight
entries: The witch owl has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on hearing or sight.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The witch owl can mimic owl sounds and Humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they're imitations with a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The witch owl makes two attacks: one with its Bite and one with its Talons.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Talons
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave cha} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed to become a witch owl.

action.name: Illusory Appearance
entries: The witch owl casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} (save {@dc 12}), requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Keen Hearing and Smell
entries: The wolfentroika has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

trait.name: Shared Life
entries: Each of the wolfentroikas in a trio shares life. If the wolfentroika starts its turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and within 100 feet of another member of its trio that has 1+ {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the wolfentroika regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}. If a wolfentroika is at 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and at least one member of its trio is alive, the wolfentroika can die only if its body is destroyed in such a way that only the {@spell True Resurrection|XPHB} spell or similarly powerful magic could restore it to life.

trait.name: Shared Mind
entries: Each of the wolfentroikas in a trio shares consciousness. While within 100 feet of one another, if one wolfentroika is aware of something, all three are. The wolfentroika can have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} conditions only if the other two succumb to the same condition or are more than 100 feet from the wolfentroika. When one wolfentroika recovers from one of these conditions or moves within 100 feet of an affected sibling, each other trio member within 100 feet recovers.

trait.name: Trio Tactics
entries: The wolfentroika has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the wolfentroika's trio is within 5 feet of the creature.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Acid damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Spit
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4}, range 30 ft. {@h}16 ({@damage 4d6 + 2}) Acid damage.

reaction.name: Stay Down
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 5 feet of the wolfentroika stands up, ending the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actResponse} The wolfentroika makes an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} against that creature.
Three wolves attacked in unison, and we focused our attacks on the one we thought was the leader. But it refused to die no matter how many times we hit it.

entries.name: Beast's Corruption
entries: The mutative powers of the Beast spawn terrible creatures, but one of the more unusual is the wolfentroika. When the Beast corrupts a wolf carrying unborn pups, the wolf gives birth to triplets. Born strong, tough, malevolent, and clever, the trio eats their way out of their mother. Then, they grow to enormous proportions.

entries.name: Three Bodies, One Soul
entries: The three wolves share life force and awareness. They don't willingly stray more than 100 feet from one another, and if forced to do so, their primary goal becomes ending this separation. This supernatural relationship means that all three must be slain within moments of one another, or none of them can die. Similarly, the three resist magic that can only affect one or two of them.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The acid glands of a wolfentroika trio contain magic. Someone with proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill succeeding on a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check can harvest these glands within 1 hour of death. Somebody proficient with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} can use the acid from all three wolfentroikas from one trio to create a {@item Potion of Life Sharing|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}. Making the potion takes 1 day of work and reagents worth 200 GP, and the alchemist must succeed on a {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check to create the potion.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Where the presence of the Beast has been rumored, mutated wolves with acidic saliva might be encountered. These giant monstrosities come in trios, and they are notoriously difficult to kill.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
entries: A wolfentroika trio works perfectly together, better than a wolf pack.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Wolfentroikas share life force and consciousness. What one knows, the others know. To kill one, you must kill all three within seconds. To affect one with certain types of magic, you must affect all simultaneously.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While motionless, the wood weird is indistinguishable from a clump of beautiful wildflowers.

action.name: Restful Spores
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 10}, one creature the wood weird can sense within 10 feet (wood weirds are immune). {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While poisoned in the way, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 and cannot be increased. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on a success.

bonus.name: Cocoon
entries: A Medium or smaller Humanoid that is {@condition Prone|XPHB} within 10 feet of the wood weird must succeed on a {@dc 11} Strength or Dexterity saving throw. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 11}). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The wood weird can cocoon only one creature at a time.

At the start of each of the wood weird's turns, the target is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 11}. {@actSaveFail} 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Poison damage. If the target dies while cocooned, it lignifies over 24 hours and then rises as a {@creature Wood Weird Seeder|GrimHollowMG24}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wood weird uses its Alluring Spores, then makes a Slam attack.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Alluring Spores
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 11}, one Humanoid the wood weird can sense within 10 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} and uses its turns to approach the wood weird, stopping when it is within 5 feet. The target avoids obvious danger, including {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. If it can't avoid such danger, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It also repeats the save if it takes damage or at the end of each of the target's turns. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute or if the wood weird is destroyed.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 2}, reach 5 ft. {@h}1 Piercing damage. {@actSave con} {@dc 9}. {@actSaveFail} 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.
It was hideous! Hundreds of writhing worms squeezed from the walls and swarmed over poor Mugsy. His screams didn't last long.

entries.name: Creatures from Beyond
entries: Most hope the Aether Kindred slumber still, but the disgusting creatures known as worms-in-the-walls have been seen with an alarming frequency near places of learning or powerful magic. Their ties to the Aether Kindred are irrefutable.

entries.name: Hidden Infestations
entries: These gray-colored worms are roughly 1 foot long and exceedingly thin. They hide in the walls of old decrepit buildings, especially dwellings where arcane magic suffuses the area. They can merge, creating fast-moving swarms with frightening intelligence.

entries.name: Alien Minds
entries: These worms can speak telepathically and mentally assault threats. Strange markings are carved into structures infested with the aberrations; however, no one has yet deciphered their meaning.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Alchemists given the carcasses of at least ten worms, and 200 GP worth of alchemical regents, can craft a {@item Potion of Mind Reading|XDMG}. This task requires 8 hours and a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence check using {@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB|alchemist's tools}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: Individually, the worms are intelligent, but they gain genius-level intellect when gathered in a swarm.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The bites of the creatures can briefly poison victims. Swarms of these creatures can psionically cast powerful magics that affect the mind.

trait.name: Aetheric Resilience
entries: The swarm has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

trait.name: Aura of Psychic Disruption
entries: The swarm deals 5 Psychic damage to any creature that ends its turn in the same space or within 5 feet of the swarm.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny worm. The swarm can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain Temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

action.name: Bites
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 0 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d8 + 1}) Piercing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Psychic damage, or 10 ({@damage 2d8 + 1}) Piercing damage if the swarm has the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition. {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Frightful Presence
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 14}, each creature of the swarm's choice in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the swarm. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute. If the creature succeeds on its saving throw or the effect ends for it, it is immune to the swarm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.

name: Wretched Reveler
languages: the languages it knew in life

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wretched reveler makes two attacks, using Dart or Tankard in any combination.

action.name: Tankard
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Poison damage.

action.name: Dart
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4}, range 20/60 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Poison damage.

bonus.name: Body Moving
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 12}, one creature within 30 feet of the wretched reveler that can hear it singing. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the start of the wretched reveler's next turn. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target uses its movement to dance in place without leaving its space, imposing {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws. Other creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the target while it dances.

The wretched reveler can stop singing at any time, ending the effect. The effect ends early if the wretched reveler is killed or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if the target can't hear the wretched reveler.

name: Wretched Driver
languages: the languages it knew in life

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wretched driver makes two Rapier attacks. It can replace one attack with a Cursed Shout.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Cursed Shout
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 13}, two creatures within 30 feet of the wretched driver that can hear it. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage, and the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of the wretched driver's next turn.

bonus.name: Angry Driving
entries: The wretched driver controls a vehicle. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13}, each other creature on the same vehicle as the wretched driver. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

name: Wretched Master of Ceremonies
languages: the languages it knew in life

spellcasting.name: Disguise Self
headerEntries: The wretched master of ceremonies casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}), requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

spellcasting.name: Misty Step
headerEntries: The wretched master of ceremonies casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Turning Defiance
entries: The wretched master of ceremonies and any Undead within 30 feet of it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against effects that turn undead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wretched master of ceremonies makes two Whip attacks. It can replace one attack with Macabre Direction.

action.name: Whip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 10 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Psychic damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller, the master moves the target to another unoccupied space within the whip's reach.

action.name: Macabre Direction
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 15}, one creature of the wretched master of ceremonies' choice within 30 feet that can hear it. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the start of the master's next turn. The master can use the target's {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, forcing it to make a weapon attack or cast a cantrip at a target of the master's choice.

action.name: Jubilant Thralls (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: {@actSave cha} {@dc 15}, each Humanoid of the wretched master of ceremonies' choice within 30 feet of it that can hear it (creatures fighting the master have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}). {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks to perceive creatures other than the master.

Each time the target takes damage, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect ends after 1 hour or if the master is destroyed or on a different plane of existence than the target. The master can end the effect early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

If the target remains {@condition Charmed|XPHB} for 1 minute, it no longer has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and regains its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. However, it remains {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, regarding the master as someone to be heeded and protected. It takes the master's requests and actions in the most favorable way possible. The target protects the master from those trying to harm it, but takes great risks only if bravery or foolhardiness is part of its normal nature.

trait.name: Magic Absorption
entries: If a xakalonus succeeds on a saving throw against a damaging magical effect and takes no damage, it regains 11 ({@dice 2d10}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Alternatively, if the xakalonus has all of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the next successful melee attack by the xakalonus deals an additional 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Force damage.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The xakalonus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The xakalonus makes one Bite attack and one Claws attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Sonic Bark {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the xakalonus that can hear it (other xakalonus and the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24} are immune). {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Thunder damage and the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.
The Stillborn Forest crawls with these beasts, and their howls foretell even larger monsters approaching.

entries.name: Spawn of the Hraptnon
entries: The legendary monster known as the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24} holds sway in the Stillborn Forest, protecting its hidden heart at a central glade. Xakalonus are spawn of this monstrosity, coming into being when blood spurts from that monster's wounds. Unlike their progenitor, xakalonus can leave the Stillborn Forest, and they now threaten the lands that border the dangerous place.

entries.name: Driven Away, Called Home
entries: When their creator, the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24}, is in danger, the xakalonus in its vicinity rush to its defense. When all threats are gone, however, the creatures have the innate urge to wander far and wide. Their goal is to devour the brains of magic-using creatures. Once they do this, they instinctively return to the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24}, disgorge the brains for the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24} to consume to maintain its horrible existence, and then they wander off again.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A xakalonus brain is encased in a viscous jelly which can be turned into a substance called {@item Arcane Oil|GrimHollowMG24} {@homebrew |(see Chapter 4)}. This oil's creation requires a proficient alchemist to spend 8 hours and 200 GP of components. They must succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check to create the substance.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Xakalonus are created from wounds to the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24}. These creatures, though always originating in the Stillborn Forest, can be found anywhere in Etharis. They feed on the brains of creatures that use magic, then return to offer up the brain to the {@creature Hraptnon|GrimHollowMG24}.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: If magic effects but does not harm a xakalonus, the magic might heal them or power their attacks instead.

trait.name: Assimilation
entries: A creature that drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} within 15 feet of the drone is subjected to the following effect. Assimilation can penetrate barriers, but 2 feet of rock, 2 inches of metal, a thin sheet of lead, or a barrier of force blocks it. {@actSave cha} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target becomes an {@b Yggdrasili Drone}. If the target is near multiple yggdrasili, it makes a single saving throw against the highest DC among them.

trait.name: Psychic Feedback
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 13}, each creature in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the drone when it takes Psychic damage. {@actSaveFail} The target takes the same amount of Psychic damage. If the target is near multiple yggdrasili, it makes a single saving throw against the highest DC among them and takes only the highest amount of Psychic damage.

trait.name: Psychic Static
entries: Attempts to read the drone's thoughts fail. {@actSave int} {@dc 13}, a creature that tries to read the drone's thoughts. {@actSaveFail} 8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Psychic Lash
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 13}, one creature the drone can sense within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} 8 ({@damage 2d4 + 3}) Psychic damage.

trait.name: Assimilation

Assimilation can penetrate barriers, but 2 feet of rock, 2 inches of metal, a thin sheet of lead, or a barrier of force blocks it. {@actSave cha} {@dc 15}. {@actSaveFail} The target becomes an {@creature Yggdrasili Drone|GrimHollowMG24}. If the target is near multiple yggdrasili, it makes a single saving throw against the highest DC among them.

trait.name: Cloud
entries: The cloud can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the cloud can move through any opening large enough for air to enter, but it can't enter or move through liquid.

trait.name: Psychic Static
entries: Attempts to read the cloud's thoughts fail. {@actSave int} {@dc 13}, a creature that tries to read the cloud's thoughts. {@actSaveFail} 11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The cloud uses Psychic Thrash twice.

action.name: Psychic Thrash
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 15}, one creature the cloud can sense within 60 feet, plus one creature in the cloud's space. {@actSaveFail} 11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Psychic damage. {@actSaveFailBy 5} The target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute. The effect ends early if the creature takes damage or a creature takes an action to shake it from its stupor.

trait.name: Aetheric Aura
entries: When a creature within 10 feet of the crown takes Psychic damage, it takes an extra 5 (2d4) Psychic damage.

entries: The crown makes two Slam attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Psychic Whip.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Whip

action.name: Mind Bomb (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: {@actSave int} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 20-foot radius Sphere centered on a point the crown can sense within 120 feet. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Psychic damage, the target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, and each time the target makes an ability check or saving throw, it must roll a d4 and subtract the result from its roll. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

trait.name: Inscrutable
entries: The truthseeker has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any Divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to determine the truthseeker's intentions or sincerity have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The Zabrielite truthseeker has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The truthseeker makes two attacks, using Talons or Eye Beams in any combination.

action.name: Talons
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. Hit 22 ({@damage 3d10 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Eye Beams
entries: {@atkr rs} {@hit 9}, range 120 ft. {@h}27 ({@damage 5d10}) Radiant damage. This attack ignores all but {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}, and the truthseeker doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll while adjacent to an enemy.

action.name: Transfixing Gaze
entries: {@actSave wis} DC 17, one creature the truthseeker can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, the truthseeker can read the target's mind to learn its surface thoughts and gain insight into its motivations, emotional state, and major concerns. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

The truthseeker must maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on this effect or it immediately ends. While maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on Transfixing Gaze, the truthseeker can't make Eye Beams attacks.
Have no fear, mortal. Look into my eyes so that the truth might be revealed.

entries.name: Messenger Eagle
entries: A Zabrielite truthseeker manifests as a giant, stalking eagle-heron with a human head and crest of incandescent head feathers. Its enormous silver eyes project blazing beams of radiant energy. They were created to be messengers of the gods, and aid mortal rulers in governing their realms with wisdom.

entries.name: Birds of a Feather Flock Together
entries: During the War of the Four Divines, all sides summoned and bound Zabrielite truthseekers, assigning them to divine justiciars and inquisitors in their reckless pursuit to eliminate rival faiths. It wasn't uncommon to see flocks of truthseekers accompanying a celestial host as flying artillery or assisting with ferreting out spies and informants. Zabriel's own dereliction of duty encouraged her servitor angels to follow suit, and they pursued their own truth-seeking agendas as they served court mages, judges, and would-be philosopher-kings.

entries.name: A Separate Agenda
entries: The longer they spend away from the divine presence the gods, the more uncompromising and fervent Zabrielite truthseekers become. The act of uncovering secret cabals and conspiracies has taken on a life of its own; they search for truth for its own sake and not in service to the higher good. They're just as likely to attempt to reveal the secrets of incautious adventurers as they are the machinations of evil-doers.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Four Zabrielite truthseekers' plumage is a key ingredient in {@item Wings of Flying|XDMG}. A proficient weaver can spend 7 days and 2500 GP of components to craft those wings with a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: The avian creature known as the truthseeker ferrets out large conspiracies, using their abilities to slay the transgressors. They are often overzealous in their pursuits.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: Truthseekers were servants of the gods, but they are tied directly to Zabriel, the Arch Seraph of Truth.

entries.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
entries: The eyes of the truthseeker can shoot radiant bolts, and its gaze can transfix those who the creature attacks.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: A truthseeker can act as an ally to characters one moment, and an enemy the next, depending on the moral and ethical decisions and makeup of the adventuring party. Accepting the assistance of a truthseeker comes with certain risks and obligations.

entries: As part of one claw attack, the vampire extends its reach by 5 feet.

trait.name: Rampage
entries: When the bugbear vampire reduces a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack on its turn, the bugbear can take a bonus action to move up to half its speed and make a bite attack.

trait.name: Reckless
entries: At the start of its turn, the vampire can gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls until the start of its next turn, but attack rolls against it have advantage until then.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The vampire regains 15 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point and isn't in sunlight. If the vampire takes radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the vampire's next turn.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The vampire can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Surprise Mauling
entries: If the vampire {@quickref Surprise|PHB|3|0|surprises} a creature and hits it with an attack during the first round of combat, the target takes an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage from the attack. If the attack is a bite, 3 ({@dice 1d6}) of this damage is necrotic damage.

trait.name: Vampire Weaknesses
entries: The vampire has the following flaws:
{@i Forbiddance.} The vampire can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of the occupants.
{@i Stake to the Heart.} The vampire dies if a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into its heart while it is {@condition incapacitated} in its resting place.
{@i Sunlight Hypersensitivity.} The vampire takes 15 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The vampire makes three attacks, only one of which can be a bite.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) slashing damage. If the target is a creature, the vampire can {@action grapple} the target (escape {@dc 16}).

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) piercing damage and 10 ({@damage 3d6}) necrotic damage. The target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains hit points equal to that amount. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

action.name: Mist Form
entries: If the vampire isn't in sunlight, it polymorphs into a Medium cloud of mist, or back into its true form. Anything it wears or carries transforms with it. While in mist form, the vampire can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of 30 feet, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, but it can't pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. A vampire in mist form is immune to nonmagical damage, except damage from sunlight, and has resistance to damage other than radiant. The vampire reverts to its true form if it dies.

reaction.name: Misty Escape
entries: When it drops to 0 hit points outside its resting place, the vampire transforms into its Mist Form instead of falling {@condition unconscious}. If the vampire can't transform, it dies.

While it has 0 hit points in mist form, the vampire dies if it takes damage three times or radiant damage once. It can't willingly revert to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or die. Once in its resting place, it reverts to its vampire form. It is then {@condition paralyzed} until it regains at least 1 hit point. After spending 1 hour in its resting place with 0 hit points, it regains 1 hit point.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The vampire moves up to its speed without provoking {@action opportunity attack|PHB|opportunity attacks}.

legendary.name: Claws
entries: The vampire attacks once with its claws.
I thought the brutes were going to tear me apart. Little did I know they had a worse fate planned for me.

entries.name: Physically Imposing
entries: Already an imposing creature, a bugbear afflicted with vampirism becomes even more of a hulking brute. Their muscles grow enormous, with ropey veins bulging from flesh that their fur fails to cover. Bugbear vampires are capable of great feats of strength. They eschew the weapons they used in life in favor of the visceral close combat of tooth and claw.

entries.name: Reckless Predators
entries: Corruption has made bugbears wild and chaotic in their normal lives. Vampirism has a similar effect. A bugbear vampire is a brutal fighter who aims to kill quickly without much consideration for personal safety. Few vampires survive to the adult stage, but even fewer bugbear vampires do.

entries.name: Might and Stealth
entries: Only an elder vampire of considerable might can prevent young bugbear vampires from reducing prey to gory remains. But under such direction, bugbear vampires are effective — if ruthless— agents for missions that require infiltration or a bloody ambush.

entries.name: Bugbear Vampire Customization
entries: A bugbear vampire is stronger than others of its age, having a higher Strength score and the Rampage trait— see the stat block. The vampire relies on this brute force and much less on reason and charm, so their Intelligence and Charisma is often lower. Such vampires outgrow the brashness of the spawn stage more slowly, and they're therefore often still chaotic evil. The vampire loves to {@quickref Surprise|PHB|3|0|surprise} foes, then fight, feed, and kill in an efficient but brash manner. A bugbear vampire has the Clawing Lunge, Reckless, and Surprise Mauling traits, as shown in the stat block. As with many other creatures who have {@sense darkvision} in life, the bugbear vampire has {@sense darkvision} superior to that of typical vampires its age (add 30 feet).

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The muscles of a bugbear vampire can provide a gruesome reward. Somebody who has proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill can harvest muscle tissue from a bugbear vampire. Someone who has proficiency with {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} or the {@skill Arcana} skill can then treat the muscles with reagents worth 2,500 gp over 14 days. Exposure to sunlight during this process causes the tissue to wither and become useless. Otherwise, the process requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence or Wisdom check and, if successful, produces one {@item muscle graft|GHMG} {@homebrew |(see chapter 4)}.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
entries: The vampiric curse intensifies a bugbear's worst tendencies while increasing their strength to astonishing levels. Bugbear vampires relish close combat.

entries.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
entries: Bugbear vampires are so bloodthirsty and overconfident that they can fail to look out for their own safety. Goading such a vampire into anger is one way to make them reckless.

entries.name: GM Advice:
entries: Bugbear vampires play a strange role in the history of their kind. Having already succumbed to {@disease Tormach's Rage|GHMG}, bugbears are fearsome killers. Those bugbears who succumb to vampirism take on new powers, but they no longer fit into the plans of Tormach. Different groups of normal bugbears might treat a bugbear vampire much differently. Some might assume the vampirism is another blessing from Tormach, while others might see it as a corruption. Adventurers might easily find themselves caught in a struggle between a group of bugbears and a bugbear vampire's followers.

trait.name: Death Burst
entries: When the chalk chatterling dies, it explodes in a burst of dust. Any creature within 5 feet of the chalk chatterling must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Distracting Chatter
entries: Any creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of and able to hear the chalk chatterling must succeed on a {@dc 11} Wisdom saving throw or be unable to {@action cast a spell||cast} or maintain {@status concentration} on a spell. Constructs and undead are immune. A creature who intended to {@action cast a spell} can choose another course of action.

trait.name: Water Weakness
entries: If the chalk chatterling is doused in water or ends its turn submerged in water, the chalk chatterling takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) acid damage. Maximize this damage if the water is soapy.

action.name: Dust Whip

action.name: Maddening Chatter {@recharge}
